## What is in force at delivery (`in_force.py`)

`in_force` reproduces `in_force.py` whole, in one unit (about 200 lines of
Rust). It needs nothing from the machine: the store and the admission
are its arguments.

| function | reference lines | needs | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `InForce`, `history` | 47 to 65 | nothing | built |
| `in_force`: the walk of inbound links | 67 to 95 | `Store.inbound_links`, `RecordView.prime`, `admits_id` | built |
| `held_ids` read | 97 to 100 | `standing.held_ids` | built, as a trait method |
| `newest`, `newest_head` | 102 to 109 | nothing | built |
| `admitted_sources`, `head` | 111 to 126 | `admits_id` | built |
| the answers | 128 to 141 | nothing | built |

What each part reproduces, and why:

- The store's two reads are the trait `LinkReader` (`inbound_links`,
  `held_ids`) and the admission is the trait `RecordView` (`prime`,
  `admits_id`). The store, `standing` and `admission` are not ported, so
  their answers come in as data; the walk calls them in the reference's
  order with the reference's arguments (`prime` with every source read,
  duplicates kept, an empty list included; `admits_id` only where the
  reference's `and` reaches it; `held_ids` with the asked ids followed by
  every source in the order first read, and not at all when nothing is
  asked). The golden file pins that order of calls.
- A source's stamp is the last one read for it, as the reference's dict
  assignment keeps it, while its place in the list given to `held_ids` is
  where it was first read.
- `newest` is the greatest `(stamp, id)`; Python compares `str` by code
  point, which is the byte order of UTF-8, so Rust's `String` order is
  the same. A lone surrogate cannot be an id here; the store's ids are
  ULIDs.
- `newest_head` keeps Python's `or`: an empty id among the sources not
  held is falsy, so the newest of the whole pool, held ones included, is
  taken instead.
- The answer is a `Vec<InForce>` in the order of first occurrence of the
  asked ids, which is the reference's dict order.
- No regular expression is involved.

Reference findings (reproduced, not changed):

- The empty id falls through `newest_head`'s `or`: with `a` superseded
  by `""` (stamp `1`) and by `c` (stamp `2`), `c` held, the reference
  gives `a`'s slot to the held `c`, where its documentation says the
  newest not held is followed (`in_force_kills.rs`,
  `the_empty_id_falls_through_to_the_newest_held`).
- The walk follows the sources of every row `inbound_links` answers, of
  any type: a store answering a `contradicts` row would have its source
  read and walked, though only `supersedes` and `extends` are followed.
  The real store answers only the two types asked for.

Fixtures and tests: `tests/contract/gen_in_force.py` writes
`in_force.jsonl`, not gated (ASCII and code point order): 40 cases
covering every branch (chains, ties, cycles, admission, held heads and
extenders, the empty id, another link type, Unicode ids) with the answers
and every call, and a sweep of 3000 cases drawn by a 64-bit linear
congruential rule from a seed, pinned as a count and a SHA-256.
`golden_in_force.rs` checks both; `in_force_kills.rs` holds nine cases a
plausible wrong walk fails; `in_force_robustness.rs` runs chains and
cycles of 20,000 records, a fan-in of 30,000, a 1 MiB id and 50,000
asked ids, and holds time at 2n within five times time at n. The
reference takes 0.14 s on the 20,000 chain; the port takes a few
milliseconds in release.

Nothing of the module is left for a later unit; wiring the traits to
`store` and to `store::caller`'s admission is the store's and standing's.

## The admission vocabulary and the health answers (`admission`, `health_summary`, `health_roots`)

Three small modules, one unit (unit leafkit2, about 330 lines of Rust
outside tests). None needs anything from the machine: the report, the
roots and the times are arguments.

| function | reference lines | needs | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `admission.NO_RESOLUTION`, `Admission`, `admits_row` | 59-60, class | nothing | in `store::caller`; re-exported |
| `admission.DriftScope`, `CountedRecords` | 65-89 | nothing | built |
| `admission.EveryRecord`, `EVERY_RECORD` | 106-121 | nothing | built |
| `admission.admitted_nothing` | 124-126 | nothing | built |
| `admission.recorded_caller` | 129-163 | the membership model | later |
| `health_summary._empty`, `_attention` | 34-50 | nothing | built |
| `section_names`, `health_summary` | 53-68 | `json.dumps(default=str)` | built |
| `health_section` | 71-85 | nothing | built |
| `health_roots.EstateProgress` (`ordered`, `attempt`) | 21-52 | nothing | built |
| `progress_for_store` | 55-73 | an open Store | the Store owns its progress |

What each part reproduces, and why:

- `admission`: `NO_RESOLUTION` and `Admission` stay where
  `store::caller` ported them; the module re-exports `NO_RESOLUTION`.
  `EveryRecord` implements `in_force::RecordView` (`prime`, `admits_id`)
  and has `admits_row` as an inherent method with the signature of
  `store::caller::Admission::admits_row`, since the crate's `RecordView`
  has no `admits_row` until a reader of it is ported. `DriftScope` is a
  trait with `prime` and `drift_counts`; `CountedRecords` holds a
  `HashSet` (the reference's frozenset) and its `prime` does nothing.
- `health_summary` reads the report as a `PyValue::Dict` in insertion
  order (a repeated key answers its last value, as a dict holds the last
  one set). A report that is not a dict is iterated and indexed as the
  reference does: a list, tuple or string yields its items or characters
  as section names, `report[name]` is TypeError for a `str` name and
  IndexError out of range, `key in report` is membership (a substring for
  a string), `report.get` is AttributeError, and anything else is
  TypeError at the iteration. Errors are `HealthError` (the class, and `str(exc)` for KeyError
  and ValueError). `_empty` is None or an empty list or dict only; a
  zero, a False, an empty string and an empty tuple are values.
  `_attention` evaluates as the reference does: `list(memory_ids)` of a
  truthy value (a string gives its characters, a dict its keys, any other
  non-iterable TypeError), the first three, replaced by `str(scope)` split
  on `", "` when the scope is truthy; the line is `str()` of kind, count
  and action in that order (a missing key is KeyError), and a named item
  that is not a `str` is TypeError at the join. A recommendation that is
  not a dict is AttributeError. `section_chars` is the code point length
  of `json.dumps` with `DumpOptions` built for `separators=(",", ":")`,
  `default=str`, `ensure_ascii`. `health_section` splits on `,`, strips
  each part with Python's `str.isspace` set (`unicode::is_space`, so
  U+3000 and U+0085 strip and U+200B does not), drops empty parts, keeps
  a repeated part at its first place, and raises the reference's
  ValueError text with the `repr` of the first unknown part, or of the
  whole name when nothing is asked.
- `health_roots`: `EstateProgress` keeps `checked` as a `VecDeque` in
  attempt order (the `OrderedDict` with `move_to_end`), capped at
  `LAST_CHECKED_CAP` (1024) by dropping the oldest. `ordered` sorts the
  distinct roots by code point (Python `str` order; `Vec<u32>` order, so a
  lone surrogate sorts where Python puts it) and rotates to
  `bisect_left` of `retry_root` when it is among them, else `bisect_right`
  of the cursor. The reference's `RLock` becomes a `Mutex` its owner
  holds, and `progress_for_store`'s weak map becomes the open Store's own
  `EstateProgress::default()`; `store` is not edited by this unit.
- No regular expression is involved.

Fixtures and tests: `tests/contract/gen_health_summary.py` writes
`health_summary.jsonl` (45 rows over hand-built reports: empty sections
and zero values, scope against memory ids, odd recommendation shapes and
every exception, padded, empty, repeated, unknown and comma-separated
section names, non-ASCII values, a lone surrogate name, a datetime
section) and `tests/contract/gen_health_roots.py` writes
`health_roots.jsonl` (16 rows of root lists with cursor, retry root and
attempt sequences, and one digest row of 3000 attempts over 1500 roots
that evicts past the cap). Neither is gated: every value spells the same
under every interpreter and platform. `golden_health_summary.rs` and
`golden_health_roots.rs` check every row; `health_kills.rs` holds the
cases a plausible wrong port fails; `health_robustness.rs` orders 200,000
roots, attempts past the cap, asks a million commas, and holds growth
claims through `tests/timing`. The admission vocabulary has unit tests in
its module.

Left for later: `admission.recorded_caller` and `admits_row` on
`RecordView`, with their first reader; wiring `EstateProgress` into the
Store.

## The report model of health (`health_model.py`)

`health_model.py` (1,571 lines) is the report model `health.compute_health`
fills: its dataclasses, caps and shared predicates. It imports
`models.Category` (`records::Category`), `store.EpisodeVolume`
(`store::journal::EpisodeVolume`), `time_utils.isoformat_utc_optional` and
`verify.BASIS_AUTHOR_DATE`, all built. Nothing in it asks the machine: the
datetimes, counts and events are arguments. It is cut into three units,
leaves first; unit health_model-1 is built (`src/health_model.rs`, 571
lines of Rust outside tests, and `round(x, ndigits)` in `search::num`),
and unit health_model-2 (`src/health_model/debt.rs`, a child module
re-exported from `health_model`, 493 lines, and the module line and its
`pub use` in `src/health_model.rs`, 9 lines).

Unit health_model-2 is lines 662-1241 less `explicit_ratio`, unit
health_model-3 lines 1244-1567. `eval_model.py` imports only
`explicit_ratio` from this module, so eval_model-1 waits on this unit
alone. `compute_health` and the event walk belong to the health and
health_stats units.

What unit 1 reproduces, and why:

- The types hold Rust values: text as `PyStr` (a lone surrogate is kept),
  datetimes as `DateTime`, `Category` as `records::Category`, counts as
  `i64`, `resolution_timeline` as a `Vec<PyValue>` copied as given, and the
  `models` and `principals` censuses of `ActorSlice` as `(key, count)`
  pairs in insertion order (a dict's keys are distinct; the caller keeps
  them so). Every caller counts rows, so no count passes `i64`; a sum of
  two counts (`MarkerStats.total`) is taken in `i128`, where a Python `int`
  does not wrap either. `to_dict` answers a `PyValue::Dict` in the
  reference's key order; the JSON text is a later caller's, through
  `json::dumps`.
- The events are `dict[str, Any]`, read as a `PyValue`. `ev.get(key)` is
  the last value of a `str` key, None when missing, and AttributeError
  for a value that is not a dict. `ev.get("auto") is True` is the bool
  True only: 1, 1.0, `"true"` and `[True]` are not, and such an applied
  use is `model`. Every `== "literal"` is Python's: only a `str` of those
  code points equals it, never an int, a bool, a path or a list.
- `_is_dead_weight` takes its keyword arguments as the struct
  `DeadWeight`. Each gate compares as Python does: `freshest_ts >=
  cutoff_ts` and `earliest_retrieval_ts >= grace_cutoff_ts` exclude at
  the bound, a NaN compares false and excludes nothing, and
  `applied_count > 0` lets a negative count through.
- `_freshest_touch_ts` reads `datetime.timestamp()` of an aware value as
  CPython does: the microseconds since the epoch divided by 10**6 with one
  correct rounding (`timedelta.total_seconds`). Dividing the microseconds
  as an `f64` by 1e6 rounds twice once they pass 2**53 (after about
  2255: 5530-03-03T08:26:42.691225Z is 112348024002.69122, not
  112348024002.69124). The latest of the four is kept as `max` keeps it.
  A naive datetime's timestamp is the machine's local time (`mktime`):
  that reading is not ported, and the port declines it
  (`HealthModelError::NaiveTimestamp`), as `review::related`'s
  `related_entry` declines a naive `updated` (`NaiveUpdated`).
- `_has_unresolved_contradiction` orders two aware datetimes as instants
  (one instant at +23:59 and at -23:59 is not later), two naive ones by
  their wall clocks, and raises TypeError for a naive against an aware at
  whichever comparison meets it; without a contradiction nothing is
  compared. `MemoryStats.to_dict` raises that TypeError where the
  property does.
- `explicit_ratio`, `model_endorsement_ratio` and `override_rate` are
  Python's `int / int`: correctly rounded at any size (`search::num`'s
  division), the sign that of the quotient, so `0 / -3` is `-0.0`.
  `explicit_ratio` answers None for `applied <= 0`, and
  `model_endorsement_ratio` only for `applied_count == 0` (a negative
  count divides); `override_rate` is 0.0 when the total is not positive.
- `MarkerStats.to_dict` rounds the rate with `round(x, 3)`:
  `search::num::round_digits`, CPython's rounding of the exact binary
  value to the digit count, half to even, read back correctly rounded.
  `round4`, which the ranker and the dedup call, is `round_digits(x, 4)`
  with its answers unchanged. `round_digits` holds 0 to 15 digits and
  panics past 15 in every build (an `assert!`): Python's `round` is exact
  at any count, and the `u128` arithmetic here would answer wrongly from
  22 digits (`round(0.5, 22)` as 0.0). `(x * 1000).round() / 1000` differs at the
  exact tie 0.0625 (0.062, not 0.063) and at 1.0005 (1.0), and a half to
  even of the scaled product at 0.0025 (0.003, not 0.002).
- `_iso` is `time_utils::isoformat_utc_optional`: every `+00:00` becomes
  `Z`, so an offset of 30 seconds spells `Z:30`. `last_used_at` and
  `last_verified_at` are None only when None (a datetime is never falsy).
- Two answers of the reference differ from its own docstrings, and the
  port reproduces them as written. `isoformat_utc` promises
  `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ` but writes six fractional digits or none
  (`2026-01-01T00:00:00.123456Z`, `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`) and turns a
  non-UTC offset whose text starts `+00:00` into `Z` and a tail
  (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z:30` at 30 seconds east). `model_endorsement_ratio`
  promises the None-on-zero contract of `endorsement_ratio`, yet at
  `applied_count = -3` it divides (`0 / -3` is `-0.0`) where
  `endorsement_ratio` is None. No counted row is negative, so no store
  reaches the second.
- No regular expression is involved.

What unit 2 reproduces, and why:

- The rollups hold Rust values as unit 1's types do: text as `PyStr`,
  counts as `i64`, `unread_causes` and the `ActorSlice` censuses as
  `(key, count)` pairs in insertion order, `CrossRepoDrift.skipped` (a
  `list[dict[str, Any]]`) as a `Vec<PyValue>` copied as given, and
  `CommitDriftRow.basis` as a `PyStr` (any text the caller sets is
  written back). Each type has the dataclass's defaults: `new` takes the
  fields without one (`VerificationDebt::new(stale_after_days)`,
  `CommitDriftRow::new` with `basis` at `BASIS_AUTHOR_DATE`,
  `CommitDriftDebt::new(current_repo, current_cwd)`,
  `CrossRepoDriftGroup::new(repo, worktree_root)`,
  `ColdEndorsementMemories::new(min_retrievals)`), and the types with no
  required field are `Default` (`ActorSlices`' `undeclared` is
  `ActorSlice(client=None)` at zero). The caps are constants
  (`VERIFICATION_DEBT_CAP`, `COLD_ENDORSEMENT_MIN_RETRIEVALS`,
  `COLD_ENDORSEMENT_CAP`, `CROSS_REPO_MAX_ROOTS`, `COMMIT_DRIFT_DEBT_CAP`,
  `RECENT_SILENT_MISSES_CAP`); the callers that apply them are the health
  units'.
- `to_dict` keeps the reference's key order, which is not the
  declaration order: `VerificationDebt` writes its six counts first
  (`never_verified_checkable` after `never_verified_total`, `fresh_count`
  last) and then its two row lists, `CommitDriftDebt` and
  `CrossRepoDriftGroup` write `total_drifted` before `rows`, and
  `CrossRepoDrift` writes `total_drifted` first. `VerificationDebt` and
  `ColdEndorsementMemories` hold `MemoryStats` rows, whose `to_dict`
  raises TypeError on a naive datetime ordered against an aware one, so
  theirs answers `Answer` and raises at the first such row: the scalars
  are built first, then `never_verified`'s rows, then `stale`'s.
- `CommitDriftDebt.to_dict` writes `unconfirmed` when it is not zero (a
  negative count is truthy and is written), and `_unread_dict`'s keys
  when `unread` is not zero, even with no causes or ids, and none at zero
  whatever the causes and ids hold. `CrossRepoDriftGroup` has no
  `unconfirmed` and writes its unread keys after `last_checked_at`.
  `_unread_dict` copies the causes in the order given (`dict(causes)`)
  and every id given, uncapped, a repeated id included (`list(ids)`);
  `unread_fields` (`Counter` of each
  cause's `str(value)`) sorts the causes by their text, code point order,
  and keeps the first `COMMIT_DRIFT_DEBT_CAP` (20) ids in the mapping's
  insertion order, capped before anything else. The keys of every
  `unread_causes` (`CommitDriftDebt`'s, `CrossRepoDriftGroup`'s,
  `UnreadFields`' and `_unread_dict`'s argument) are distinct, as a
  dict's are: a repeated key is refused by a `debug_assert` (a release
  build writes both pairs, a value no reference dict holds), so a port
  that kept one of them could not be told apart on any value the
  reference makes. `unread_fields` takes the
  mapping as its items, ids distinct as a dict's keys are (a repeated id
  is refused the same way), the causes as
  `origin_history::HistoryUnread` (`verify_basis.CommitDriftUnread` is
  that enum), and answers `UnreadFields`, the three fields by name, which
  a caller assigns where the reference spreads the dict into a
  constructor.
- `CommitDriftRow.to_dict`'s `_iso(x) if x else None` is None only for
  None (a datetime is never falsy), and `CrossRepoDriftGroup`'s
  `last_checked_at` is `isoformat_utc_optional`: an offset of 30 seconds
  spells `Z:30`, and a naive datetime is written without a zone.
- `clamp_ratio_threshold` is `float(value)`, NaN to 0.0, then `min(1.0,
  max(0.0, value))` as Python's `max` and `min` choose: the first
  argument is kept unless the second compares strictly beyond it, so
  `-0.0` becomes `0.0`, `5e-324` stays, and `inf` is 1.0. `f64::clamp`
  keeps `-0.0` and passes NaN through, and `f64::max` and `f64::min` may
  answer either zero, so none of them is used. The port takes an `f64`:
  `float()` of an int past the double range (OverflowError) or of
  another type is the caller's conversion, and `BehaviorConfig` holds a
  float.
- `weakly_endorsed` is the reference's four steps: `explicit_ratio` None
  (no applies, or a negative count) is not weakly endorsed, even with no
  explicit apply; `explicit_applied == 0` is; a threshold `<= 0.0`
  (`-0.0` included) is off; else `ratio < ratio_threshold`, strictly, so
  a ratio equal to the threshold (1/10 at 0.1) is not. A NaN threshold is
  not `<= 0.0` and fails `ratio < NaN`: never weakly endorsed past the
  `explicit_applied == 0` step. A negative explicit count is a negative
  ratio, below any positive threshold. `_is_weakly_endorsed` reads
  `applied_count` and `explicit_applied_count`, not the auto count.
- No regular expression is involved.

Fixtures and tests: `tests/contract/gen_health_model.py` writes
`health_model.jsonl`: 238 rows (round to three places at ties and their
neighbours, timestamps at years 1 and 9999 and past 2**53 microseconds,
contradiction orderings with naive and aware values, 49 events through
the three predicates, each dead-weight gate alone and at its bound, ratios
past 2**53 and at the ends of `i64`, and each report type's properties
and `to_dict` with surrogates, offsets of seconds and microseconds and
extreme counts) and three digest rows: 20,000 drawn stats (three
`MemoryStats` to each `MarkerStats`, 181 of them raising TypeError) by
the SHA-256 of their `json.dumps(to_dict())`, 20,000 drawn floats each
rounded to three and four places, and 20,000 sets of four drawn aware
datetimes through `_freshest_touch_ts`. The draws are a 64-bit linear
congruential generator the Rust test runs by the same rule. Input
datetimes travel as their fields, not their isoformat:
`fromisoformat` reads an offset of minus one microsecond as zero. The
file is not gated: integer division, `round`, `float.__repr__`,
`isoformat` and ASCII-escaped `json.dumps` spell the same under 3.11 to
3.14 on every system. `golden_health_model.rs` checks every row and the
three digests; `health_model_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong
port fails (half away from zero, rounding the scaled product, truthiness
for `is True`, an int or a path equal to a `str`, each dead-weight bound
moved, the timestamp through `f64` microseconds, naive datetimes
accepted, wall-clock order of aware values, `f64` division of counts,
`i64` overflow of the total, the key order, an event's first value of a
repeated key or a key one code point off read for its own);
`health_model_robustness.rs` takes counts at both ends of `i64`, years 1
and 9999 at offsets up to a microsecond short of a day, `round(x, 3)` over
every exponent, `round(x, 15)` against CPython and the refusal of 16 and
22 digits, a timeline of 100,000 entries and events of 200,000 keys with
growth claims through `tests/timing`, and events 100,000 deep and 100,000
keys wide.

Known costs, release builds against CPython 3.13 on the same input, best
of three on a loaded machine. The predicates read every key they need in
one pass from the end of the event, stopping once each is found: on a
three-key event `endorsement_tier` takes 0.011 us (the reference 0.11
us). A `PyValue::Dict` is a list of pairs, not a hash table, so on an
event of 100,000 keys with the read keys first the pass still meets
every key: `is_hook_telemetry_event` 140 us and `endorsement_tier` 166 us
against 0.08 and 0.11 us (about 1,700 and 1,500 times; one scan per key
took 159 and 316 us). `MemoryStats.to_dict` copies `resolution_timeline`
and the texts into the answer, where the reference's `list()` copies
references: 27 ms against 0.25 ms for 100,000 entries (about 110 times).
Both are linear in an input the caller already built or parsed in linear
time, and real events and timelines hold a few entries; removing either
needs a shared or hashed `PyValue`, which `pyvalue.rs` does not have.
`health_model_robustness.rs` holds the predicates and `to_dict` linear
in their input.

Unit 2's fixtures: `gen_health_model.py`'s `generate_debt` writes
`health_model_debt.jsonl`, not gated for unit 1's reasons: 103 rows
(`clamp_ratio_threshold` over both infinities, both zeros, both smallest
subnormals, the double below 1.0 and three NaNs (quiet, negative and
signalling); `weakly_endorsed` and
`_is_weakly_endorsed` at each branch, applied zero and negative,
thresholds 0.0, -0.0, NaN, the ratio equal to the threshold and one unit
above it, counts at both ends of `i64`; `unread_fields` over 0, 1, 20, 21
and 25 ids counting down with the causes out of order, and ids holding a
surrogate; `_unread_dict` at zero with causes, at negative counts and
with 25 ids; and every report type, defaults first, with surrogates,
offsets of seconds and microseconds, naive datetimes, extreme counts and
`MemoryStats` rows that raise TypeError in either list) and two digest
rows: 20,000 drawn report values, the kind by `pick(9)`, their
`MemoryStats` rows by unit 1's `draw_memory` (93 of them raise
TypeError), by the SHA-256 of their `json.dumps(to_dict())`; and 20,000
drawn counts and thresholds (unit 1's `draw_float`) through
`clamp_ratio_threshold` and `weakly_endorsed`. `golden_health_model_debt.rs`
checks every row and both digests, drawing the inputs by the generator's
rule; `health_model_debt_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port
fails (the causes left unsorted in `unread_fields` or sorted in
`_unread_dict`, the ids capped after a sort or not at all, `unconfirmed`
or the unread keys written at zero or dropped at a negative count,
`f64::clamp` for the clamp at `-0.0` and NaN, a NaN threshold firing, the
ratio equal to the threshold firing, a TypeError row in `stale` or the
cold rows not raised, the declaration order for the key order, a repeated
unread id dropped) and, in debug builds, the refusal of a repeated cause
key or `unread_fields` id;
`health_model_debt_robustness.rs` takes counts at both ends of `i64`
through every rollup and threshold, 100,000 rows in each list (a raise at
the last still raises), `unread_fields` over 100,000 ids and
`_unread_dict` over 10,000 causes and ids with growth claims through
`tests/timing`, and `to_dict` linear in its rows. The rollups copy their
rows and texts into the answer as unit 1's types do; their cost is that
of the `MemoryStats` rows they hold.

Unit 2's known costs, release builds against CPython 3.13.13 on the same
input, best of three on a loaded machine: `_unread_dict` over 100,000
causes and 100,000 ids takes 9.5 ms (32 ms in a debug build) against
0.6 ms, about 16 times, since `dict(causes)` and `list(ids)` copy
references where the port clones each text into the answer. Real rollups
hold at most six causes and the 20 ids `unread_fields` keeps. Every
other measured ratio is under 2: `unread_fields` over 100,000 ids 0.7 ms
against 16.7 ms, `VerificationDebt.to_dict` over two lists of 100,000
rows 846 ms against 588 ms, `CommitDriftDebt` 126 ms against 129 ms,
`CrossRepoDrift` over 100,000 groups and skipped entries 83 ms against
52 ms, `ActorSlices` over 100,000 declared slices 92 ms against 51 ms.

Left for later: unit health_model-3 as mapped above.

## The eval family's model (`eval_model.py`)

`eval_model.py` (1,320 lines) holds what `eval.py`'s rates and reports
build on: the Wilson interval and `RateCI`, the row types, the
silent-miss readers of one event, the threshold and widening rule
registries, the widening lanes' walk over the audited turns, the
`--since` and `--until` parsing, the recall surfaces' split on each

What unit 1 reproduces, and why:

- Counts are `i64`: every caller counts events. A span is `i128`
  microseconds where the reference holds a `timedelta` (the crate has
  none): the longest span `parse_since` returns, 999,999,999 days and
  86,399 seconds, is past `i64` microseconds. `Bound` is the
  `timedelta | datetime` `parse_window_bound` returns.
- `RateCI.from_counts` gives no rate and no interval for a denominator
  `<= 0` (`torn_read` False); a numerator past the denominator is a torn
  read with the rate 1.0; else the rate is `numerator / denominator` as
  Python divides two ints (`search::num::int_true_div`, correctly
  rounded), never an `f64` division of the counts, which differs past
  2**53 (`(2**53 + 1) / (2**53 + 2)` is `0x3fefffffffffffff`, the `f64`
  quotient `0x3feffffffffffffe`). A negative numerator divides (`-1 / 3`)
  and is not torn.
- `_wilson_interval` takes `z` as the reference does. `k` is clamped to
  `[0, n]`; `p = k / n` is int division; every other step keeps the
  reference's order of operations, with `n` read as a float (`n as f64`
  from `i64` rounds to nearest even, as Python's `float(int)` does):
  `z * z / n`, `z * z / (2.0 * n)`, `p * (1.0 - p) / n`,
  `z * z / (4.0 * n * n)`, `z * sqrt(...) / denom`. Reordering one step
  moves the last bit (`z * (z / n)` gives another upper bound at 1/5).
  The bounds go through Python's `max(0.0, x)` and `min(1.0, x)` (the
  first argument kept unless the second compares greater or less), so a
  NaN bound from a NaN or infinite `z` is 0.0 below and 1.0 above. Rust's
  `f64::max` and `f64::min` answer the same on every input this
  function produces (they return the non-NaN argument, and no bound is
  ever -0.0 here); a clamp or an `if x < 0.0` would let the NaN through.
  The port writes the lower bound with `search::num::py_max` and the
  upper with `f64::min`.
- `ColdEndorsementMemoriesRow.endorsement_ratio` calls `explicit_ratio`
  on `auto + explicit`; the sum is an unbounded `int` in the reference,
  so past `i64` it is divided here by the same rule (None when not
  positive). `SilentMissCandidate.recent_retrieval_count` keeps the
  event's `int` as `PyValue::Int`'s decimal text: the reference keeps any
  `int`, past `i64` too.
- `parse_since` answers None for None, `""` or `"all"`, compared before
  the strip (`" all"` is refused). The token is
  `_SINCE_PATTERN.fullmatch(spec.strip())`: the engine's `Regex` built
  from the reference's text (decision rule 1; `\d` is every Unicode
  decimal digit, `$` at a fullmatch); the pattern is in the engine's
  inventory already (T1, `eval_model.py:_SINCE_PATTERN`). `str.strip` is
  `str.isspace` at both ends (`unicode::py_strip`, U+001C to U+001F
  included). The value is `int()` of the digits (`pyvalue::int_from_str`:
  `٣٠d` is 30 days), and past 4,300 digits (leading zeros count) it
  raises CPython's own ValueError text, which `parse_since` does not
  catch. Zero is the "must be positive" ValueError (`\d+` has no sign);
  `timedelta` overflows from 10**9 days (`86400000000000s`,
  `1000000000d`), turned into the "out of range" text. Every message
  spells the spec with `repr` (`pyvalue::repr_str`).
- `parse_timestamp_utc` strips, turns one final `Z` or `z` into
  `+00:00`, reads `DateTime::from_isoformat` (CPython 3.13's reader),
  refuses a naive value with the reference's text (which writes the
  stripped spec unquoted before `Z`), and turns `astimezone`'s
  OverflowError outside the calendar into the "lies outside the
  calendar" text.
- `parse_window_bound` takes `now` as an argument (the reference's
  `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` is the caller's). A stripped `""` or
  `"all"` is None. A token is `parse_since` of the stripped text, so its
  errors name `--since` under `--until` too, and it is refused when it
  is longer than `now - _EARLIEST_START` as instants, exact to the
  microsecond (a span equal to it is kept). The shape test reads the raw
  spec: a `str.isdigit` character (`unicode::is_digit`) and a `-`; the
  compact `20261001T000000Z`, which `fromisoformat` reads, is refused
  there for want of a `-`. An absolute bound later than `now` as an
  instant is refused when the flag is the literal `--since`; under any
  other flag it is kept. A naive `now` raises TypeError where the
  reference subtracts it (a token) or compares it (an absolute
  `--since`), and is used as given elsewhere.
- `resolve_window` is `now` minus a span (`DateTime::minus_micros`, the
  offset kept) and an absolute bound as it is; OverflowError ("date
  value out of range") outside the calendar. A span past `i64`
  microseconds is refused before the subtraction: no `timedelta` holds
  one, and it leaves the calendar from any `now`.
- `_show_in_window` reads `show.get("ts")` (AttributeError with
  CPython's text for a value that is not a dict), `parse_event_ts` of a
  `str` only, and keeps a row without a readable stamp only in an
  unbounded window; `stamp >= start` and `stamp < end` compare instants,
  in the reference's order, so a naive `end` raises only when the start
  test passed.
- `_canonical_top_hit_id` and `_silent_miss_from_event` read the event
  as `health_model` does (the last value of a `str` key). The session is
  `ev.get("session_id") or ev.get("session")` with Python truthiness
  (`events::truthy`: an empty `str`, 0, -0.0, False, an empty list,
  tuple or dict and None fall through). The legacy `top_hit_ids` is read
  when `top_hits` is not a list or is an empty one, never when its first
  entry is not a dict. `recent_retrieval_count` is an `int` that is not
  a `bool`, else 0.
- Unit 1 adds no regular expression to the inventory; `_SINCE_PATTERN`
  was there.

Fixtures and tests: `tests/contract/gen_eval_model.py` writes
`eval_model.jsonl` (437 rows and a sweep, 84 KB): `RateCI` over 25
count pairs (zero and negative denominators, torn reads, past 2**53, the
ends of `i64`), the interval over 8 pairs at 10 values of `z` (NaN, both
infinities, both zeros, a negative `z`, the extremes) and at one `z`
whose square is a subnormal (where `z * z / (2.0 * n)` and
`z * z / 2.0 / n` differ), 10 cold rows
(surrogates, sums past `i64`, negative counts), 57 `parse_since` specs
(every unit, zero, leading zeros, whitespace from `str.isspace`, Arabic,
Devanagari and fullwidth digits, a superscript, the overflow edges in
every unit, 4,300 digits), 76 window bounds over `now` at 2026, with
offsets, naive, one microsecond either side of a second, and at years 1
and 9999 (the year-1 edge in seconds and days, offsets of hours,
naive, outside the calendar at both ends, later than now under each
flag, and a spec padded with spaces for each message that spells the
stripped spec), 12 resolutions, 100 `_show_in_window` cases over stamp shapes at
each bound, and 69 events through both readers. The sweep is 20,000
drawn `(k, n)` pairs through `RateCI.from_counts` by the SHA-256 of their
bits. `eval_model_python.jsonl` (`PYTHON_GATED`, 53 rows, 9 KB) holds
timestamps at `fromisoformat`'s edges (offsets of seconds and
microseconds, reduced and compact forms, an hour of 24, a lowercase `z`
inside `parse_event_ts`) and the text of `int()`'s digit limit,
CPython's own message. 3.11.15 and 3.12.13 write it byte for byte as
3.13.13 does; 3.14.10 differs on 7 rows: its `fromisoformat` keeps an
offset's microseconds, which 3.13.13 drops
(`2026-10-01T00:00:00-00:00:00.000001` is 00:00 UTC under 3.13.13 and
00:00:00.000001 under 3.14; `0001-01-01T00:00:00+00:00:00.000001` leaves
the calendar only under 3.14), and it reads an hour of 24
(`2026-10-01T24:00:00Z`, refused by 3.13.13, is the next midnight).
CI's 3.13.18 reads `fromisoformat` otherwise than 3.13.13 too
(`PYTHON_VERSION` in `generate.py`). `golden_eval_model.rs` checks every row of both, the
header's constants and the sweep; `eval_model_kills.rs` holds the cases
a plausible wrong port fails (`f64` division of counts past 2**53 for
the rate and for `p`, `z * z / n` reordered, a clamp for Python's
`max` and `min`, the rate not clamped on a torn read, `\d` or `int()`
read as ASCII, the digit limit turned into the `--since` text, the
year-1 edge off by a microsecond, a later `--until` refused, a
wall-clock comparison of offsets, `or` read as is-None for the session,
the legacy ids not read for an empty `top_hits`, a bool counted);
`eval_model_robustness.rs` takes counts at both ends of `i64`, `z` at
every extreme, a megabyte of digits (with a unit, without one, and with
a `-`) and of whitespace with growth claims through `tests/timing`,
every numeric code point before a unit, `now` at years 1 and 9999 with
offsets up to a day, and events 100,000 deep and 200,000 keys wide.

Known costs, measured in release against CPython 3.13.13 on one machine
(two runs each); both come from shared parts, not from this unit:

- A megabyte of ASCII digits and a unit (`'1' * 10**6 + 'd'`):
  `parse_window_bound` takes 30 to 35 ms where the reference takes
  2.6 ms (11 to 13 times), `parse_since` 13.7 to 16.3 ms against 1.5 ms
  (9 to 11 times), and `'0' * 10**6 + 'd'` as a bound 28.7 to 35.1 ms
  against 2.6 to 4.8 ms. The time is the engine's `\d+` over the run
  (`pyre`), matched twice as the reference matches it (once in
  `parse_window_bound`, again in `parse_since`); it grows linearly
  (`eval_model_robustness.rs` holds the claim). Every other input
  measured is under 5 times the reference (a megabyte of Arabic digits
  1.7 times; a megabyte of ideographic spaces around `30d` is faster
  than the reference).
- `silent_miss_from_event` of a dict of 10**6 keys takes 10.9 ms
  against 0.017 ms (about 640 times): `PyValue::Dict` is a list of pairs
  read from the end for each key, the crate-wide representation, and
  building such an input is linear already.

## The eval family's renderers (`eval_render.py`)

`eval_render.py` (1,199 lines) turns the reports `eval.py` computes into
text: the plain-text rendering of each `eval` mode and the markdown of
`eval --report`. Its report classes live in `eval.py`; unit 1 of
`eval.py` (`src/eval.rs`) builds `EvalReport`, the one class the first
renderer unit reads. Nothing here asks the machine: a report is an
argument, and every text the store or the log gave goes through
`history.printable` (built, `printable::printable`). The module is cut
into four units; unit eval_render-1 is built (`src/eval_render.rs`, 783
lines with comments, and 218 in `src/eval.rs`), with two formats of
Python's `format` added to `src/float_repr.rs`.

| function | reference lines | needs | unit, status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render_text`, `_text` | 49-174 | `EvalReport`, `printable`, `isoformat_utc_optional`, `HOOKLESS_REASON` | eval_render-1, built |
| `_review_text_lines` | 176-220 | the review dict (`review_counters.ReviewReport.to_dict()`) as a `PyValue` | eval_render-1, built |
| `_rate_from_dict`, `_SURFACE_RATES`, `_surface_text_lines`, `_rule_split_text_lines` | 223-325 | the surfaces dict (`compute_surface_report`) as a `PyValue`, `EARLIER_RULES` | eval_render-1, built |
| `_format_rate`, `_bar`, `_truncate`, `_humanize_seconds`, `_short_ts` | 332-380 | `format_fixed`, round half to even | eval_render-1, built |
| `render_threshold_sweep_text`, `render_widening_preview_text` | 387-506 | `ThresholdSweepReport`, `WideningPreviewReport` and eval_model-2's rows | eval_render-1b, after eval_model-2 |
| `_clip`, `render_widening_detail_text`, `render_tool_usage_text` | 508-652 | `WideningDetailReport`, `ToolUsageReport` | eval_render-2 |
| `_md_escape_cell` through `render_report_markdown` | 654-1199 | `ReportDocument` and every report above | eval_render-3 |

**`EvalReport`** (`eval.py` 138-321) carries every count, row and rate
of `compute_eval`. The reference gives its first thirteen fields
(`generated_at` through `silent_misses`) no default; `EvalReport::new`
sets them to zero, None and the empty text for a caller to fill, and
every other field to the reference's default: `RateCI(0, 0, None, None,
None)` (`NO_RATE`), `DEFAULT_ENDORSEMENT_MIN_RETRIEVALS`, a ratio
threshold of 0.0, False, empty lists and dicts, None. `by_model` is the
reference's `dict[str, dict[str, int]]` as pairs in insertion order, its
keys distinct as a dict's are; `window_seconds` is `Option<i64>`.
`review` and `surfaces` are the dicts `ReviewReport.to_dict()` and
`compute_surface_report` make, carried as `PyValue`s and passed through
`to_dict` as they are. `to_dict` answers the reference's key order,
`surfaces` only when it is not None (a `PyValue::None` counts as None),
`suppressed_reason` the shared `HOOKLESS_REASON` sentence or None.
`compute_eval` and `_eval_report` fill it in unit eval-1; the other
report classes of `eval.py` and their computations follow with the
renderer units that read them.

**Unit eval_render-1, built.** `render_text` reproduces the reference
line by line: the window header three ways (all time, `last` a
humanized span, or both absolute ends with `the start` for an open
one), the scope part only for a non-empty scope, the count rows as
`:>5d` (the no-signal and repeat rows only when non-zero), the rate
trio, the per-model rows in `sorted(by_model)` order (code point order,
which is `Vec<u32>`'s), each model padded to 28 code points with
`counts.get(key, 0)` at `:<5d` and `:<4d`, the cold-endorsement bucket
(the first ten rows, `printable(','.join(scopes)) or` the em dash
(U+2014), the explicit share only when `ratio > 0`, so never for a NaN
ratio, the rule naming `{ratio:g}`, the remainder line past ten) or the
suppressed sentence, the silent-miss rows (`top_missed_id or` the dash,
so an empty id reads as missing; `session_id[:12]` and `_short_ts` in
code points), the threshold rule, the review and surfaces sections, the
torn-read note, and `_text`'s second `printable` pass with a final
newline.

Python's `format` is built on Rust's, which writes the exact binary
value's digits rounded half to even. `'0.2f'` is
`float_repr::format_fixed(x, 2)`, Rust's `{:.2}` (0.125 is `0.12`, 2.675
is `2.67`, 0.005 is `0.01`, a minus sign on every negative value, so
`-0.00` for -0.001, and `inf`, `-inf`) but for a NaN of either sign,
`nan` where Rust writes `NaN`. Past 1,074 places every digit is a zero
and is written out, since Rust's precision stops at `u16::MAX`; a
precision past `INT_MAX` is refused (`PrecisionTooBig`), as Python
refuses it with ValueError before it reads the value. `'g'` is
`float_repr::format_general`: the six significant digits of Rust's
`{:.5e}`, positional for a decimal exponent in `-4 <= exp < 6` and
`1e-05`, `1.23457e+06` otherwise (Rust's `{}` writes `0.00001` and
`1234567`), trailing zeros and a bare point dropped, `-0` for negative
zero, `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`. `_bar` is Python's `max(0.0, min(1.0,
rate))`, under which a NaN rate is a full bar, then `round(rate * 10)`
half to even (`round(2.5)` is 2; `f64::round` gives 3). The NaN is
tested before the clamp: an optimised arm64 build folds `if rate < 1.0
{ rate } else { 1.0 }` into `fminnm`, which passes a signalling NaN
through to an empty bar. Widths
(`:<28s`, `:<18s`, `:<20s`) pad by code points, not bytes or columns.
`_humanize_seconds` floors as Python's `%` and `//` do (-90 is `-90s`,
-120 is `-2m`). `_truncate` and `_short_ts` count code points;
`_truncate` with `n = 0` slices to `-1` as Python does, a case the
reference never reaches.

The review and surfaces sections read their dicts as the reference
does, and where it raises the answer is its exception class
(`RenderError`; messages are not compared): subscription is KeyError
for a missing key and TypeError for a value that is not a dict;
`.items()` on anything but a dict is AttributeError; `', '.join(value)`
reads a list's or tuple's elements, a `str`'s characters or a dict's
keys, TypeError for a non-`str` element or a value that is not
iterable; truthiness decides `not review`, `not chains['issued']`
(a NaN is true), `if suppressed`, `if grades['n']`, `if
grade['graded']` and `if tally['deliveries']`; `surfaces is None` is an
identity test, so an empty dict is read and raises KeyError. `str()` and
an f-string's `format(value, '')` spell through
`pyvalue::py_str_limited`, shared with `history_render`'s detail names
(a float as its `repr`, True as `True`, a container as its `repr`),
which raises the first of `repr`'s two faults in the order it writes: a
level past `json::MAX_DEPTH` (RecursionError) or an `int` of more than
4,300 digits (ValueError). Through `_review_text_lines` CPython 3.13.13
answers RecursionError for `[<9,998 nested lists>, 10**4300]` and
ValueError for 9,997; the bound follows the release, so
`eval_render_robustness` pins it and no golden row sits near it. `_rate_from_dict` reads its six keys in order,
`torn_read` included though nothing prints it. `_format_rate` over a
dict's values runs `_bar` first: an `int` or a bool compares exactly
(one and above a full bar, zero and below an empty one) and any other
type but a float is TypeError there, so a `str` rate is TypeError where
a `str` bound is ValueError (the format code); an `int` bound formats
through `float()` (OverflowError past the doubles), a datetime as its
`strftime('0.2f')`, which is `0.2f`, a path, list, tuple or dict
TypeError. `_rule_split_text_lines` answers nothing when `by_rule` is
not a dict, the membership delta line included; a group other than
`earlier` is its key's `str()`, spelled after `split[surface]` is read
(an `int` key past 4,300 digits over an empty split is KeyError, not
ValueError).

Fixtures: `tests/contract/gen_eval_render.py` writes `eval_render.jsonl`
(not gated: ASCII texts but for the renderer's own characters, which
every Unicode release calls printable, and float formatting from the
exact binary value) and `eval_render_unicode.jsonl` (`UNICODE_GATED`,
mirrored in `gates_of`: ids, models, summaries, scopes, keys and stamps
past ASCII, whose `printable` escapes read the Unicode database). Reports
are written as specs (what differs from the empty report), dicts as
edits of a base review and a base surfaces dict in the header, and each
answer as one edit of a base text (the empty report's text, its
`to_dict` dumped with `indent=1`, the base sections), so a reader sees
what each case changes. `to_dict` of a report carrying a review or
surfaces dict is pinned by the SHA-256 of its dump. The last row is a
sweep of 5,000 reports drawn from a seed (windows, scopes, counts at
both ends of `i64`, rates from `RateCI.from_counts`, cold rows, ratios
with NaN and infinity, misses, models, the base dicts), pinned by count
and the SHA-256 of each `render_text` and `json.dumps(to_dict())`.

Tests: `golden_eval_render` (every row of both files, the header's base
texts against the port's own answers, the sweep redrawn by the
generator's rule); `eval_render_kills` (`f64::round` in `_bar`, a
signalling NaN's bar, `NaN`, `{}` for `'g'`, decimal-text rounding for
`'0.2f'`, byte or width padding, `by_model` sorted by UTF-16 units or
by the escaped text, `or` read as is-None, the share for a NaN ratio,
`.get` where the reference subscripts, truthiness where it tests `is
None`);
`eval_render_robustness` (100,000 cold rows and models and 100,000
review actions, megabyte ids, summaries and models, every float extreme
in each rate field and the ratio, `i64` extremes, review and surfaces
dicts nested 10,000 deep, the depth bound against the int limit, a
precision past `INT_MAX`; growth linear through `tests/timing`, and the
float extremes through `'g'` and `'0.2f'` within ten times the cost of
0.5).

Patterns: none. The unit matches no regular expression.

Reference observations, reproduced: a `str` rate in a surfaces rate dict
raises TypeError from `_bar` before `'0.2f'` could raise ValueError; a
`by_rule` that is not a dict drops the membership delta line with the
split; a negative `cold_endorsement_memories_total` with no rows prints
the bucket's header with that total and no rows.
