No regular expression is used.

### An entry advanced over the log (unit store_index-advance)

`store::docfreq_store::advance` (a child module of `docfreq_store`, so it
uses the parent's private `digest_row`, `cells`, `value`, `scopes`,
`actor_of`, `home_key` and the source's connection as they are) is `store_index._advanced_inputs`
(store_index.py 474-602) with `_HEAD_KINDS` (459) and `_ADVANCE_ROWS`
(463); `StoreDocFreq`'s `advanced_inputs` calls it, and
`DocFreqMemo::current_inputs` calls that for an entry kept at an older
head and copies the entry's terms on `Some`. Step by step, as the
reference:

- None when the entry carries no lengths (read without the digest), no
  `group_of` or no `length_of`, or when the head's seq is not past the
  entry's.
- `SELECT mac FROM log WHERE seq = ?` at the entry's seq: None when the
  row is gone or `str()` of its MAC differs (another history). A failure
  of this statement is raised, uncaught, as there.
- The log's rows of `_HEAD_KINDS` after the entry's seq and up to the
  head's, in seq order, read as sqlite3 hands them on (a row converted,
  the step to the next taken, then the row used; a text that is not UTF-8
  is OperationalError, raised). `memory_put` names
  `json.loads(payload)['memory']['id']`, `home_put`
  `['home']['record_id']`, `home_delete` `['record_id']`: a text payload
  is read with `json::loads_detailed`, a BLOB with `json::loads_bytes`
  (`json.detect_encoding`), anything else is TypeError. A `memory_delete`
  or `index_rebuilt` row, or a payload whose reading or indexing fails
  (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, all caught), is None. RecursionError
  is not caught: past `json::MAX_DEPTH` it is raised. That limit is
  CPython 3.13.13's at the shallowest call site, a script's top level
  (9,999 containers); the reference's C decoder counts against the C
  stack its callers have already used, so inside the advance, reached
  through `Store.document_frequencies`, it raises from 9,981 containers
  (measured in a pytest run), while the port raises from 9,999 wherever
  it is called. No fixture row holds a depth within 30 levels of 10,000. The id is `str()` of the value (`pyvalue::py_str`: a number's
  digits, a list's `repr`), kept first seen first without repeats; as
  soon as the ids and the entry's `changed` together pass 256, None.
- `digest_mark(build=False)`: None when it answers None. Its warning is
  the advance's own, so on a read-only connection, under `query_only` or
  a busy writer, after a moved head, the reference's two `could not be
  brought current` warnings are both logged here.
- The digest's active rows of those ids, `provenance::BATCH` (500) per
  statement, with `digest_admission_rows`' typing (`int()` of the row
  number and length raised where it does not read, ValueError or
  TypeError, and for an infinite REAL OverflowError; a number past 64
  bits read whole, as store-2 above says). The statement is
  prepared before the ids are bound, so a statement that fails is None
  and an id holding a lone surrogate is then UnicodeEncodeError, raised
  (the reference's `sqlite3` binds after it prepares and does not catch
  it). An SQLite error in the read (a step, a text that is not UTF-8, a
  table that is not there) is None with no warning. Each row is typed in
  the fold, its failures in the reference's order: a scopes text that is
  not JSON (JSONDecodeError), an index past an array of the entry
  (IndexError), an actor pydantic refuses on a new group (a row whose
  scopes are a list), a length past 64 bits `array('q')` refuses
  (OverflowError). A group key made here equals one `from_rows` makes.
- The fold: a row number not in the index takes the index's length as a
  new position only when its scopes are a list (else the row is
  skipped); a known one is taken out of its group (the bit cleared, the
  group's length reduced) and left in none; `(version, rid, position)`
  is appended to `changed` for a position that exists; then a row whose
  scopes are a list joins the group of its key (a new group at the end,
  with its `Actor`, where none has that key) and takes its length. The
  version is the entry's plus one. A row number past 64 bits is a key
  like any other: a new one takes a new position, one the entry holds
  (read so by a full read) its old one. Index, `group_of`, `length_of`,
  groups and keys are copied once (the reference's own `dict(...)` and
  array copies), and the work past that is per row read.

Decisions:

- The chunked read is reproduced though it cannot be reached: 256 ids is
  the most an advance reads, and a chunk holds 500. 500 and 501 ids in
  one span are None at the bound (robustness).
- Only rows the log names are read. A digest row changed with no log
  row keeps its old group in the advanced entry, where a fresh read
  would see it as it now stands. This is the reference's behaviour,
  reproduced (`advance_digest_unread` in the fixture). Linear ENG-413
  records it as a reference finding (the memo disagrees with the
  reference's own fresh read); until the reference changes, the port
  answers as it does now.
- An index past any array of the entry (`group_of`, `length_of`,
  `groups`, `lengths`), which no entry the grouping makes holds, is
  `DocFreqError::IndexError`, the reference's IndexError (each array
  shortened by one, a new row's position past a shorter `group_of`, a
  new group's total past a shorter `lengths`: robustness), rather than a
  panic.
- An entry at version `u64::MAX` is read again (None) where the
  reference answers an advanced entry at version 2**64, which a u64
  does not hold. The reference cannot reach that version (2**64
  advances); None is the answer closest to it, since the entry read
  again answers as the advanced one would, and debug and release answer
  alike.
- A reference finding, reproduced and not corrected: a digest row whose
  row number was changed under the digest (planted), then named by the
  log, is a new key, so the record counts at its old position and at a
  new one (the reference's `index.get(rid)` is None for the new number).
  A row number changed within 64 bits does the same in both;
  `advance_big_numbers` holds it for one past 64 bits. Related to Linear
  ENG-413.

Fixture: `gen_store_docfreq_store.py` no longer runs each case a second
time without `_advanced_inputs`; the golden test compares every step's
answers, memo keys and terms, warnings and memo entries with the
reference's one run, with the one allowance below. Each step records every memo
entry's inputs in canonical form (head; groups with scopes as JSON text,
home, actor and the positions their mask holds; lengths; the index as
sorted pairs; keys; `group_of`; `length_of`; version; `changed`), or the
SHA-256 of that JSON text past 500 bytes; the test builds the same form
from the port's entry. The one stated difference is a group key's client
or model the reference holds as bytes, which the port holds as its UTF-8
text (store-2's bytes client; `digest_client_bytes`): the test reads
such a fixture key as that text. Cases added: `advance_moves` (a row in
place, a new position, a new group at the end by scopes, client, model
and home, a group the entry holds, two puts of one record, then a reader
and `query_only` after a moved head), `advance_scopes_not_list` (a
digest row whose scopes stop being a list and become one again; a new
row whose scopes are not a list), `advance_not_followed` (a
`memory_delete`, an `index_rebuilt` row, then an entry read without the
digest), `advance_bound` (253 and 254 ids after three changed rows, 256
and 257 after none, 600 rows naming 256 and 257 ids), `advance_head_row`
(the MAC at the entry's head changed, then the row gone),
`advance_payloads` (an id that is a number, a list, bytes of JSON, a
real record named again; a payload that is not JSON, without the key,
not a dict, not text; an id holding a lone surrogate and a payload that
is not UTF-8, both raised), `advance_big_numbers` (a length past 64 bits
on a named row whose scopes are not a list, then on one whose scopes are
a list after an earlier row's refused actor; a row number past 64 bits
named, counted at both positions, a kept term patched from it alone and
with a lower row number, then named again) and `advance_digest_unread`
(a digest row changed with no log row, a new memo key reading it, then
the digest's join failing after the advance's mark). A step's `plant` holds log rows
planted after the step's tables were taken (a run of `home_delete` rows
naming records no store holds, a changed or deleted log row), which the
replay runs after it lays the tables. To keep the files small the tables
are recorded without their column lists and `memories` and
`digest_records` as the rows changed since the last step; each file's
header holds each table's columns in the opened store once, and the
replay checks its own open against them before it lays a step by
position (a column order that drifted fails there). An integer past 64
bits is recorded as its decimal text under `$int`. The advance's cases
are `store_docfreq_advance.jsonl` (128 KB); the store's cases are split
over `store_docfreq_store.jsonl` (107 KB) and
`store_docfreq_store_b.jsonl` (116 KB). Tests:
`golden_store_docfreq_store`, `store_docfreq_advance_kills` (a moved
row's bit and length left behind, a new non-list row given a position,
a row that left every group missing from `changed`, the bound off by
one or without `changed`, a `memory_delete` or rebuild followed, the MAC
check dropped, `digest_mark` not called, a digest row the log did not
name read, the id not `str()` of the value, payloads that do not read,
a digest text that is not UTF-8 read again with no warning, a head at
the entry's own seq) and `store_docfreq_advance_robustness` (256 rows on
an entry of 200,000 within four times a copy of the entry plus the
timing module's 50 ms of slack: in release the advance takes 0.8 ms
against 0.12 ms for the copy, so the test holds the advance to no copy
per row, hundreds of milliseconds, not to the factor; payloads nested
at `json::MAX_DEPTH` and 100,000 deep, 500 and 501 ids, row numbers at
the ends of `i64` with lengths past it, numbers past 64 bits, an entry
at the last version, entries whose arrays disagree, eight threads each
held inside its advance until all eight advanced);
both run everywhere, over a store made by hand
(`common::docfreq_store::HandStore`).

A payload nested past the JSON limit is pinned in the robustness test
and not in the fixture: where the decoder stops follows the release and
the system (CPython 3.14 on Linux reads it), and the fixture has no
Python-gated sibling.

No regular expression is used.

### A search pool's rows through the memo (unit poolmemo)

`store::docfreq_store::admitted` (a child module of `docfreq_store`) is
`store_index.admitted_rows`, `_admitter`, `ranked_admitted_rows`,
`admitted_share` and `_admitted_rows_read` (store_index.py 680-811), each
over any `DocFreqSource`, the connection the rows and the ranking are
read on, and a `DocFreqMemo`; the predicate is `StoreAdmit` (scopes,
home, actor), as `document_frequencies` takes it. `store::index_reads`
gains `ranked_rows(conn, text, limit)` (215-236: the ranking's text, with
` LIMIT ?` when a limit is given; nothing read for a blank text or an
empty match query) and `newest_rows(conn, limit, offset)` (271-282: `...
LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`), and `RankedQuery` now takes its statement from the
connection's statement cache, as these do: the reference's `execute`
goes through `sqlite3`'s.

Step by step, as the reference:

- `admitted_rows`: no row answers at once, before any input is read.
- `Admitter::new` (`_admitter`): inside a transaction (`in_transaction`,
  the reference's `_tx_depth or in_transaction`) it holds nothing and
  every row is decided from its own columns. Outside, through
  `DocFreqMemo::admitted_inputs`: `_current_inputs`, `_admitted_mask`,
  and the entry kept with no terms when this call read it and the memory
  head did not move meanwhile. The mask is read as `to_bytes((len(index)
  + 7) // 8 or 1, "little")` reads it: a mask wider than those bytes is
  OverflowError, a position past them IndexError (neither is reached by
  inputs the grouping makes, which raises IndexError first).
- `Admitter::decide`: the rows the inputs do not hold (a repeat kept) are
  read first, all of them, by `_admitted_rows_read`; then each row in
  its turn, a held row by its bit, another by that read.
- `_admitted_rows_read`: `_ADMISSION_INPUTS WHERE m.rowid IN (?,...)`, one
  statement per `_PROVENANCE_BATCH` (500) of the rows, each through the
  statement cache. Every row a statement finds is fetched (each column
  decoded: a text that is not UTF-8 is OperationalError) before any is
  decided, a later row of one number replacing an earlier one; then each
  row asked: one not found is admitted nowhere; its scopes are
  `_load_json(column, None)` (NULL and a value that is not a list admit
  nowhere; a text that is not JSON is JSONDecodeError, a number
  TypeError, bytes read as `json.loads` reads them); its actor is
  `Actor(client, model)` where either is set (a column pydantic refuses
  is ValidationError); its home is the column as it is.
- `ranked_admitted_rows`: the admitter first, then the ranking's one
  statement read `batch` rows at a time, each batch decided, until
  `size` rows are found; at most `size` are returned.
- `admitted_share`: None inside a transaction; else the admitted count
  and the inputs' row count.

`store::pool` draws its pool as `handlers.search._admitted_candidates`
(272-321) does, with `FIRST_READ` (`_FIRST_READ`, 800): an empty query
(`str.strip` leaves nothing) pages `newest_rows(800, offset)` through
`admitted_rows` until `size` rows or a short page; another asks
`admitted_share` and, where the request admits enough of the store
(`share is None or admitted * 800 >= size * rows`, in `u128`, which no
`usize` operands overflow), reads `ranked_rows(query, 800)` through
`admitted_rows`; where the share was narrow, or those rows fell short
with 800 read, `ranked_admitted_rows(size, 800)` from the start. Then
the stored tokenizer and `light_many(rows[:size])`.
`SearchPool::statistics` is `docfreq_store::ranking_statistics_from`,
read when called: the memo's four items outside a transaction, the
uncached three and no average inside one. The predicate
(`Filters::predicate`) is `_admit_predicate` over a group's inputs: a
home in bytes is read as its `str()`, and a scope that is not a string
refuses the call (TypeError, the pool's stated difference).

The pool's source (`PoolSource`; the open point of the digest settled as
option (a)) is `StoreDocFreq` over the pool's connection, keyed by the
store's path as it was opened (`StoreFile::path`, never the private copy
a read-only open may read) and meta's store id (read at a reader's first
pool), for every read but two. The digest's rows come from
`PoolReader::digest_rows`, which brings a digest that is behind forward
in memory and writes nothing, where `StoreDocFreq::digest_mark` would
write it (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, which a read-only connection refuses). And
a kept entry is brought forward from the log (`_advanced_inputs`) only
where the digest is current, so the advance's own `digest_mark` never
writes; elsewhere the inputs are read again, to the same answer. The
question is asked where the reference asks `digest_mark(build=False)`:
after the log row at the entry's head and the log rows since are read
(`StoreDocFreq::advanced_inputs_marked`, the store's advance with the
digest's check given), so a digest that cannot serve the advance (its
state gone, made under other rules, marked at a log row whose MAC is not
the one it saw, or behind) costs those two reads on both sides, and a
log payload nested past the parser's depth raises before it. Option
(b), `StoreDocFreq` whole, was measured on `search_store.jsonl`'s twenty
stores: on the eleven whose digest is behind and can be brought forward
(`far behind`, `one put`, `restore`, `several puts`, `tombstone`,
`unseen blob payload`, `unseen blob payload with bom`, `unseen id
float`, `unseen id null`, `unseen id true`, `update`) it answers no
average where the fixture pins one (the reference's generator brings
the digest current), so those rankings would move; (a) keeps every
answer. A digest fingerprint other than the one this build computes
(`digest::fingerprint()`), or none, goes into the key after a NUL, which
no store id holds, so inputs read under one set of rules are never
handed to another.

`PoolReader::new(&StoreFile)` reads through the process's memo
(`docfreq::memo()`) and `PoolReader::with_memo(&StoreFile, &DocFreqMemo)`
through another (the second open point: a test passes a memo of its
own, and no caller's call changed). The reader's own inputs memo, its
per-row read of a row the inputs lack, its whole-ranking and whole-newest
reads and its per-term reads of the index are gone. `reads::term_masks_by`
takes its statement from the statement cache, as `Store._term_masks`
sends its one text through the reference's.

Decisions:

- A failure of the memo or of a row's own columns that names a Python
  exception the crate models (`PyError`) is `PoolError::Store(Py)`, as
  the pool raised it before; any other class (JSONDecodeError,
  ValidationError, IndexError, `sqlite3`'s classes) is the new
  `PoolError::Raised(class)`.
- The share test is taken in `u128`: a pool size of `usize::MAX` reads
  the whole ranking where an `i64` or `usize` product would overflow.
- A pool's statistics are read through the memo each call, as the
  reference's provider does, not from inputs the pool held when drawn.

Left for later units: the error surface of a refused prepare (set-aside
item 1), the hydrator and `seed_tokens` (the pool still tokenizes
bodies), and a writable open's pool, whose digest the memo's source
would bring current by writing it.

Tests: `store_provenance_cache.rs`' pool cases, each against the
reference (below, in "The store connection's statement cache");
`store_pool_memo_kills` (inputs kept for another store of the same id or
another memory head, the key naming the private copy, statistics from
the memo inside a transaction, unknown rows read one by one or all in
one statement (the texts a 600-row pool sends, by the statement cache),
inputs read for no row, the share test past 64 bits (a wide then a
narrow pool told apart by the texts they send), an empty query
not paged, a narrow request and a short wide one not ranked whole, mask
positions each side of the first two 64-row words; and by the texts a
pool sends, the batch of 500 (stores of 500, 501 and 600 unknown rows),
the share test at equality (50 of 50 rows for a pool of 800: wide), a
first read that fills the pool exactly (not read again), the first
read's 800 rows (a request whose rows start past them reads the
ranking again), a pool inside a transaction reading the index's best
rows first, a kept entry not advanced over a digest behind the log;
rows the inputs lack decided by their own columns (scopes `null` and
`{}` admitted nowhere; a writer with a model and no client, and client
and model told apart), the empty query's pages reading each row once
(the 800th newest row admitted), a scope that is not a string refused
on the empty query's pages, `ranked_admitted_rows` called directly (it
stops at its size at a batch's end, so a later row that does not load
is never read, and cuts to its size), and `PoolReader::new` keeping its
inputs in the process's memo) and
`store_pool_memo_robustness` (100,000 rows with a request that admits
one in 10,000, its time within `TENFOLD` of 10,000 rows' by the wall
clock; 2,001 unknown rows, five statements of at most 500 rows; eight threads drawing
pools through one memo; pool sizes 0 and `usize::MAX`), over copies of
`store_files.jsonl`'s ``intact`` base (`tests/pool_memo`).
`golden_search_store` and `golden_caller_admission` answer unchanged.

No regular expression is used.

## The restore lock, the writing open's side (`restore_lock.py`)

The module map (`src/bettermemory/restore_lock.py` as it is now) and its
cut. Status: built (reader), built (restore_lock-1), built (restore_lock-2,
the hold). The whole module is now ported.

| function | lines | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lock_path`, `_try_lock`, `_unlock`, `_lock_within`, `_open_record` (no create), `_store_handle`, `reading` | 239-243, 260-306, 330-344, 585-602, 855-922 | `flock`, a Windows handle | built (reader) |
| `_file_key`, `_Target`, `_open_target` (no create), `_take` | 309-327, 347-418 | `fstat`, `flock` | restore_lock-1 |
| `_read_marker`, `read_marker`, `describe` | 428-477 | one read of the record file | restore_lock-1 |
| `RestoreLockedError` | 480-535 | none | restore_lock-1 |
| `_SharedHold`, `_RecordCheck`, `_identity`, `_refuse_restored`, `_record_admission`, `admit` | 556-582, 640-734, 774-852 | `stat`, `flock` | restore_lock-1 |
| `_holds_by_handle`, `_open_store_handle`, `_behind_handle`, `_pause` | 605-637, 737-771 | a Windows handle, the clock | restore_lock-1, `cfg(windows)`, untested |
| `restore_state` | 1189-1222 | `flock` | restore_lock-1 |
| `_this_thread_holds`, `_HELD`, create mode of `_open_record` | 225-227, 330-344, 421-425 | a process-wide registry | restore_lock-2, built |
| `RestoreLock`, `mark`, `release` | 924-985 | the record file written, the clock, the pid | restore_lock-2, built |
| `held_here`, `acquire` | 987-1045 | `flock`, `fstat` | restore_lock-2, built |
| `probe` | 1053-1115 | SQLite (rusqlite) | restore_lock-2, built |
| `_holder`, `unlock` | 1118-1186 | `flock` | restore_lock-2, built |
| `state_finding` | 1225-1256 | `flock`, one read of the record file | restore_lock-2, built |

What restore_lock-1 reproduces (`store::restore_lock`):

- `take` is `_take(create=False)`: the store's directory (the parent of the
  path as given) opened and locked within the wait; a lock that cannot be
  had at all (`_Unlockable`) falls to the record file, which, when it
  cannot be locked either, counts as taken so that only a marker refuses.
  An open or `fstat` that fails is the reference's OSError: `admit` then
  admits with nothing held and `restore_state` answers clear. On Windows
  the lock is always exclusive, as `msvcrt.locking` is.
- `read_marker` is one read of at most 64 KiB (`_MARKER_CAP_BYTES`): None
  when the file does not open or holds only `bytes.strip()` whitespace
  (space, tab, LF, CR, VT, FF; the old create-side check used
  `u8::is_ascii_whitespace`, which leaves out VT); the object's items when
  `json.loads` of the bytes gives one; an empty marker for anything else
  (a decode or parse failure, a non-object); `{"unreadable": str(exc)}`
  when the read fails (a directory at the lock path), which `describe`
  ignores but which refuses as unfinished. `json.loads` of bytes is
  `json.detect_encoding` (UTF-32 and UTF-16 by BOM, then by the null bytes
  of the first four, `utf-8-sig`) with a `surrogatepass` decode: the
  helper `loads_bytes` takes the decode from
  `store::provenance::decode_json_bytes`, which already reproduces it.
  A marker nested past the decoder's depth raises RecursionError in the
  reference, out of `admit` and `restore_state` alike: here
  `AdmitError::Recursion`, `OpenError::MarkerRecursion` and
  `CreateError::MarkerRecursion` (class `RecursionError`; the message is
  not the reference's and is not pinned).
- `describe` and `RestoreLocked`'s `Display` (`str(RestoreLockedError)`):
  `<store> is not opened: ` and the running, unfinished or replaced text;
  `describe` and the "again" command go through `printable`, the paths do
  not, as in the reference. A `pid` that is a bool or a float is left out.
- `admit` returns `Admission::Shared` (the directory held shared),
  `Admission::Record` (`_RecordCheck`) or `Admission::None`; dropping it is
  `close`. `confirm` repeats the check in record mode (`restore_state`,
  then the store file's device and inode against those at `admit`: a
  different file is the replaced refusal) and does nothing for a shared
  hold. On Windows the record check holds the store file open and looks
  again behind the handle (`_behind_handle`), as the reference; that path
  is compiled only there and untested.
- `_this_thread_holds` is the `mine` argument (a `fn(FileKey) -> bool`, so
  a `RecordCheck` keeps it for `confirm`): no native restore exists, so
  `store::open` and `store::create` pass one that names nothing;
  restore_lock-2 supplies the registry. On Windows the key is the
  volume serial number and file index of `GetFileInformationByHandle`
  (`bettermemory_sys::file_index`), as `os.fstat` fills them.
  `_identity` still answers None there, so when the store
  file exists but no handle opens on it, a file replaced between `admit`
  and `confirm` is admitted where the reference raises the replaced
  wording of `RestoreLockedError` (part of the Windows gap).
- Record mode is found again on each call, as the reader does: no
  process-wide memory of record-mode directories and no log line. Tests
  reach it through `admit_in_record_mode` and
  `restore_state_in_record_mode`, as the generator puts the directory in
  `_RECORD_MODE_DIRS` (no local file system here refuses `flock`).

The writing open (`store::open`) and create (`store::create`) take
`admit` where they took `reading` and the create-side marker check
(`unfinished_restore`, removed with its private `printable`): a running
restore is now the reference's `RestoreLockedError` with the running text
(`OpenError::RestoreLocked`, `CreateError::RestoreLocked`), not the
reader's `RestoreRunningError`, which stays for the read-only path only.
`confirm` runs once the connection has read the store's schema
(`admission::admit`) and before the open reads its meta or keys; create
confirms once its temporary store is taken, before the schema is written.
No pattern of `re` is involved.

Pinned by the `admit` rows of `store_restore_lock.json` (53 cases: 36
marker shapes, a helper holding the directory shared or exclusively with
and without a marker, an unreadable marker, a missing directory, the
record mode free, empty, marked, held exclusively and shared, a directory
at the lock path, the store file swapped between `admit` and `confirm`,
a marker left after `admit`, and the same two in directory mode, where
neither refuses). The marker nested 70,000 lists deep is the one row of
`store_restore_lock_python.json`, gated on the Python release too:
whether `json.loads` raises RecursionError there is the interpreter's and
the system's. Each row holds `admit`'s answer, `confirm`'s and then
`restore_state`'s, with the store spelled `<store>` and the lock
`<lock>`; an unreadable marker's `str(exc)` (C library text) is not
recorded. Tests: `golden_restore_lock_admit` (the rows),
`restore_lock_admit_kills` and `restore_lock_admit_robustness`. POSIX
only, as the fixture; on Windows `restore_lock_not_posix.rs` records the
gap, and under `fsdata`'s Windows flavour nothing here resolves a path.

The Windows lock (fix unit winrestore). The reference's `_try_lock` on
Windows seeks to `_WINDOWS_LOCK_OFFSET` (1 MiB) and calls
`msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1)`, which is the CRT's `_locking` and so
`LockFile(h, 1 MiB, 0, 1, 0)`: one byte, exclusive, failing at once;
`_unlock` is `UnlockFile` of that byte, and every OSError of the take
reads as held. The port first took std's `File::try_lock`, which is
`LockFileEx(LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK | LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY)` over
the whole file. A range so locked refuses `ReadFile` through every other
handle, this process's own included (ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION), and
`read_marker` opens its own handle (`CreateFileW` with GENERIC_READ and
std's share mode READ | WRITE | DELETE): in `admit`, with the take's
handle holding, the read failed and the marker read as the
`{"unreadable": ...}` record, so the refusal said "no record of it
reads" (CI, golden_store_create, case restore_marker_beside). The port
now locks the reference's byte through `bettermemory_sys::lock_byte` and
`unlock_byte` (`LockFile`, `UnlockFile`); a marker is at most 64 KiB
read, so no read reaches the locked byte. A Python bettermemory and the
port lock the same byte of the same file, so they exclude each other,
and each reads the other's marker while it holds. The POSIX flavour is
unchanged (`flock`). The Windows paths, each with its verdict after the
fix: `reading`/`record_running` (record file opened read-write, locked
and let go, no read): right. `admit` (take, then `read_marker` through a
second handle while the take holds): was wrong, now reads. `restore_state`
(running: `read_marker` while another holds; unfinished: after the
unlock): was wrong while held, now reads. `acquire` (the marker read
through the holding handle after a seek): right, and still right.
`RestoreLock::mark` (truncate and write through the holding handle):
right. `release` (truncate, `UnlockFile`, close, then remove): right.
`unlock`'s held report (`read_marker` while a restore holds): was wrong,
now reads. `_holder`/`probe` (take and let go; `probe` opens the store
through SQLite, not the lock file): right. `_store_handle` (store file,
GENERIC_READ, share READ | WRITE): right, it locks nothing. No path takes
one lock twice through two handles of this process except where the
reference does too (a second handle's take is refused, as its second
descriptor's is). `restore_lock_byte_not_posix.rs` pins, on Windows, the
marker read while `admit` takes and while `acquire` holds, a second
handle's take refused (running), and the record read after release.
None of this has run on Windows here; CI runs it.
Every open of the record file (`open_record`, `open_lock_file`,
`read_marker`) now shares READ | WRITE without DELETE on Windows, as the
reference's `os.open` (the CRT's `_SH_DENYNO`) does. With std's default
share mode a release's unlink met a port handle and left the file
delete-pending, so the next restore's create and every opener's open of
the name failed with access denied, where the reference's unlink fails
and leaves the empty file. The module's `lock_tests` pin that an
`unlock_file` frees the lock while its handle stays open (flock on
POSIX, `UnlockFile` of the taken byte on Windows; a close frees either,
so the call sites that close right after an unlock cannot show it) and,
on Windows, that an open record file is not removed. Nothing of this has
been compiled or run on Windows here (the MSVC check stops in
libsqlite3-sys), and no test has a Python `msvcrt.locking` holder exclude
a port take or the reverse; CI's Windows jobs compile and run the Rust
side.


## The restore lock, a restore's own hold (`restore_lock.py`, restore_lock-2)

What restore_lock-2 reproduces (`store::restore_lock`), with the
reference's lines as they are now:

- `_HELD` and `_this_thread_holds` (225-227, 421-425): a process-wide
  `Mutex<HashMap<FileKey, ThreadId>>` behind a `OnceLock`, keyed by the
  locked file's device and inode. `this_thread_holds` is the `mine` that
  `store::open` and `store::create` now pass to `admit` (they passed one
  naming nothing); `acquire` passes `key in _HELD` by any thread. A
  poisoned mutex is used as it stands. On Windows the key is the volume
  serial number and file index (`bettermemory_sys::file_index`, the
  `GetFileInformationByHandle` call), as `os.fstat` gives `st_dev` and
  `st_ino` there, so the restore's own writing opens are admitted and
  `held_here` answers true for the holding thread; that branch is
  compiled and checked by clippy only.
- `RestoreLock` (924-985): `acquire` returns it; `mark(fields, now)`
  writes `format`, `pid` (`std::process::id`), `started_at` and `store`
  on the first mark only, updates the fields over them (a key already
  there keeps its place, as `dict.update`), and writes `json.dumps(...,
  sort_keys=True)` and a newline after `set_len(0)` and a seek to 0, then
  `fsync` with errors swallowed. The clock is an argument (`now`, the
  UTC time; `strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`). `store` is `str(Path)`:
  `config::pure_path` of the path as given, so `./` segments and doubled
  separators go as `pathlib` drops them; on POSIX a byte that is no UTF-8
  is the lone surrogate `os.fsdecode` makes of it (written `\udcXX` in
  the marker), as it is in `unlock`'s `lock`, the probe's message and
  `state_finding`'s `record`. The write is `write_all` where
  the reference makes one `os.write`; they differ only on a short write.
  A field JSON cannot spell (a datetime) is `HoldError::Type`, the
  reference's TypeError; one nested past `json.dumps`'s depth is
  `HoldError::Recursion`. `release(clear)` empties and removes the marker
  under the lock when `clear` (after the close on Windows), drops the
  registry entry, unlocks and closes. A `RestoreLock` dropped without
  `release` (a panic) stays held: its files are left open and its
  registry entry kept until the process ends, as the reference's file
  descriptors and `_HELD` entry outlive its object.
- `held_here` (987-997): `_take` shared with no wait; an OSError (no
  directory, a directory at the record path in record mode) is raised,
  as the reference raises it.
- `acquire` (1000-1045): `_take(create=True)` exclusively within `wait`
  (`RESTORE_WAIT`, 10 s, is the caller's default); None when held past
  the wait or by this process; the marker file opened read-write and made
  owner-only (`0o600`) when missing, read once as `previous`. A marker
  nested past the decoder's depth is `HoldError::Recursion`, as the
  reference's RecursionError, and the lock is let go. The unreachable
  "could not be made" FileNotFoundError is kept.
- `probe` (1053-1115): None unless the path is a regular file (following
  links); then `canonicalize` (the reference's `Path.resolve`) and the
  crate's `store::file_uri` (the reference's `sqlite_file_uri`, already
  in the crate, so none was written here) with `?mode=rw`, opened
  read-write without create, `busy_timeout(0)` (rusqlite's open sets five
  seconds; the reference's `timeout=0` none), then `PRAGMA trusted_schema
  = OFF`, `PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE` and `PRAGMA schema_version`,
  each stepped once as `Connection.execute` does. An error whose primary
  code is SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_LOCKED gives the message with the path as
  given (`str(Path)`); any other error, or an open that fails, is None.
  A rollback-journal connection inside a read transaction does not make
  the probe busy (it reads under SHARED); an open WAL connection does.
- `_holder` and `unlock` (1118-1186): `unlock(store, apply, wait)` with
  `wait` for `OPEN_WAIT_SECONDS`; the report is `UnlockReport` (status,
  `str(lock)`, marker, holder) and `UnlockStatus::exit` is `UNLOCK_EXIT`.
  `lock.exists()` follows links, as `Path.exists`.
- `state_finding` (1225-1256): `restore_state` with no wait and
  `this_thread_holds`; summary, remedy and details (`state`, `record`,
  then `restore` for running and unfinished) as `PyStr` and a dict in the
  reference's order; `describe` and the "again" command through
  `printable`.

Record mode is a parameter as in restore_lock-1: each public function
has a hidden `*_in_record_mode` twin for tests. No pattern of `re` is
involved.

Pinned by `store_restore_lock_hold.json` (18 hold rows, 11 probe rows)
and `store_restore_lock_hold_python.json` (1 hold row):
each hold row is a list of steps on one store (`acquire`, `mark`,
`release`, `held_here` from the holding thread and from another,
`state_finding` likewise, `unlock`, the names in the directory), over a
free store in directory mode, in record mode and spelled with a `./`
segment, a killed holder's marker taken over and cleared, markers that
are not JSON, blank or nested too deep, a helper holding the directory
or record file shared or exclusively, a directory at the lock path, and a
missing directory. The probe rows: no file, a directory, an empty file, a
file that is not a database, rollback-journal and WAL stores closed, idle,
reading and held open, the last also through a `./` segment and a link.
The pid, the clock's time, the paths and an unreadable marker's C library
text are spelled as placeholders. The marker nested 70,000 lists deep is
the one row of `store_restore_lock_hold_python.json`, gated on the Python
release too: whether `json.loads` raises RecursionError there is the
interpreter's and the system's. Tests: `golden_restore_lock_hold`,
`restore_lock_hold_kills` and `restore_lock_hold_robustness`; POSIX only
as the fixture, with `restore_lock_hold_not_posix.rs` recording the gap
(class os). Under `fsdata`'s Windows flavour nothing here resolves a path
(ENG-124).

## A restore's late `store_restored` row (`restore_rows.py`)

`restore_rows.py` (727 lines, its rules in the module docstring, 1-128)
appends the `store_restored` row a restore could not write: the restore
record beside the head (`<store_id>.backup_restore.json`) names each
restore of the store, and an entry whose `row` is still null gets its
row from the next owner's writing open (`settle`) or from the next
restore (`append_for`), or is withheld, with the reason written into the
entry (`row_withheld`) and said once. `store::restore_rows` holds the
whole module as functions over a `WritableStore` open for writing and
the caller's `Provider` (the log clock for the row and the head, the
engine version for its payload). The cut:

| function | reference | needs | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `restore_record_path` | 192-196 | nothing | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `_write_private` | 199-202 | the file system (`store::write::replace_retrying`, then 0600) | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `record_row`, `_fill` | 205-269 | the record's `flock`, `bounded_read`, `json` | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `pending` | 272-303 | `bounded_read`, `json`, `log::replaced::history_replaced_kind` | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `_seq_mac`, `_mac_at`, `_written_before`, `_row_at`, `_replaced_head`, `_withheld`, `_standing`, `_still_stands`, `_payload`, `_logged`, `_decide` | 306-469 | the connection, `datetime::parse_event_ts`, `store::rows::CONTROL_KINDS` | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `_settle_one` | 472-492 | `WritableStore::begin`, `log::replaced::append_history_replaced_in` | restore_rows-1a, built |
| `append_missing`, `_SAID`, `_SAID_BY_CLOCK`, `_clock_reading`, `_said`, `_report_withheld`, `append_for`, `settle` | 495-711 | all of the above | restore_rows-1a, built |
| the owner's writing open's calls of `settle` | `store_open.py` 98, 131, 248 | `store::open` | restore_rows-1b, built ("Opening a store for writing", "A restore's rows at the owner's open") |
| `backup._apply_restore`'s call of `append_for` | `backup.py` 1683 | the backup units | not built |

What restore_rows-1a reproduces, and the decisions:

- Warnings are data: each `log.warning` is a `Warning` pushed onto the
  caller's list in the reference's order, so a call that raises keeps
  what it said first. `format()` is the reference's format string and
  `args()` its arguments: the store's path, the record's path, a value
  `%s` spells as `str()` (a `restored_at` or `bundle` of any JSON type, a
  seq or None), a text, an int, and an exception kept as its class and
  SQLite's error name (`store::open::UpkeepCause`), never its text.
- What the reference raises is `RestoreError`: SQLite's error, a column
  that is not UTF-8 (`sqlite3`'s OperationalError), the transaction's or
  the append's `WriteError`, the record lock's `FlockError`, and
  RecursionError, OverflowError (a seq past SQLite's INTEGER, from the
  bound parameter), TypeError and ValueError. `RestoreError::cause` is
  what `settle`'s `except (sqlite3.Error, OSError, RuntimeError,
  ValueError)` catches, as the class it logs; OverflowError, TypeError
  and a refusal of this build raise out of `settle`, as the reference's
  OverflowError does.
- The record is read as `json.loads` reads bytes
  (`store::provenance::decode_json_bytes`, then `json::loads_detailed`):
  UTF-8 with or without its BOM, UTF-16 and UTF-32 by their BOM or their
  null bytes, read as the reference reads them (an editor's UTF-16 record
  is settled, and rewritten as `json.dumps` writes it, ASCII). The
  classes `pending` logs: FileNotFoundError is no record; any other
  OSError by `fsdata`'s class; IsADirectoryError for a directory (Python's
  `open` of the descriptor refuses it after `os.open` succeeds); ValueError
  for a file over the cap or not regular, and for an integer past 4,300
  digits; UnicodeDecodeError; JSONDecodeError. RecursionError leaves
  `pending` and `_fill`, as the reference's does.
- Python's `==` is `history_rows`' comparison (`py_ne`), used for every
  `==` of the module: numbers by value (`True == 1 == 1.0`), and a NaN
  inside a list or dict equal to a NaN there, since every NaN
  `json.loads` reads is one object (`json.decoder.NaN`) and a container
  compares its items by identity first; at the top a NaN equals nothing.
  So `append_for` of an entry whose `restored_at` is NaN finds no place
  for it and returns None (its row is appended, once), while one whose
  `restored_at` is `[NaN]` returns its row (`append_for_nan`,
  `append_for_nan_in_list`).
- `_fill` takes the record's lock (`fsutil::flock_excl(path, ".lock")`,
  blocking on POSIX), reads the record again, finds the last dict whose
  `row` is None (or missing) and whose `kind`, `store_id` and
  `restored_at` equal the entry's, sets the key in place (a new key at the
  end, as a dict does), drops `drop`, and writes `json.dumps(document,
  indent=2, sort_keys=True)` and a line feed atomically and owner-only.
  `fsutil` holds no atomic write and the two copies of `_write_private`
  in the crate (`log/ring.rs`, `machine/open.rs`) are private to their
  units, so this is a third over the same shared
  `store::write::replace_retrying`. The record's lock file is made 0600
  when missing; with the keys directory not writable that open fails
  and the OSError leaves `_fill`, as the reference's does
  (`lock_unmade`).
- `_standing` and `_logged` run the reference's SQL as written, with
  `sorted(CONTROL_KINDS)` as parameters; every column a row holds is
  decoded as `sqlite3` fetches it (a text that is not UTF-8 raises), a
  MAC or kind is compared as `str()` of its column (a blob is `b'...'`),
  and `ts` and `restored_at` are read by `parse_event_ts` and compared as
  instants. `_logged` reads a payload as `json.loads` reads it (text, or
  bytes for a blob; any other type is TypeError and skipped). A seq is an
  int, not a bool, bound as SQLite's INTEGER (OverflowError past it).
- `_settle_one` reads on the connection outside the lock, then begins the
  write transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, the busy timeout the wait),
  decides again, and appends through `append_history_replaced_in`
  (payload: the entry less `row_withheld`; `row` dropped and `kind` and
  `engine_version` set by the append) before it commits: the head moves
  once. When the second decision does not append, the transaction is
  committed with nothing written, as the reference's `with` exits.
- An entry `append_missing` is given is a dict (the reference's
  `Mapping`): another value is TypeError where the reference, calling
  `.get` on it, raises AttributeError. `append_for`'s entry is a dict
  too, and another value is TypeError, where the reference's
  `dict(entry)` answers by the value: TypeError for a number,
  ValueError for a str such as `"ab"`, an empty list read as `{}` (the
  pending entries settled, None returned) and a list of pairs read as
  the dict it spells. Both are outside the reference's signature; no
  caller passes one.

Reference findings, reproduced by the port:

- An entry with no `kind` key (one the module counts as a restore's),
  or whose `kind` is not `store_restored`, or that holds an
  `engine_version`, is never found by `_logged`: the payload its row
  carries has `kind` `store_restored` and the appending build's
  `engine_version`. Such an entry's row, once on the log but not named in
  the record (the record could not be written), is appended again at the
  next open (`no_kind_appended_twice`: a second `store_restored` row
  with the same payload).
- Entries that share `kind`, `store_id` and `restored_at` by Python's
  `==` are one place in the record: `_fill` names the last of them. Two
  entries whose times are `true` and `1` get each other's rows named
  (`true_and_one`); two equal entries get one row, named in both
  (`twins_appended`).
- `_fill` writes the record with `indent=2`, so a value nested `n` deep
  takes about `n²` bytes: two values 600 deep make a record of
  1,457,513 bytes, past the 1 MiB cap, so the second entry's row is
  appended and returned but named nowhere, and every later read logs
  ValueError (`restore_rows_robustness`).

Pinned by `restore_rows.jsonl` (57 cases, 78 steps) and
`restore_rows_python.jsonl` (2 cases, 4 steps), made by
`tests/contract/gen_restore_rows.py`: the store `Store.create` makes
under `store_create.json`'s values, opened as the owner, then the case's
log rows inserted on the connection (raw rows: kinds, stamps and MACs of
the case's choosing, a blob among them) and its record written as
`backup._append_record` writes one, or as a hostile file. The record is
written after the open, so the open's own `settle` finds none (that
call is pinned by `store_open_restore.jsonl`). Each step calls `settle`,
`append_missing` or `append_for` under fixed clocks and an optional hook
(`PRAGMA query_only`; a second connection holding the write lock with a
100 ms busy timeout; the keys directory 0500, skipped as root), and
records the answer or the class raised, the warnings, the rows appended,
the record's text after, the head's text, whether the connection is left
in a transaction and the clocks read. Cases: no record; a record not
JSON, over and at the cap, a directory, UTF-16 that does not decode, an
integer past 4,300 digits, not a dict, `restores` not a list, in UTF-16
and behind a UTF-8 BOM; entries of the other kind, another or no store
id, a row set, no `row` key, a string, a bogus kind; `head_after`
missing, absent from the log, with another MAC, with a bool seq, with a
blob MAC; a replaced head on the log and one not on it; each branch of
`_clock_reading`; unreadable times; a record row past the head, said,
kept, decided again silently and then for a new reason; control rows
only; the row already on the log (as text and as a blob), payloads that
do not read; withholdings that stand, are gone, or have another shape;
the record or its lock not writable; `query_only`; `append_for` with its
entry missing, in the record, after an earlier one, as 1.0 against 1,
and NaN; `append_missing` with entries given; true against 1; twins;
a busy store; a seq past 64 bits; odd values said; a blob kind; the
first row past the head stamped at the restore's very time; a withheld
entry the record does not hold; an early first row that is the entry's
own logged row; `append_for` of an entry sharing a pending one's place
but not its bundle; a `head_before` behind the bundle's head at seq 0
under the clock's words. The
Python-gated sibling holds a record and a log payload nested 100,000
deep (RecursionError out of `append_missing`, logged by `settle`), which
follows the interpreter and the system. Gates: Unicode (the created
store's tokenizer) and POSIX only (modes, a `flock`), as
`store_open_upkeep.jsonl`'s; the sibling is Python-gated too.

Tests: `golden_restore_rows` (every step of both files, through
`tests/restore_rows/mod.rs`), `restore_rows_kills` (the clock asked where
a replaced head decides, MACs compared as bytes, Rust's `==` for
Python's, the decision skipped inside the lock, a control row counted as
a record, the reason said twice, the record written without its lock),
`restore_rows_robustness` (two settles at once on two connections append
one row and fill the record once; 400 restores at the cap settle in
linear time; nesting 100,000 deep raises without a panic, 9,000 deep is
compared without one; 600 deep makes a record past the cap that later
reads decline; seqs at and past SQLite's bounds; a record at 0644
rewritten 0600, as `atomic_write_bytes(mode_before_rename=0o600)` leaves
it on macOS and Linux; the connection out of any transaction after
every path). POSIX only as the fixtures, with `restore_rows_not_posix.rs`
recording the gap (class os). `restore_rows_cause` runs on every target:
`RestoreError::cause` for each class `settle`'s four bases catch (the
Windows lock's TimeoutError among them, logged as the reference logs
it), and None for those it lets raise. No path
is resolved here, so `fsdata`'s Windows flavour (ENG-124) does not
touch it; on Windows `flock_excl` is `_flock_windows`, compiled and not
run. No regular expression is used.

## Windows fixes to the settings write and the restore lock (winfix3)

A fix unit; it ports nothing. Its Windows behaviour is not run locally:
CI's native parity jobs on windows-latest are its test.

- The default configuration text. `config/default_config.toml` is embedded
  with `include_str!`, which keeps the bytes as they are on disk. Without a
  `-text` rule, a Windows checkout rewrote its line ends to CRLF, and the
  build there would write a first-run config file 218 bytes longer than the
  reference's. `.gitattributes` now marks the file `-text`.
  `tests/test_native_embedded_files.py` finds every literal `include_str!`
  and `include_bytes!` path under `native/crates`, resolved against the
  including file, and asserts with `git check-attr text` that each is
  unset; the two reference JSON copies already pass. A unit test in
  `config/create.rs` asserts the embedded text holds no carriage return,
  for a checkout made before the rule.
- `an_open_record_file_is_not_removed` asserted `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied`.
  A file opened without FILE_SHARE_DELETE refuses deletion with
  ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION (32), which std maps to no named kind; the test
  now asserts raw error 32 and keeps its other assertions.
- `restore_lock_hold_kills::a_shorter_mark_replaces_a_longer_one_whole`
  asserted the marker held no `x` at all, but the marker names the store
  path, and a checkout path holding an `x` failed it on every platform. It
  now looks for the old bundle's run (`xx`).

Windows paths of `restore_lock.rs` and `bettermemory-sys` judged for the
same fault (an ErrorKind expected where Windows gives raw error 5, 32 or 33):

| Path | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `try_lock` (Windows): `lock_byte` at `WINDOWS_LOCK_OFFSET` | sound: any error is Held, no kind read (a held byte gives 33) |
| `unlock_file` (Windows): `unlock_byte` | sound: errors ignored |
| `record_options` share mode | sound: no error inspected |
| `record_running`, `store_handle`, `windows_reading` | sound: a failed open is `None`, any kind |
| `read_marker`, `open_record` | sound: any open error is no marker |
| `open_lock_file` NotFound when not creating | sound: a missing file is ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (2), mapped to NotFound |
| `behind_handle`, `record_admission`, `Admission::confirm` | sound: no error kind read |
| `RestoreLock` release's `remove_file` | sound: result ignored |
| `os_error_text` | sound: formats the raw code on every platform |
| `bettermemory_sys::file_index`, `lock_byte`, `unlock_byte` | sound: return `last_os_error` unchanged |
| test `an_unlock_frees_the_lock_while_the_handle_stays_open` | sound: compares `Try` values only |
| test `an_open_record_file_is_not_removed` | fixed (above) |

## The hook's store refusals (`_store_refusal.py`)

The module a hook loads to refuse a store before it starts a daemon,
ported whole as `store_refusal.rs` (about 600 lines with its comments).
The reference keeps it apart from `backup` and `restore_lock` for the
hook's import cost and reads the same files its own way, so it is its own
port: it reads only `restore_lock::LOCK_SUFFIX` from the crate's restore
lock and calls nothing of it.

| Function | Reference lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| constants | 29-42 | none | built |
| `printable` | 45-53 | none | `crate::printable::printable` |
| `_may_be_bundle_manifest` | 56-70 | an open with O_NONBLOCK, `fstat`, a read | built (`may_be_bundle_manifest`) |
| `bundle_refusal` | 73-108 | `realpath`, `stat` following links, the link count | built |
| `_restore_marker`, `_restore_marker_at` | 111-136 | an open and one read | built |
| `_record_lock_held` | 139-163 | `flock` (POSIX), `msvcrt.locking` (Windows) | built |
| `restore_state` | 166-204 | the directory's `flock`, the record file | built, and its record branch alone (`restore_state_record_branch`) |
| `_describe_restore` | 207-222 | none | built (`describe_restore`) |
| `restore_refusal`, `store_refusal` | 225-258 | as above | built |

What each reproduces, and the decisions:

- Paths are spelled as `pathlib` spells them, worked on as text: on POSIX
  each byte of the path is one character, so a byte that is no UTF-8
  survives and `str(path)` shows the lone surrogate `os.fsdecode` gives it.
  `Path.name`, `Path.parent`, `parent / name` and `with_name` are textual
  over `config::pure_path`, so a store named `..` keeps its name (std's
  `file_name` has none) and `with_name` on a path with no name (`/`, `.`)
  is the reference's ValueError, out of `restore_state`, `restore_refusal`
  and `store_refusal`.
- `Path.resolve()` (strict=False) is Python 3.13's `posixpath.realpath`
  step for step: each component `lstat`ed, each link read and its target
  pushed, every error of a step leaving the component as spelled, a link
  met again before it resolved (a loop) left as reached, `..` taken off
  the resolved text. `os.getcwd` failing drops the second candidate. The
  golden files hold no loop row: how `resolve` answers a loop changed
  between releases (RuntimeError before 3.13). Under the Windows flavour
  `ntpath.realpath` is not ported (ENG-124): `bundle_refusal` answers from
  the spelled candidate when it finds a manifest and otherwise declines
  (`Failure::NotPorted`), as `store_refusal` then does.
- `manifest.is_file()` follows links and is false on any error. The
  manifest is opened with O_NONBLOCK (the C library's value on each
  target, `bettermemory_sys::O_NONBLOCK`) so a FIFO swapped in does not
  block; not a regular file, or past 1 MiB by `fstat`, it counts; at most
  1 MiB is read and given to `json::loads_bytes`. Any error counts; a
  document counts only when it is an object whose last `format` key is
  `"bettermemory.backup"`. A document that is not an object does not
  count, as the code says and against the docstring.
- `json::loads_bytes` (new in `json.rs`) is `json.loads` of bytes:
  `json.detect_encoding` and a `surrogatepass` decode
  (`store::provenance::decode_json_bytes`), a decode failure a ValueError
  (`LoadError::Decode`), then `loads_detailed`.
- The hard-link test is `stat().st_nlink > 1` following links, false on
  any error; a directory as the store has more than one link on POSIX.
  On Windows the count is `nNumberOfLinks` of the opened file
  (`bettermemory_sys::file_links`), as `os.stat` fills `st_nlink` there.
- `restore_state` on POSIX opens the store's directory with O_DIRECTORY
  (`bettermemory_sys::O_DIRECTORY`: 0o200000 on most Linux targets,
  0o40000 on arm and aarch64 Linux, the BSDs' own values elsewhere) and tries a shared `flock` once (`File::try_lock_shared`): taken, it is
  let go and the record read read-only; held (WouldBlock, or EINTR), the
  state is running with the record; any other error leaves the directory
  and takes the record branch. The record branch opens the record file
  read-write (an error is clear), tries its lock (held only for
  WouldBlock or EINTR), then reads the marker from the same handle. A
  marker is one read of at most 64 KiB; `bytes.strip()` whitespace alone
  is none; JSON that is an object is the record, anything else an empty
  record; a read error is `{"unreadable": str(exc)}`; RecursionError
  passes out.
- Windows: the record branch alone, its lock the reference's one byte at
  1 MiB taken with `msvcrt.locking`; std locks the whole file, which
  overlaps that byte, so the port takes `try_lock` and lets go at once, as
  `store::restore_lock`'s Windows reader does, and any error is held. The
  record file is opened with the CRT's share mode. A path that is no
  Unicode text (a lone UTF-16 surrogate, which `str(Path)` keeps) is
  declined by every function. Untested here.
- `restore_refusal` and `_describe_restore` spell the text with
  `printable` around the description and the again-command; the paths are
  not passed through it, as in the reference.

No regular expression is used.

Fixtures: `gen_store_refusal.py` writes `store_refusal.jsonl` (every
platform: manifests of each shape and encoding, the cap on either side as
a sparse file and as text, records of each shape, each read through the
directory lock and through the record branch) and
`store_refusal_posix.jsonl` (POSIX_ONLY: a restore holding the directory
or the record file, the record branch with its lock held, an unreadable
record, a FIFO and links as the manifest, hard links, a store reached
through a symbolic link file or directory, a directory as the store, `..`
past a missing directory). Paths are `@` for the case directory; an
unreadable record pins its key and the refusal, not the C library's text.
`golden_store_refusal.rs` and `golden_store_refusal_posix.rs` build each
case and compare (on Windows the rows `bundle_refusal` declines are
recorded as a gap, class os); `store_refusal_not_posix.rs` records the
POSIX file's gap elsewhere. `store_refusal_kills.rs` also holds a relative
store (parent `.`) and `/..` (`..` at the root stays at `/`); a `flock`
error other than WouldBlock or EINTR on the record file (ENOLCK on a
mount without a lock daemon) needs a filesystem the suite does not have
and is untested.

Left for later: the hook client (`_daemon_client.hook_main`) that calls
`store_refusal`; `backup.bundle_refusal` itself (`backup.py`'s units).

## The additive schema steps (`store_schema.py`, unit store_schema-1)

`store::schema` holds the schema steps a writing open runs on a store an
earlier build made, and four leaves of `store_schema.py`. Read from
`src/bettermemory/store_schema.py` at the unit's base (lines as there).
Nothing is wired into `open_for_writing` or `run_steps` yet: `store::open`
still refuses a store a step would change (`NotPorted::MembershipStep`),
and now reads its `wanted` list through `schema::wanted`, the one copy of
it.

| function | reference | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wanted` | `_add_membership_tables` 1227-1251 | `sqlite_master` (rows given) | built |
| `add_membership_tables` | 1214-1291, `_MEMBERSHIP_*` and `_ADDITIVE_*` 1204-1211 | the connection, the `create::Provider`'s membership id | built |
| `add_returned_marks`, `RETURNED_BACKFILL_KEY` | 1300-1329 | the connection | built |
| `add_proposals_index` | 1332-1371 | the connection | built |
| `add_session_index` | 1374-1411 | the connection | built |
| `add_path_targets` | 1414-1423 | nothing (no column) | built |
| `absent_text` | 1059-1067 | nothing | built |
| `orphan_names` | 1135-1150 | the host's path flavour (a parameter, `IS_WINDOWS` for the host) | built |
| `refuse_unmigrated_v8` | 1169-1179 | `Fs::stat`, `Fs::listdir` | built for POSIX (`#[cfg(unix)]`) |
| `holds_v8_files`, `is_v8_name` | 1183-1201 | `Fs::listdir` | built |

What each reproduces:

- `wanted`: the membership and additive objects `sqlite_master` lacks, by
  exact name, sorted; `the store id` when meta's value is missing or empty
  (a falsy `meta.get`); `checkouts.unresolved_json` when the table's text
  does not hold the word (`\b` search, case-sensitive). The only optional
  column of `_MEMBERSHIP_SPECS` is that one (`OPTIONAL`). An empty list
  returns before the id is drawn, so the provider is asked only when
  something is wanted.
- `add_membership_tables`: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, every statement of the two
  schema texts (split on `;` as the reference splits them), `ALTER TABLE
  ... ADD COLUMN ... TEXT` for each optional column `PRAGMA table_info`
  lacks, `INSERT OR IGNORE` of the id, `COMMIT`; a rollback when any fails
  inside the transaction. The ALTER set comes from `PRAGMA` and `wanted`
  from the word search, and the two disagree: a column named only in a
  comment is never added, and a column named in another case
  (`Unresolved_JSON`) makes `wanted` name it and the ALTER fail with
  `duplicate column name` (an OperationalError the step raises). Meta's
  dict gains the id the table holds after (`str()` of it: an integer
  value reads `7`), not necessarily the minted one.
- The read-only store: an OperationalError whose text, spaces removed and
  lowercased, holds `readonly` is the warning `store <path> is read-only;
  not added: <wanted>` (or `; no backfill marked`), returned as a value
  in the order the reference logs it. `add_returned_marks` and
  `add_proposals_index` return their warnings beside the outcome, so a
  warning the membership step gave stays when the statement after it
  raises (the reference has logged it by then). Any other sqlite error is
  `StepError::Sqlite` with the class `_pysqlite_seterror` gives its
  primary code and SQLite's message alone (rusqlite's `SqlInputError`
  appends the statement and an offset, which the reference's text lacks).
- `add_returned_marks`: the membership step, then `INSERT OR IGNORE` of
  `returned_backfill = pending`; meta's dict reads `pending` after it even
  when the table keeps an earlier value (`done`), as the reference sets
  it unconditionally.
- The two index steps compare names lowercased (an index named in
  capitals counts as there) where the membership step compares them
  exactly (`LOG_CORROBORATIONS` leaves `log_corroborations` wanted; its
  `IF NOT EXISTS` statement is then a no-op, as SQLite's names are
  case-insensitive, and only the id is written).
- `absent_text(kind, args)`: `str(args[0])` for one argument, `str` of the
  tuple otherwise; `NotFound` adds `no record ... in the store`.
- `orphan_names(value, windows)`: `json.loads` (ValueError and
  RecursionError give none), a list's non-empty strings whose
  `Path(name).name` is the name: no `/` and not `.`, and under Windows no
  backslash and no drive (any character then a colon).
- `holds_v8_files`: a listing that fails holds none; `.events.jsonl`,
  `.tombstones`, `.events.*.jsonl`, or a memory file.
- `refuse_unmigrated_v8(fs, path)`: the file test and the parent read
  the path as `PurePosixPath` spells it (`config::pure_path`, so
  `a//memory.sqlite` names `a`, and `a/memory.sqlite/` or
  `a/memory.sqlite/.` is tested as `a/memory.sqlite`); no refusal when a
  regular file is there, the parent is not a folder, or it holds no v8
  file. Not built for Windows, where the reference's `WindowsPath` takes
  a drive and backslashes; `store_schema_not_posix` records the gap.

The pattern `_V8_MEMORY_NAME` (`.*-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}\.md$` under
`match`) is matched by hand under rule 3 of the pattern decision
(`store_schema-1` is named there; `pyre` has no `api` module yet). The
reference tests `name.endswith(".md")` first, so the pattern reduces to a
dash at 30 from the end, 26 upper-case Crockford characters and `.md`;
`$` before a final newline cannot arise. A newline before the dash does:
`.*` does not cross it, so `a\nb-<ULID>.md` is no memory file
(`store_schema_steps.jsonl` pins it, and the seeded sweep mixes newlines in).
The pattern is in the engine's inventory already: `gen_pyre_atom` scans
every literal the reference passes to `re`. It gains the engine
cross-check when pyre-6 lands.

Fixtures (`gen_store_schema`): `store_schema_steps.jsonl` (ungated) runs each
step on in-memory stores made from the five schema texts and changed by
the row's SQL (each object dropped, the id missing, empty or an integer,
`checkouts` without the column, bare, with the column only in a comment or
in capitals, indexes in capitals, the backfill done, no meta table, a
trigger whose error spells `read only` with a space, a meta dict without
the id), recording whether the id was drawn, the warnings,
the error, meta, and what `sqlite_master` lacks or holds beyond the full
schema; `orphan_names` under both flavours (the reference's `Path`
replaced by `PurePosixPath` and `PureWindowsPath`), `holds_v8_files` over
names and 4,000 seeded names by digest, and `absent_text`.
`store_schema_posix.jsonl` (POSIX only) runs the steps on a mode-0444
store file (among them no meta table, no proposals table and the indexes
in capitals) and `refuse_unmigrated_v8` over real folders (a trailing `/`
and `/.` among them), the scratch root spelled `<T>`. Its generator
refuses to run as root, and its test asserts that the mode-0444 file
cannot be opened for writing.
Tests: `golden_store_schema`, `golden_store_schema_posix` (with
`store_schema_not_posix` recording the gap off POSIX), `store_schema_kills`,
`store_schema_robustness` (deep and wide orphan values, megabyte names,
growth claims through `timing`).

Left for later units: wiring the steps into the writing open and
`run_steps` (`store_steps.py`), the log's warning itself (no `log.py`
dependency here), and the engine cross-check of `_V8_MEMORY_NAME`.

## The episode journal's reads and the upgrade's proof (`store_journal.py`, `store_upgrade.py`)

`store::journal` reproduces the read half of `store_journal.py` over a
`rusqlite::Connection`, and `store::upgrade` the proof of
`store_upgrade.py` that no other connection holds a store open. Lines as
in `src/bettermemory` at the unit's base.

| function | reference | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_episode` | `store_journal.py` 62-68 | the connection | built |
| `iter_episodes` | 71-80 (both branches; the list, not the generator) | the connection | built |
| `count_episodes` | 83-84 | the connection | built |
| `episodes_by_session`, `sort_by_created` | 149-152 | the connection | built |
| `episodes_by_swarm` | 155-163 | the connection | built |
| `episode_session_ids` | 166-174 | the connection | built |
| `prunable_episode_sessions`, `cutoff` | 177-194 | the connection, the clock (`now`, `None` reads it) | built |
| `episode_volume`, `EpisodeVolume`, `DEFAULT_EPISODE_TTL_DAYS` | 248-268, `store_schema.py` 539-562 | the connection, the clock as above | built |
| `TRANSACTION_WRITER_REVISION` | `store_upgrade.py` 23 | nothing | built |
| `prove_exclusive`, `sqlite_class`, `refusal` | 26-47 | the connection (SQLite's file locks) | built |
| `prune_episode_sessions` | `store_journal.py` 197-245 | a writing store | left for a later unit |
| `quiescent` | `store_upgrade.py` 51-67 | `restore_lock.held_here`, `acquire` | left for unit store_steps-2 |

What each reproduces:

- The statements are the reference's text. `records::stored` spells the
  episode select without an order once (`episode_select_prefix!`), and
  `EPISODE_SELECT` is that prefix with ` ORDER BY episodes.rowid`, byte
  for byte as before; each read appends what the reference appends
  (` WHERE id = ?` with no order, ` ORDER BY rowid`,
  ` WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY rowid`,
  ` WHERE swarm_id = ? ORDER BY created, rowid`), so SQLite gives the
  reference's order. Rows are read by `select_rows_with` (the loop
  `select_rows` now calls) and `records::rows::episode`.
- `episodes_by_session` sorts stably as `list.sort(key=created)` does:
  aware values by their UTC instant, so equal instants in different
  offsets keep rowid order; naive values by their fields; a naive and an
  aware value among two or more raise `TypeError`
  (`JournalError::NaiveAware`). `_dt` makes every stored value aware,
  so no row reaches that branch. `episodes_by_swarm` orders by the
  `created` text, so the same rows can come in another order there.
- `prunable_episode_sessions` answers none for a TTL of zero or less
  without reading the clock; else the cutoff is
  `(now - timedelta(days=ttl)).isoformat()` in `now`'s own offset (or
  naive), `OverflowError` past `timedelta`'s 999,999,999 days or out of
  the years 1 to 9999, and `HAVING newest < ?` compares TEXT: a cutoff
  spelled in another offset can take a session whose newest instant is
  not before it.
- `get_episode` raises `NotFoundError(episode_id)` (`JournalError::NotFound`;
  `absent()` is its `absent_text`). A row the model refuses raises what
  `_row_to_episode` raises (`JournalError::Record`). `iter_episodes`
  answers the list: where the reference's generator yields the rows
  before a bad one and then raises, the port answers the raise.
- A session id column that is neither text nor an integer (a blob) is
  declined as `JournalError::NotPorted` (class `NotPorted`); the
  reference answers `str(bytes)`.
  The schema's `TEXT NOT NULL` column holds such a value only if written
  by hand.
- `prove_exclusive` reads the busy timeout and locking mode, then sets
  no wait and the exclusive mode and runs `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` and
  `ROLLBACK`, each statement stepped once as `sqlite3` steps it. An
  error `_sqlite3` classes as `OperationalError` becomes the
  `StoreVersionError` refusal (`quoted(str(Path(path)))` with the
  host's path flavour, so `a//b/` shows as `a/b` and an empty name as
  `.`; key and needed `None`);
  any other propagates with its class (`UpgradeError::Sqlite`).
  `sqlite_class` is `_pysqlite_seterror`'s table by primary result
  code: `ERROR`, `PERM`, `ABORT`, `BUSY`, `LOCKED`, `READONLY`,
  `INTERRUPT`, `IOERR`, `FULL`, `CANTOPEN`, `PROTOCOL`, `EMPTY`,
  `SCHEMA` are `OperationalError`; `CONSTRAINT` and `MISMATCH`
  `IntegrityError`; `MISUSE` and `RANGE` `InterfaceError`; `TOOBIG`
  `DataError`; `INTERNAL` and `NOTFOUND` `InternalError`; `NOMEM`
  `MemoryError`; every other code (`CORRUPT`, `NOTADB`, `NOLFS`,
  `AUTH`, `FORMAT`) `DatabaseError`. The clean-up runs on both paths
  in the reference's order (a transaction still open rolled back, the
  mode put back, `schema_version` read, the timeout put back), and an
  error there replaces the pending outcome. On a connection already in
  a transaction the proof refuses and rolls the caller's transaction
  back.

Reference findings, reproduced:

- A second connection holding `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` on a rollback-journal
  store: the proof's `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` fails (the refusal pending), the
  locking mode returns to normal, and the `schema_version` read in the
  `finally` fails with `database is locked` because the busy timeout is
  still 0. That `OperationalError` replaces the refusal, and the
  caller's busy timeout is left at 0 (`store_upgrade_posix.jsonl`, case
  `delete_exclusive`).
- `prune_episode_sessions`' cutoff and `prunable_episode_sessions` order
  by `created` text, not by instant (above).

Fixtures: `gen_store_journal.py` writes `store_journal.jsonl` (gated on
pydantic-core: the episodes are read through the model) from an
in-memory store holding `store_schema.SCHEMA`; `gen_store_upgrade.py`
writes `store_upgrade.jsonl` (a connection alone on its store, both
journal modes, the exclusive mode, its own transaction open, a name
that needs quoting) and `store_upgrade_posix.jsonl` (POSIX only: a
second connection open, reading, reserved or exclusive, in both journal
modes; its file locks were seen on POSIX only).
`store_upgrade_not_posix.rs` records that gap. No pattern of the
reference is matched here (no regular expression). Tests:
`golden_store_journal`, `golden_store_upgrade`,
`golden_store_upgrade_posix`, `store_journal_kills`,
`store_journal_robustness`.

and `admitted`, and the helpers that compare and rebase recorded paths.
Several of its parts are already ported where other units read them.

| `Machine`, `View`, `Checkout` and its methods, `_live_key`, `Project`, `ProjectFile` | 540-679 | nothing (`checkout_token.Lineage`, ported) | built (units 2 and 3) |
| `Home`, `Proposal`, `Declaration`, `Resolution`, `Declared`, `Why`, `UnresolvedProject`, `Health`, `EpisodeRef`, `Handoff`, `RecallAdmission` | 682-888 | nothing | `Home` and `Resolution` in `store::caller`; `Proposal` built (units 2 and 3); the rest built (unit 4) |
| `_strings`, `_flag`, `PortableIdentity` (`to_json`, `from_json`, `digest`), `ImportedProject` | 890-997 | nothing | built (unit 4) |

| `_found_token` | 1152-1156 | nothing | built (units 2 and 3) |

The whole module is past 600 lines of Rust, so it is cut, leaves first:
unit 1 the path helpers and the legacy rule; unit 2 the manifest and the
portable identity (JSON in and out, the digest); unit 3 the stamps, the
reader protocols, the machine, view, checkout and project records with
`_found_token`; unit 4 the remaining frozen records.

### Unit 1, built (`membership_records`, `membership_records::paths`)

- `legacy_asks(rule, same_name, compatible)`: `rule` compared as text,
  only `ambiguous` and `none` read.
- `_same_number`: device and inode compared as text, the birth time
  aside, a missing key never the same.
- `_same_path` and `_basename`: `capture::paths`' `norm` and `basename`.
- `_flavour`: `_DRIVE_PATH` (`^[A-Za-z]:`) is matched by hand: one ASCII
  letter at index 0 and a colon at index 1. `re.match` with `^` and no
  flags reads exactly that; a non-ASCII letter and a digit do not match.
  No regex crate is used.
- `_path_under`, `_rebase`: `os.path.join` of any number of parts,
  `relpath` and `normpath` in the spelling's flavour.
- `_common_by_pointer(os_path, kind, git_dir)`, `_dir_key(dir_paths,
  path)`, `_dir_below(dir_paths, here, root)`: the host's `os.path` (and
  `_DIR_PATHS`, which a caller may swap) is an argument, a `Flavour`.

`gitfile_rule::hostpath` gained `text`, the same two flavours over a
Python `str` (code points): `sep`, `isabs`, `join` of any number of
parts, `normpath`, `normcase`, `split`, `dirname`, `basename`, `abspath`
and `relpath` as CPython 3.13.13 has them. The byte half and the text
half share `splitroot`, `nt_isabs`, `nt_join` and one generic
`posix_normpath`. `ntpath.join` compares two drives by `str.lower`, now
the crate's `unicode::lower` (final sigma included) where the byte half
used `char::to_lowercase`; the two differ on no drive the byte half's
golden files hold.

Decisions:

- `abspath` asks the process for `os.getcwd()` and, where `ntpath` runs
  on Windows, `nt._getfullpathname`, through the trait
  `hostpath::text::Process`; the defaults answer as off Windows. The
  working directory is asked only where a path is relative, once per
  path, as the reference asks it; its OSError is returned
  (`Raised::Os`). `relpath`'s ValueErrors (`no path specified`, two
  drives) are `Raised::Value` with the reference's text, `repr` of each
  drive by `pyvalue::repr_str`.
- `ntpath.normcase` is the one CPython has off Windows (`/` to `\`, then
  `str.lower`). On Windows it calls `LCMapStringEx`, which is not ported:
  `_dir_key` with the host's `ntpath` on Windows is left for the unit
  that wires the host in.
- That is a known difference of the Windows build, not fixed here. This
  build's `ntpath.normcase` answers as CPython does on a POSIX host. On
  a Windows host CPython asks the OS, and this build does not, so on
  Windows a folder key (`_dir_key` under `ntpath`) of a name holding
  U+0130 (LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE) differs from the
  reference's there: the reference keeps U+0130 where this build writes
  `i` and U+0307 (seen on the Windows runner). A capital sigma at the
  end of a word (after a cased letter and before none) is reachable in
  the `ntpath` digests: `str.lower` writes final sigma U+03C2 there,
  and `LCMapStringEx`, which lowers each letter alone, is expected to
  write U+03C3; no Windows run has shown that row alone. Equally,
  `_rebase` from a root read with `ntpath` makes paths absolute on a
  Windows host through `_getfullpathname`, which reads the process's own
  drive and folder, where this build asks `os.getcwd()` as off Windows.
- `commonpath`, named in the plan, is read by no function of this unit
  and is not added.

Reference findings (reproduced, pinned):

- `_rebase` reads a path a separator alone begins, written with a
  backslash, by the running Python's `ntpath`: 3.11 and 3.12 take `\v`
  as absolute and 3.13 does not, so `_rebase("/C:b", "a\\x", ".t.")`
  answers `.t./C:b` under 3.11 and 3.12 and `../../../C:b` under 3.13
  (both against working directory `/w/cwd`). The answer of a recorded
  path depends on the release.
- `_dir_below(here, "")` is true for every `here` that starts with the
  separator: an empty root key stands for the root.
- `_same_path("/a\\", "/a")` is false: a POSIX spelling trims `/` only.

Fixtures: `gen_membership_records.py` writes
`membership_records_paths.jsonl` (not gated: 308 cases, each the same
under 3.11.15, 3.12.13 and 3.13.13 as checked by running the generator
under each and on every host, and a digest of 4,000 seeded path triples
drawn without a backslash or a drive, every function asked of each),
`membership_records_paths_python.jsonl` (gated on the Python release: the
69 cases `_release_bound` picks by input, an `ntpath` path a single
separator or a separator and a colon begins, or holding `\\?\` or `\\.\`)
and `membership_records_paths_platform.jsonl` (gated on the platform and
the Python release: the 16 cases `_host_bound` picks by input, `_dir_key`
under `ntpath` of a path past ASCII and `_rebase` from a root read with
`ntpath`, whose reference answer follows the host as above, and the two
`ntpath` digests: one of 4,000 triples drawn from every piece, `_rebase` left out and a triple
redrawn while `_release_bound` picks any other case asked of it or
`_path_under` would join through `ntpath` a path two separators begin
that names no server and share, `_short_unc`: 3.11's `ntpath.splitdrive`
reads no drive there, or a drive ending in a separator after which its
`join` writes another, where 3.12's `splitroot` reads a UNC drive and
`join` writes none, and one of 4,000 triples drawn from every piece
with `_rebase` and those joins, which is release-bound too). The rows
moved there unchanged from the other two files. The sweep's
generator is a 64-bit LCG with Knuth's MMIX constants, run alike in the
test.

Tests: `golden_membership_records` (the three files, every case
counted; on a set made on a Windows host a differing `_dir_key`,
`_rebase` or digest row of the platform file is named and counted as
set aside, class os, and any other difference fails),
`membership_records_kills` (12: among them `ntpath.abspath` and
