  `str()` of an OSError with a winerror does, with the system text's
  trailing spaces and dots removed as `PyErr_SetExcFromWindowsErr` removes
  them (`winerror_text`); no fixture holds one.
- `mkdir` recurses once per missing level, as `Path.mkdir` does; CPython
  stops at about 1,000 levels with RecursionError, which POSIX's PATH_MAX
  never reaches. On Windows a long path can, and the port then recurses on.
- The write takes no lock, as the reference's does not.
- An error of the write itself names the destination here; the
  reference's names its random temporary file (`tempfile`'s
  `NamedTemporaryFile`), which no row holds.
- The path is text already spelled as `str(Path(...))` spells it: an
  empty text, which `Path` reads as `.`, is not an input, nor is
  `config.toml/`, `./x` or `a//b`. A debug build asserts it on POSIX
  (`create::is_posix_spelled`).

Fixtures (`gen_config.generate_create` and `generate_create_posix`):
`settings_create.jsonl` (ungated) holds `DEFAULT_CONFIG`'s length and
sha256 and the write over a missing file, a missing parent chain, a
parent that is there, and a file that is there (unchanged, read: a
setting, an empty file, a malformed one whose `tomllib` text is left out
because it follows the release). The reference runs each with a relative
path in its scratch directory and records the notice and messages with
`/` between parts, so the bytes are the same on Windows.
`settings_create_posix.jsonl` (POSIX only; `settings_create_posix_not_posix.rs`
records the gap elsewhere) holds the mode of a new file and of one in new
parents, a directory at the path (IsADirectoryError from the read), a
file parent and grandparent, and a parent of mode 0o600 (the class only).
The Rust tests run each row with an absolute path and compare after
taking the scratch prefix off. `settings_create_kills` checks the order
of the effects, that a file there is never written, that an `exists`
error writes nothing, that a failed write makes no notice and that a file
gone after the write is FileNotFoundError; `settings_create_robustness`
gives a NUL, a 100,000-byte name, the root, a 100-level chain and a file
of 100,000 lines (linear by the wall clock).

No regular expression is involved.

Left for later units: `default_config_path` (the caller passes the path),
`report::SystemFs` for use beyond the tests, the registry, the renderings.

## Body diffs and `str.splitlines` (`difflib`)

`history._body_diff` (`history.py` 534-543) is the only caller of
`difflib` the native build needs: `unified_diff` over the two bodies'
`splitlines()`, with `fromfile` and `tofile` the version names,
`lineterm=""` and no dates, the lines joined with a newline. The module
`difflib` reproduces that path of CPython 3.13.13's `Lib/difflib.py`,
built whole in one unit (335 lines of source with its comments). The `difflib` of
`config` (`config::difflib`, `get_close_matches` only) is a separate
port over characters and is left as it is.

| function | reference | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body_diff` | `history._body_diff` 534-543 | nothing | built |
| `splitlines` | `str.splitlines()` (no `keepends`) | nothing | built |
| `SequenceMatcher::new` | `SequenceMatcher(None, a, b)`: `set_seqs`, `__chain_b` | nothing | built |
| `find_longest_match` | `find_longest_match` | nothing | built |
| `get_matching_blocks` | `get_matching_blocks` | nothing | built |
| `get_opcodes` | `get_opcodes` | nothing | built |
| `get_grouped_opcodes` | `get_grouped_opcodes(n)` | nothing | built |
| `format_range_unified` | `_format_range_unified` | nothing | built |
| `unified_diff`, `unified_diff_lines` | `unified_diff(..., lineterm="")`, and its lines joined | nothing | built |

What each reproduces, and the decisions:

- The matcher is generic over `Eq + Hash` elements; the diff's lines are
  `PyStr`, so a lone surrogate is a line's code point like any other.
- Autojunk: when `b` holds 200 lines or more, a line occurring more than
  `len(b) // 100 + 1` times is popular and dropped from `b2j`. With no
  junk function the junk set is empty, so `find_longest_match`'s second
  pair of extension loops (over junk) never moves and is not written; its
  first pair extends over popular lines, as the reference does, also from
  a match of size 0 (a block can start on a popular line).
- Ties go to the earliest `i`, then the earliest `j`: the `j2len` maps
  roll per `i` as the reference's dicts do, and a longer match replaces
  the best only when strictly longer.
- `get_matching_blocks` keeps the reference's explicit queue (a stack,
  popped from the end), so no input recurses; the blocks are sorted and
  adjacent ones merged, then the sentinel `(len(a), len(b), 0)`.
- `get_grouped_opcodes(3)`: with no opcodes (both sides empty) the one
  `equal (0, 1, 0, 1)` stands in and, being a lone equal group, is not
  yielded, so `unified_diff` writes nothing at all, no header either. The
  first and last equal runs are trimmed to the context, and an equal run
  longer than twice the context splits the groups.
- The header is `--- old` and `+++ new` with no tab and no date; a range
  of one line is its number alone, an empty one `start,0` with the line
  before it.
- `splitlines` ends a line at `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` (one end),
  `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x1c`, `\x1d`, `\x1e`, `\x85`, `\u2028` and
  `\u2029`; a final end makes no empty last line.
- Cost: the reference is quadratic in the worst case
  (`find_longest_match` walks every `j` of a line for each `i`, once per
  block); the port grows the same way. `difflib_robustness` pins that
  twice the lines cost under 4.5 times the time for identical, disjoint
  and interleaved sequences.

No regular expression is involved. The golden file `difflib.jsonl`
(`tests/contract/gen_difflib.py`) holds every text as a list of code
points; it pins the hand pairs (empty, equal, one-line edits, every
`splitlines` boundary and some that are not, CRLF, a trailing newline,
lone surrogates, the context and group bounds), `unified_diff` over line
lists (an autojunk case written out) and seeded random sweeps as digests:
199, 200 and 201 lines with a line at `n // 100 + 1` and `n // 100 + 2`
places, and 3,000 small pairs over four lines. The file is not gated:
`difflib`, `SequenceMatcher` and `str.splitlines` answer its rows alike
under Python 3.11 to 3.14 on every system, so every Python CI job
compares it. The Rust test reads the committed file on every host.

Left for later units: `history.py`'s unit 3 (`_changed`, `_event_detail`)
calls `body_diff`.

## The refusals and the bundle of the tool handlers (`_handlers.py`, unit handlers-2a)

`tool_handlers` reproduces the part of `_handlers.py` that is not one of
the nine served tools. The map, by reference line:

| Function | Lines | What it needs from the machine | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DESC_*` | 70-78 | nothing (re-exports of `handlers/__init__.py`) | handlers-2b re-exports them |
| `RefusedError` | 81-96 | nothing | built: `Refusal` with `RefusalClass::Refused` |
| `_in_the_way` | 99-106 | nothing | built: `in_the_way` |
| `RetryableRefusal` | 109-132 | nothing | built: `retryable_refusal` |
| `KeptWriteRefusal` | 135-153 | nothing | built: `kept_write_refusal` |
| `store_refusal` | 156-169 | the store's classification | built: `store_refusal`, classification an argument |
| `_ABSENT` | 172 | nothing | built: `Failure::Absent` |
| `_kept_or_retryable` | 186-207 | the store's commit counter | built: `kept_or_retryable` |
| `_refusals_as_tool_errors` | 210-261 | nothing | built: `refusals_as_tool_errors` |
| `_read_only` | 264-268 | nothing | built: `read_only` |
| `ToolHandlers.__init__`, `for_request`, `with_store`, `_run` | 271-367 | a store source, a worker pool | built: `ToolHandlers` |
| `memory_search` through `memory_admin` | 370-650 | the per-tool modules | handlers-2b |

A tool body is a closure answering a value or a `Failure`, the exception
it raised: `Value` (a `ValueError`), `Absent` (one of `_ABSENT`, by
`store::schema::Absent` and its args), `Sqlite` (a
`sqlite3.OperationalError`: its `sqlite_errorcode` and `str()`), `Tool`
(a `ToolError`, the refusal classes among them), `Other` (any other
exception, raised as it is) and `Py` (an error `absent_text` raised).
Another `sqlite3.Error` subclass is `Other`: the reference catches only
`OperationalError`. The bodies run synchronously: the reference awaits
nothing that yields inside one, so no async runtime is needed.

Decisions:

- `store.retryable_code` and `STORE_BUSY` are lane storereads' (`store`
  reads). Every function that classifies takes it as an argument,
  `Fn(&SqliteFailure) -> Option<&'static str>`; the tests use a
  test-only mapping of the low byte (5 and 6 busy, 13 full).
  `STORE_FULL` is spelled here because `_in_the_way` compares with it.
- `sqlite_errorcode` is `Option<i64>`: an attribute that is not an
  `int` is None, as `getattr` and `isinstance` read it. Python's `int`
  has no bound; a caller that holds a larger code passes it wrapped to
  64 bits (`wrap_code` wraps a decimal spelling), which keeps the low
  byte, the only part either check reads.
- The store is a trait, `BundleStore`: `commits` and `same_store`, the
  identity `resolved is self.store` (pointer identity, `Arc::ptr_eq`).
  The recorder's `dataclasses.replace(recorder, store=store)` is
  `RebindStore::with_store`. The store source is `StoreSource`, whose
  request context is opaque (`Option<&dyn Any>`) until handlers-2b
  settles the MCP context's type. `for_request` answers a borrowed
  bundle where the reference answers `self`, and a shallow copy (the
  recorder not rebound) with no offload otherwise.
- `Offload` is a closure that is given the body over a worker's store
  and runs it.
- The refusal texts of a store error and of the read-only refusal carry
  the error's text as it is, control tokens included, and a `ToolError`
  a body raises passes unchanged: the reference defangs only a
  `ValueError`'s text and the `_ABSENT` texts. The port does the same
  (rows of `tool_handlers.jsonl` pin it).

No regular expression is used. `tool_handlers.jsonl` (ungated) is
written by `tests/contract/gen_tool_handlers.py`: each scripted body
through the wrapper and, with the commits moved or not, through
`_kept_or_retryable`. The errors are built by hand with fixed messages
and codes, so no row holds SQLite's own text.

Left for handlers-2b: the nine forwarders (`memory_search` at line 370
through the end of `memory_admin`, about line 650), each a
`refusals_as_tool_errors` over `for_request(ctx).run(...)` of its
per-tool module, and the `DESC_*` re-exports.

## The event kinds and their row classes (`events.py`)

`events` reproduces the telemetry recorder's module, unit by unit. The map
of `src/bettermemory/events.py` by function:

| Function | Lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| the kind tables (`HARNESS_STAMPED_KINDS`, `AUDIT_KINDS`, `OVERRIDE_EVIDENCE_KINDS`, `AUDIT_STATUSES`, `OVERRIDABLE_REFUSALS`, `STATE_STAMP_FIELDS`, `STATE_FIELDS`, `STATE_KINDS`, `STATE_WRITE_ATTEMPTS`, `MEASUREMENT_KINDS`, `ROW_KINDS`), `_kept`, `RowClass` | 63-480 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `is_audit_row` | 187-212 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `row_class`, `prunable` | 483-494 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `state_fields`, `_keys_of` | 497-535 | nothing (`redact_query` passed in) | built (unit 1) |
| `_SECRET_PATTERNS`, `_strip_known_secrets`, `redact_query` | 98-104, 659-722 | nothing; `credentials.secret_spans` (passed in) | built (unit 2, `event_redact`) |
| `NAMED_EVENT_FIELDS`, `named_event_fields`, `_named_inside`, `_named_entries`, `_redact_event_fields` | 758-821 | nothing | built (unit 2, `event_redact`) |
| `suppressed`, `deadline`, `StoreBusy`, `_store_busy`, `within_hook_budget`, `hook_body`, `_NOT_DONE` | 538-656 | the clock, the calling context, the store's busy timeout | built (`event_hook`; see the next section) |
| `Recorder` (`session_for_request`, `worktree_for_request`, `records`, `record`) | 825-951 | the store's writer, the hook scope, the published caller | built (unit 4, `event_recorder`; see its section) |
| `_event_id_items`, `_event_id_list` | 954-990 | nothing | built (`event_id_items`, `event_id_list`, with `recall_settle` unit 1; see that section) |

Unit 1 holds the row kinds and classes, unit 2 the redaction, unit 3 the
hook context and deadline, and unit 4 the recorder over `EventSink`.
The id-list readers are built with `recall_settle`.

What unit 1 reproduces. A row's fields are the `dict` the handler passes,
as `PyValue` pairs in insertion order, and a kind is code points (a kind
holding a lone surrogate is a measurement kind like any other unknown
one). The tables are constants in the reference's order; the golden
header holds each one (frozensets sorted, `OVERRIDABLE_REFUSALS` and
`STATE_FIELDS` in order, each field kept by keys with its keys sorted) and
the test compares every entry.

- `is_audit_row`: `standing_guard` always; on `write` and `update`, a
  `str` status in `AUDIT_STATUSES` or `OVERRIDABLE_REFUSALS`, then
  `forced` that `is True` (the int 1 is not), then any field whose key
  ends in `_acknowledged` and whose value is true by Python's `bool`
  (`events::truthy`: NaN, any path and any datetime are true, `-0.0` is
  false). The keys are read in order and the scan stops at the first true
  one, so a key that is not a `str` raises `AttributeError` only when it
  comes before any such field (`EventsError::AttributeError`).
- `row_class` and `prunable`: state for a key of `STATE_FIELDS`,
  measurement for every other kind.
- `state_fields`: each field in input order kept whole, kept by its keys
  (`_keys_of`: a dict filtered, each dict of a list filtered and every
  other item dropped, None for anything else, a tuple included), or kept
  as a stamp or, on `write` and `update`, as override evidence by its
  suffix. A `probe_query` still in text goes through `redact_query` first;
  that function belongs to unit 2 and is the `redact` argument here. The
  golden file's texts are ones the secret strip leaves unchanged, so the
  test's redactor (SHA-256 of the UTF-8 with surrogates replaced by `?`,
  sixteen hex digits, the length in code points) is the reference's on
  them. A key that is not a `str` is dropped, except on `write` and
  `update`, where the suffix check raises `AttributeError`.

No pattern is matched in this unit, so no regular expression is involved.
`events_kinds.jsonl` (not gated, 115 KB) holds the tables, the class of
every kind and of near misses, the audit answer of every case shape on
the two evidence kinds, the audit kind, one other state kind and a near
miss (a few shapes on every other kind), the kept fields of every kind,
`top_hits` and `probe_query` of every shape, and `_keys_of` directly.
`tests/events_kinds_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port
fails; `tests/events_kinds_robustness.rs` holds 200,000-field rows and
lists (time at 2n against n), a kind of a million code points and values
nested 200,000 deep.

Reference finding, reproduced: `is_audit_row` is documented as safe on a
row read back from a hand-edited log, yet `is_audit_row("write", {1:
True})` and `state_fields("write", {1: "x"})` raise `AttributeError`
(`int` has no `endswith`). A row read from JSON always has `str` keys, so
no log row reaches it; a handler passing a non-`str` keyword cannot
either.

### Unit 2: the query redaction and the named event fields (`event_redact`)

Unit 2 lives in its own module, `src/event_redact.rs`, beside `events`,
with `store_rows.event_import_payload` in `store::rows` and the two
remaining helpers of `time_utils.py` in `src/time_utils.rs`. The lines
above were confirmed against the source as it is now (patterns 98-104,
the redaction 659-722, the named fields 758-821).

- `_SECRET_PATTERNS` (`SECRET_PATTERNS`): the five patterns' own texts,
  no flags, built once with the engine's `Regex::new_str` and applied
  with `Regex::sub` in the reference's order (the `sk-ant-` pattern before the
  generic `sk-`). Each is a bounded T0-T2 site of the decision
  (sections 5 and 6), so none is matched by hand and none waits for
  pyre-9; all five are in the engine's inventory already (the `ast`
  scan of `gen_pyre_atom`). `\b` is Unicode, as `re` reads a `str`
  pattern: `é` after a key's body is a word character, so the key is
  kept.
- `_strip_known_secrets` (`strip_known_secrets`): the five subs, then
  `credentials.secret_spans` on what they left. The detectors are not
  built; they are the `spans` argument (`Spans`), answering `(start,
  end, kind)` in code points. The pieces are joined once, each span
  sliced as Python slices (bounds clamped, an inverted span empty).
- `redact_query`: `{"hash", "preview", "len"}`. The hash is the first
  sixteen hex digits of SHA-256 over the stripped text's UTF-8 with
  `errors="replace"` (a lone surrogate is `?`, one per code point), the
  preview the first 32 code points of the stripped text, `len` the
  original's length in code points. `events::state_fields` takes it as
  `&mut |t| redact_query(t, &mut spans)`.
- `named_event_fields`, `_named_inside`, `_named_entries`
  (`named_event_fields`, `named_inside`, `named_entries`): over
  `control_tokens::named_tokens`. The reference's `named is not value`
  becomes a value rewrite in place: a field the dict lacks is never
  added, every other field keeps its value and position, so the result
  is the reference's by value. `NAMED_EVENT_FIELDS` is its own sorted
  table here and needs neither `Kept` nor `kept_of`.
- `_redact_event_fields` (`redact_event_fields`): `query` and
  `probe_query` that are a `str` redacted, then the named fields (the
  preview of a redacted query is named too).
- `store_rows.event_import_payload` (`store::rows::event_import_payload`,
  with the constants `IMPORTED_FROM_V8` and `ROW_COLUMNS`, both owned
  here): `Err` holds the `ValueError` text, the kind by its `repr`; a
  `ts` or `session` that is not a non-empty `str` is None;
  `imported_from` replaces a field of that name in its place.
- `time_utils.isoformat_utc_optional` and `ensure_utc`: `Option::map`
  over `DateTime::isoformat_utc` and `DateTime::assume_utc`.

`event_redact.jsonl` (not gated, 41 KB; a text a credential detector reads as a key is written as code points) holds each pattern at its bound,
one under and at its word boundaries, the detectors' own shapes, legacy
markers beside detector spans, surrogates, texts of 0, 31, 32 and 33
code points, every shape of every named field, `_redact_event_fields`,
`event_import_payload` on good and bad kinds, `ts` and `session`, the
two time helpers, and a sweep of 3,000 seeded texts as a digest row.
Each redacting row records the reference's calls to `secret_spans`
(made with the module's own patterns and the real detectors; nothing is
patched), which the test answers through the argument.
`tests/event_redact_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port
fails (U+FFFD for a surrogate, ASCII `\b`, the patterns reordered, a
byte preview, spans read before the first pass, an absent field added);
`tests/event_redact_robustness.rs` holds every pattern's backtracking
shape at 20,000 and 200,000 code points, 100,000 spans, values nested
200,000 deep in each named field shape, a 100,000-field event and a
million code points. `credentials::spans` supplies `secret_spans`.
The next sections cover `event_recorder` and `event_hook`.

## The recorder over the store's writer (`event_recorder`, `events.py` 825-951)

`event_recorder` is `events.py`'s unit 4: `Recorder` with
`session_for_request`, `worktree_for_request`, `records` and `record`.
Lines checked against the source as it is now: the class 825-951.

What it reproduces.

- The store is the trait `EventSink` (`record_event(kind, session,
  actor, best_effort, attempts, deadline, fields)`). The writable store's
  event writer is `store::record_event`, bound by `store::recorder::StoreEventSink`. `best_effort` and
  `attempts` are `Some` only on a state row (`false` and
  `STATE_WRITE_ATTEMPTS`), `deadline` only inside a hook body. The two
  context variables are the `HookScope` passed to `records` and `record`;
  the recorder holds none. The published caller (`identity._CURRENT`) is
  the `Published` passed with it.
- `session_for_request`: the published actor's session when its
  `sources["session"]` is `transport` or `header`, else `session_id`.
- `worktree_for_request`: `worktree_root` when the workspace declaration
  is None, else `_handlers.capture_origin().worktree_root`. The
  declaration is a closure the caller builds over
  `identity::workspace_declaration` (its environment, working directory
  and file system); the capture is a closure too, since `capture_origin`
  is not built. Only whether the declaration is None is read, so the
  host's spelling of the path never reaches a row.
- `records`: false inside `suppressed`, else telemetry on or a state kind.
- `record`, in the reference's order: suppressed returns; a measurement
  row with telemetry off returns; `attribution` and `triggered_from` set
  by `setdefault` when not empty; `worktree_root` appended when the
  fields lack the key (a given None is kept); `harness_session` set by
  `setdefault` on `HARNESS_STAMPED_KINDS`; `actor` popped, and a missing
  or None one replaced by the published actor (`EventActor`); `session`
  popped as any value (None included), else `session_for_request`. With
  telemetry off a state row's fields go through `events::state_fields`
  with `event_redact::redact_query` over the recorder's boxed
  `secret_spans`. A measurement failure is logged (`event KIND not
  recorded: TEXT`) and swallowed; a state failure is logged (`state row
  KIND not recorded, the call fails: CLASS: TEXT`) and returned. The
  declaration's and the capture's errors are returned on either class,
  as the reference raises them before its `try`. `Recorder::warn` sends
  each warning to the caller's log handler when the store call fails.
  A handler failure propagates on either row class. Store, origin and
  handler errors preserve every code point in the Python message.

Decisions. A field named like a keyword the recorder passes
(`best_effort`, `attempts`, `deadline`) raises CPython's `TypeError`
inside the reference's `try`, so a measurement row warns and a state row
raises; the text names the callable (`EventSink::call_name`, the store's
`bettermemory.store_events.record_event` by default). Such a field that
the recorder does not pass stays among `fields`, in its place, where
Python's keyword binding hands it to that parameter; the sink binds it.
A field named `self` or `kind` is CPython's `TypeError` from
`Recorder.record()` itself. The first such field in keyword order is
named in the error. Fields are `(str, value)` pairs, since a
keyword's name is always a `str`. No regular expression is involved.

`event_recorder.jsonl` (not gated, 77 KB) runs the recorder over a fake
store that records each call: every stamp and pop on a state and a
measurement kind with telemetry on and off, the redacted and kept fields
of `turn_audited` and `search_miss`, a surrogate kind, each published
caller shape (none, transport, header, env, no session, empty, declared,
process cwd, harness only), the capture answering, None and raising,
suppression, deadlines, store failures of two classes and a failing warning handler.
`event_recorder_python.jsonl` (gated on the Python release, 15 KB) holds
the colliding keywords and CPython's text. Every published caller,
context variable and environment change is set and reset inside its
row. The test's declaration closure answers the published workspace when
it is declared and None when nothing is published (the generator clears
the workspace variables of the environment for those rows).
`tests/event_recorder_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port
fails; `tests/event_recorder_robustness.rs` holds 100,000 fields with
telemetry off, a million-code-point kind and probe query, a value nested
200,000 deep, deadlines at the float edges, and time at 20,000 fields
against 2,000. Left for later: wiring the recorder into `StopSide` and
the handlers, and `_handlers.capture_origin`.

### Recording through the signed store

`store::recorder::StoreEventSink` connects `Recorder` to an owning
`WritableStore` and its clock, a caller's active `Transaction`, or a keyless
connection's refusal. A recorder can reuse that binding across requests.
The credential detector `store::recorder::secret_spans` supplies the normal
span input for both stages. Python binds extra `attempts`, `deadline` and
`best_effort` keywords to writer controls. The writer reads these where Python
first needs them. For example, a joined write skips attempts and deadline
arithmetic. Row signing serializes the redacted payload before encoding
the session. A successful SQL commit survives a later checkpoint error.

`Recorder::record_typed` exposes the structured warning and returns the
original store or handler error. The return carries its Python inheritance,
code points, SQLite code, OS fields and optionally the caller's original
opaque exception handle. A direct `BaseException` escapes immediately.
An ordinary exception reaches the recorder warning; a state row reraises it.
The original `record` and `EventSink::record_event` interfaces remain available.

`RecorderFields::from_json` reads an actual keyword object with the
standard decoder's single NaN object. For a native or runtime producer,
`ActorKeyObjects::bind` retains each NaN key's identity, including inside
tuples. `Recorder::record_fields` passes those handles through actor
conversion and canonical sorting. Repeated references update the first
key in place. Separately constructed NaNs remain distinct even when
they have identical floating-point bits.

`recorder_store_posix.jsonl` compares the ordered diagnostics, timestamps,
timeout restoration, caller and outside connection views, signed rows and
durable head on isolated stores. `recorder_store_python_posix.jsonl` holds
the unhashable-actor diagnostic whose wording changes on Python 3.14
and signed descending numeric-key runs whose NaN ordering changed in
Python 3.13. The portable rows exercise raw JSON actor pairs and nested
metadata on both sides of the 64-key threshold, comparing direct
canonical bytes by SHA-256 and persisted log rows by HMAC. The
signed-store fixtures require POSIX key-ring binding.
`recorder_store_kills` checks same-name exceptions on both sides of COMMIT
and in the keyless handler. The live hook and handler entrypoints still
supply the published context, origin capture and runtime callbacks.

## A hook's deadline and the suppression switch (`event_hook`, `events.py` 538-653)

`event_hook` is `events.py`'s unit 3: `suppressed`, `deadline`,
`_NOT_DONE`, `StoreBusy`, `_store_busy`, `within_hook_budget` and
`hook_body`, with the SQLite busy test the store's writers share. Lines
checked against the source as it is now: the two `ContextVar`s at 541 and
565, `_NOT_DONE` 571-577, `_store_busy` 594-600, `within_hook_budget`
603-636, `hook_body` 639-653.

What it reproduces.

- The two `ContextVar`s (`_SUPPRESSED`, `_DEADLINE`) are one owned value,
  `HookScope`, as `identity::Published` owns `_CURRENT`. There is no
  global: whoever reads either value receives the scope by reference.
  `HookScope::suppressed(body)` sets the flag for the body and gives back
  the flag it found; `within_hook_budget(event, store, monotonic, body)`
  sets the deadline to one clock reading plus
  `daemon_client::hook_budget_seconds(event)`, or keeps the deadline
  already set when the new one is not less (Python's `min(held, at)`, so
  a held NaN stays), and gives back the deadline it found on every return,
  error or not. `deadline()` and `is_suppressed()` read them.
- The store is `Option<&mut dyn BusyTimeout<E>>` (`busy_timeout`, and
  `set_busy_timeout`, which fails with the body's error type as the
  reference's raises). A busy timeout above the budget is lowered to the
  budget for the body and set back to the value read after it; one equal
  to the budget or below, or NaN, is not touched. The store is lent to the
  body. A lowering call that fails is raised as it is and leaves the new
  deadline set, since the reference sets it before its `try`; a restoring
  call that fails replaces the body's outcome and leaves the timeout at
  the budget. Both follow the reference's leak rather than repair it.
- A body's error is any type with `Raised` (its class name and its
  `sqlite_errorcode`). `is_busy` (`_store_busy`) holds for the class
  `OperationalError` with a primary code (`primary_code`, `code & 0xFF`
  with Python's sign: `-251` is BUSY) of BUSY 5 or LOCKED 6; such an
  error becomes `HookFailure::StoreBusy` with `store_busy_message(event)`,
  the reference's f-string with `_NOT_DONE`'s three entries and
  `nothing was shown` for any other event, and the error kept as its
  cause. Any other error, a nested hook's `StoreBusy` included, is
  `HookFailure::Raised` unchanged. `primary_code` and `is_busy` are
  public for `store_events._primary_code` and `_busy` (lane storeev1);
  `store::reads::retryable_code` answers a name, not a masked code.
- `hook_body(event)` reads `store=` only where it has `set_busy_timeout`;
  in Rust the caller settles that by passing the store or None, and
  `HookScope::hook_body` is then `within_hook_budget`.

Decisions. A `sqlite_errorcode` that is not an `int` is None; a `bool` is
its `int`; codes are `i64` (a Python `int` past that range is not a code
SQLite gives). The reference restores in `finally`, which a Python
`BaseException` also crosses; a Rust panic is not caught, so a scope a
panic crossed is not reused. No regular expression is involved.

Every reader of the two values in the reference, and how it receives them:

| Reader | Reads | Receives |
|---|---|---|
| `store_events._time_left`, `_waiting_until`, `record_event` (`store_events.py` 87-173) | the deadline, as its `deadline` argument | `deadline: Option<f64>`, from `HookScope::deadline()` at the call |
| `events.Recorder.records`, `Recorder.record` (`events.py` 870-923) | `_SUPPRESSED`, `_DEADLINE` | a borrowed `HookScope` in `event_recorder` |
| `hook.run_audit` (`hook.py` 319-447, `hook_body("stop")`, `events.suppressed` at 411) | both, through the seams | `hook_stop_side::StopSide::within_hook_budget` and `suppressed` (`hook_stop_side.rs` 79, 88): a later wiring implements them by holding a `HookScope` and the clock in the `StopSide` value and calling `HookScope::within_hook_budget` and `suppressed` from them, mapping `HookFailure` into its `Error`; the seams' shape (event, optional store, a body handed the store back) is this one's |
| `recall.py`'s `hook_body("session-start")` (713) and `hook_body("prompt")` (1451) | both | `HookScope::hook_body` when those hooks are ported |
| `_daemon_client` (1698) | `StoreBusy`'s text, as an exception's message | `HookFailure::StoreBusy`'s `message` |
| `tests/contract/generate.py`'s state guard | both, to see a generator restore them | not ported (a Python check) |

`event_hook.jsonl` (not gated, 23 KB) holds `_store_busy` of four classes
over BUSY, LOCKED, their extended codes, other codes, negative and
64-bit codes, a `bool` and a text; `StoreBusy`'s text for the three events,
an unknown one and the empty one; and run trees driven through
`within_hook_budget` and `hook_body` with a fake store and the clock
stubbed per block: budgets per event and per busy timeout, nested
deadlines (earlier, equal, later), busy and other errors in each event,
a nested hook's `StoreBusy`, and suppressed nesting. The Rust test runs
each tree over `HookScope` and compares the whole trace.
`tests/event_hook_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port fails;
`tests/event_hook_robustness.rs` holds the code boundaries, clocks at the
float edges and scopes nested 1,000 deep (time at ten times the depth).

present only on the reference's condition (a `rule` on `prompt_recall`
writes `chars` right after it, an empty `top_hits` is left off
`turn_audited` and kept on the others, `repeat` only when true). The
checks run in the reference's order: `settled_count` first (a `bool` is
refused, so is any value that is not a non-negative `int`, its message
spelling `repr` of the value), then `triggered_from`, then `reply_source`
or `cause`, then the report's `no_signal_reason`. Each message spells
`sorted(set)!r` as Python's `repr` of a list of `str` and the refused text
through `repr`. `settled_count` is taken as any `PyValue` for that reason;
a value `repr` cannot spell (a list nested past the interpreter's depth)
answers `AuditError::Repr`, as the reference's f-string raises
`RecursionError` there. `MissReport.to_dict` spells `checked_at` through
`DateTime::isoformat_utc` (every `+00:00` replaced, so an offset of
`+00:00:30` spells `Z:30`). The two builders that mint an id take
`mint: &mut dyn FnMut() -> String` in place of `generate_ulid`;
`search_miss_fields` mints only when `event_id` is None (an empty id is
kept). The reference's keyword defaults are `TurnAuditedOptions::default`
and `PromptRecallOptions::reference`; `recall_held_fields` takes its
`triggered_from` from the caller. A `held` or `suppressed` entry is a list
of `(key, value)` pairs, copied in order as `dict(entry)` does: a
repeated key keeps its first place and its last value. A hand-built
`settled_count` whose text is not canonical decimal (`" -1"`, `"-0"`) is
refused, since Python prints no int that way.

Decisions. `Verdict` is an enum: the reference annotates it as a
`Literal` and no producer writes another value. Integer fields are `i64`
(Python's are unbounded; every producer writes counts and window
lengths). `REAUDIT_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS` is defined here, the crate's one
definition; a later unit that needs it (the settlement) reads it from
`audit`, and the golden header pins its value. No pattern is matched, so
no regular expression is involved.

`audit_fields.jsonl` (not gated, 57 KB) holds the constants and the seven
reports in its header, every report's `to_dict` and `is_miss`, every hit's
two shapes, `no_owner_prompt_report`, and each builder over a grid of
keyword sets: every variant on the first report and two on each other,
every `ValueError` included. An answer is spelled as `json.dumps` with its
defaults spells it (key order kept), and every quoted text is ASCII, so no
row follows the Unicode tables behind `str.isprintable`.
`tests/audit_fields_kills.rs` holds the cases a plausible wrong port fails
(check order, key orders, keys written only when set, the bool rule);
`tests/audit_fields_robustness.rs` holds 2,000-hit reports, a 100,000
code point refused text, a `settled_count` nested 200,000 deep, integer
bounds, and the growth from 500 to 5,000 hits.

What audit-2 and audit-3 reproduce (built as one unit, `audit::probe`).

- `probe_for_miss` runs the reference's branches in order: a blank
  message (`str.strip` with Python's whitespace) or an empty pool that
  was not `searched` reports `no_signal` without a query; the thin gate
  (when `floor`), an empty searched pool, and a ranker that returns no
  hits report `no_signal` with the query; otherwise the report carries
  the hits and the verdict. `now` is coerced as `_probe_now` does (a
  naive value read as UTC, an offset kept). The creation shield keeps a
  memory whose `created` is at or before `now - creation_shield_seconds`
  (inclusive, compared as instants). The mode check runs after the
  shield, so a shield cutoff out of range raises `OverflowError` before
  a bad mode raises `ValueError`, whose message spells the mode through
  `repr`. The retrieval shield's cutoff is computed only once there are
  hits, so a lookback out of range raises only then.
- `_too_thin_to_probe`: fewer than two distinct stemmed content tokens
  (stopwords and `str.isdigit` tokens dropped), or every unstemmed
  content token in `_ACK_TOKENS` (`audit::probe::ack_tokens`).
- `_miss_hits` labels each hit with `relevance_label_v2`; `_probe_verdict`
  reads the top hit's relevance as exactly `"high"`, then the shield's
  count, then the project cohort on the top hit alone (a `projects:`
  scope and `same_project` of its id).
- `_count_recent_retrievals`: the cutoff first, then the window (a kind
  in `_RETRIEVAL_EVENT_KINDS`, a `ts` that parses and is not before the
  cutoff), then one `prime` with every window id in event order, then per
  event: the session (`session or session_id`) in the set, the worktree
  stamp equal, any retrieved id of the caller's project. The set leaves
  out empty ids.
- `is_duplicate_audit` walks newest first, skipping other kinds and
  sessions (`session_id or session`) and unparsable stamps, and stops at
  the first older event of the session; a dict `probe_query` matches on
  its `hash`, a string on the text.

Decisions. The ranker is the trait `ProbeSearch`, one method taking the
shielded pool, the message, `now` and `ProbeKnobs` (mode,
`excluded_scopes`, `max_results` = `_TOP_HITS_RETAINED`,
`half_life_days`, `conversational`, `rescue_expansion` false); it returns
`ProbeHit` (with `matched_unique` = `len(match_terms)`). The corpus
statistics provider and the admission the reference forwards to
`run_search` stay with the implementation. The admission is the local
trait `ProbeAdmission` (`prime`, `same_project`); neither
`store::caller::Admission` nor `store::pool::Admission` implements it
yet, and the fixtures drive it through a fake. `now` is required (the
reference reads the clock when it is None). An exception comes back as
`ProbeError` by type: `TypeError` for an unhashable `kind` or session
tested against a set, and for a naive `now` passed straight to the dedup
or the shield once it compares a stamp; `AttributeError` for an event
that is not a dict; `OverflowError` for a cutoff out of range. No pattern
is matched here (the tokenizer is `lexicon`'s), so no regular expression
is involved.

Reference finding, reproduced: `_count_recent_retrievals` documents that
"a single bad row never raises", yet an in-window retrieval event whose
`session` is a list raises `TypeError` from the set membership test
(`_count_recent_retrievals([{"kind": "search", "ts": <now>, "session":
["S"]}], session_ids={"S"}, now=<now>, lookback_seconds=60)`), and so
does any event whose `kind` is a list. `is_duplicate_audit` raises
`TypeError` when given a naive `now` and a same-session `turn_audited`
event, where `probe_for_miss` coerces its own.

`audit_probe.jsonl` (not gated, 80 KB) holds `_ACK_TOKENS`, the thin
gate over 19 messages, the v2 label over 120 pairs with its bounds, 75
`probe_for_miss` cases with the ranker's recorded calls and the fake
admission's primes and asks, 30 dedup cases and 13 shield cases. Every
text is ASCII and every value plain JSON. `tests/audit_probe_kills.rs`
holds the bounds, field orders, top-hit-only cohort, prime order, error
order and naive-`now` cases; `tests/audit_probe_robustness.rs` holds a
session nested 100,000 deep, every window at the integer bounds, the v2
label at the `i64` bounds and the growth of the gate, the shield and the
dedup over tenfold inputs.

Left for later: an implementation of `ProbeSearch` over the store's
search and of `ProbeAdmission` over `store::caller::Admission`, and the
callers (`recall_settle._probe_message`, the Stop hook).

## The Stop's settlement of what was shown (`recall_settle.py`)

`recall_settle` reproduces `src/bettermemory/recall_settle.py`, unit by
unit. The map by function:

| Function | Lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_used_in_segment` | 161-182 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `settle_shown` | 185-269 | the store's event reads and record loads, the recorder, the recall state, the clock (an argument) | built (unit 1) |
| `settle_unused` | 272-347 | the same, `sessions.joined_sessions`, the recorder it builds | built (unit 1) |
| `previous_audit_at` | 350-365 | the store's event reads, the clock | built (unit 1) |
| `review_unanswered` | 466-542 | the same, the recorder, the recall state, `review.find_chain` | built (unit 1) |
| `_probe_message` | 48-153 | the probe (`audit.probe_for_miss`), the pool (`handlers.search.resolve_search_pool`), `store.has_memories`, four settings | built (unit 2, `recall_settle::interrupted`) |
| `settle_interrupted` | 368-463 | the transcript (`interrupted_turns`), `Path.expanduser` and `is_file`, the probe, the store's event read, the recorder it builds, the clock | built (unit 2, `recall_settle::interrupted`) |

Unit 1 also builds `events._event_id_items` and `_event_id_list`
(`events.py` 954-990) as `events::event_id_items` and `event_id_list`,
and `recall_state._str_ids` as `events::str_ids`, the one line over them
that `recall_settle` imports.

What unit 1 reproduces. An event is a `PyValue` dict as the log reads
it; a field it lacks reads as None.

- `event_id_items`: a `list` keeps its `str` elements with their original
  indices, a lone non-empty `str` is one id at slot 0, and every other
  value (a tuple included) is empty. Only the top level is read, so a
  value nested to any depth costs one step.
- `event_joined` (`sessions.py` 343-356) is ported here, not taken as a
  trait: by the harness stamp when it equals a non-empty harness session,
  else by `_session_of` (a true `session`, else `session_id`, kept only
  when a `str`) among the sessions.
- `used_in_segment`: the `use` events stamped at or after the segment's
  start (`parse_event_ts`; a stamp that is not a `str` or does not parse
  is skipped) and joined, their `ids` (else `memory_ids`, when `ids` is
  false by Python's `bool`) read through `str_ids`.
- `settle_shown`: the shown ids not settled and not excluded, nothing when
  none or the reply is empty; the joined uses read from the segment's
  start; each pending id in sorted order not used and loadable (a
  missing or tombstoned record is skipped) goes to
  `attribution::attribute_uses`; each match records one `use` row with
  the reference's fields in its order, `prompt_id` only when non-empty
  and `client_model` whenever given; `note_settled` when any settled. An
  empty `harness` reads as `DEFAULT_HARNESS`.
- `settle_unused`: the closed segment's unsettled ids, the sessions
  `joined_sessions` names over the last `REAUDIT_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS`
  with the hook's own id, the joined `show` events with a `str` `id`
  (opened) and the joined uses (attested); the recorder is built
  (`make_recorder`, with the session, `telemetry`, the worktree and the
  hook) after those reads, whether or not anything is recorded, and each
  remaining id records one `unused` row. A clock less than an hour after
  year 1 raises `OverflowError`, as `now - timedelta` does.
- `previous_audit_at`: the session's `turn_audited` rows in the last
  `STATE_IDLE_SECONDS`; the newest instant wins and of equal instants the
  first read is kept, with its own offset. A session value compares by
  equality, so only a `str` matches.
- `review_unanswered`: nothing for an empty session set; the session
  value of each `review_issued` row is looked up in the set, so a list or
  dict there raises `TypeError` (`SettleError::TypeError`) as `x in set`
  does, while an empty list is false and reads `session_id`; the root is
  a valid ULID `parent_review_id`, else a valid ULID `review_id`; a root
  the segment already counted or already taken is skipped; `find_chain`
  is asked of every root in order and a root counts when open and not
  refused for a standing record; one `review_unanswered` row and
  `note_review_roots` when any count.

Decisions. The store's reads (`SettleStore`), the recorder (`Recorder`),
the recall state (`SettleState`, whose `segment` answers a plain
`SegmentView` with `review_roots` beside the fields the task names, since
`review_unanswered` reads them) and `joined_sessions` (`Sessions`) are
traits; `find_chain` is a closure answering `(open, standing_refused)`
and the recorder `settle_unused` builds is a factory closure. The
`recall_state` unit took `SegmentView` over: it is defined there in the
reference's whole shape and re-exported here. Every datetime handed in is
aware, as the reference's callers make them. `RULE`, `DEFAULT_HARNESS`,
`STATE_IDLE_SECONDS`, `REVIEW_UNANSWERED` (`recall_state.py`),
`REAUDIT_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (`audit.py`) and `REVIEW_ISSUED`
(`review.py`) are local constants, each pinned by the golden header. No
regular expression is used (the ULID check is `records::is_valid_ulid`).

Fixtures: `gen_recall_settle.py` writes `recall_settle.jsonl` (not gated,
48 KB): the constants, `event_id_items` over malformed values, four
`_used_in_segment` answers over one list of edge events, and each
function over scripted fakes, with every call the fakes saw in order
(the store's reads with their kinds and bounds, the loads, the recorder's
rows field by field, the state's calls, the recorder built, the join and
the chains asked) and the answer or the error raised.
`golden_recall_settle` checks every row; `recall_settle_kills` holds the
cases a plausible wrong port fails; `recall_settle_robustness` holds id
fields nested 100,000 deep and 200,000 long, clocks at the ends of the
calendar, and the event scan's growth (20,000 events against 2,000).

What unit 2 (settleint) reproduces, in `recall_settle::interrupted`.

- `probe_message` (`_probe_message`): the pool first
  (`resolve_search_pool(store, message, excluded_scopes=, admission=)`),
  then `store.has_memories()` only when the pool is empty (the
  reference's `bool(pool) or store.has_memories()` short-circuits), then
  the probe with the pool's records and statistics provider, the
  message, the recent events, the session, the server session as the
  retrieval session, `now`, `ATTRIBUTION_LOOKBACK_SECONDS` (600, from
  `hook`), the admission, the worktree, the excluded scopes, the mode
  (`search_mode or "hybrid"`), the half-life, the conversational switch,
  the caller's `floor` and `searched`. Whatever the pool or the probe
  raises comes back as `Fault::Raised`.
- `settle_interrupted`: nothing for no path or an empty one; the path is
  expanded (`str(Path(p).expanduser())`, a closure, whose RuntimeError
  for an unknown home comes back as `Fault::Raised`) and asked
  `is_file` through `fsdata::Fs::stat` (a regular file, links followed,
  false for a FIFO, socket, device or folder, a NUL or an unencodable
  path, and an errno 3.13's `_ignore_error` accepts: ENOENT, ENOTDIR,
  EBADF, ELOOP or Windows codes 21, 123, 1921; any other OSError, such as
  ENAMETOOLONG or EACCES, raises as `Fault::Os`, as the pinned 3.13 does,
  where 3.14's `is_file` answers False; an error known by its class
  alone declines); `since` is
  the previous audit, else `now` less `STATE_IDLE_SECONDS`
  (`OverflowError` before year 1). The `turn_audited` rows the store
  answers are filtered by session alone (a true `session`, else
  `session_id`, equal to the hook's), neither their kind nor their stamp
  is checked again, and each `str` `prompt_id` counts as audited. The
  recorder is built (session, telemetry, worktree, an empty
  `triggered_from`) before the transcript is read. Each turn with a
  prompt id and a prompt, not the excluded id and not audited, is probed
  at `now` with the floor and recorded as one `turn_audited` row
  (`reply_source="interrupted"`, `RULE`, `settled_count=0`,
  `assistant_present` when the reply is not None, an empty reply
  included, `client_model` the turn's model). The audited set is read
  once, so a prompt id the transcript holds twice is settled twice, as
  the reference does. A `ValueError` of `turn_audited_fields` (a refused
  `triggered_from` or `no_signal_reason`) is raised after that turn's
  probe, the rows before it kept.

Decisions of unit 2. `audit.probe_for_miss`,
`handlers.search.resolve_search_pool` and `transcript.interrupted_turns`
are closures (`Prober`, `TranscriptHost`), so this unit does not wait
for the probe's port; the pool's record and provider types are
parameters the probe receives as they are. The four settings read off
the configuration are `Settings` (`search_mode`, `half_life_days`,
`conversational`, `telemetry_enabled`), so nothing here depends on the
shape of `config`. `SettleStore` gains `has_memories` at its end with a
default that declines (`None`, raised as `Fault::NotOffered`), so
existing implementations need no change. `Path.expanduser` is a closure
because the host spells the path (`PosixPath` or `WindowsPath`);
`is_file` encodes the expanded text as the host's `os.stat` takes it
(`host_bytes`, with `STAT_TAKES_WIDE` set by cfg and both branches
tested: surrogateescape on POSIX, UTF-8 on Windows). On Windows the
reference stats a path holding a lone surrogate through the wide string;
the port declines (`Fault::NotPorted`), recorded as class os in
`recall_settle_interrupted_not_posix.rs`. No regular expression is used.

Fixtures of unit 2: `gen_recall_settle.py` also writes
`recall_settle_interrupted.jsonl` (not gated, 25 KB): 7 `_probe_message`
cases and 20 `settle_interrupted` cases over scripted fakes (the probe
answers recorded reports, the pool its recorded size, `Path` and the
transcript their recorded answers), each with every call the fakes saw
and the answer or the error with its message. The rows hold no real
path: the transcript is `/t/ok.jsonl` and `is_file` is scripted.
`golden_recall_settle_interrupted` checks every row against a
`fsdata::MemFs`; `recall_settle_interrupted_kills` holds the cases a
plausible wrong port fails (the repeated prompt id, the short-circuited
`has_memories`, the scan that trusts the store, the recorder built before
the read, the error after the probe); `recall_settle_interrupted_robustness`
holds 20,000 turns against 10,000 audited rows, a prompt id nested 1,000
deep, clocks at the ends of the calendar, and the settlement's growth
(5,000 turns against 500).

## The session join (`sessions.py`)

`sessions` reproduces `src/bettermemory/sessions.py`: the join between a
client-side hook's transcript session id and the in-process server
sessions that served its conversation, read off the event log alone. The
map by function (lines at 998253b2):

| Function | Lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_OUT_OF_PROCESS_TRIGGERS` | 47-49 | nothing | built (unit 1, `OUT_OF_PROCESS_TRIGGERS`, sorted) |
| `_disabled_scopes_from_events` | 52-103 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `_latest_in_process_session` | 106-149 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `_session_of` | 152-156 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `harness_joined_sessions` | 159-177 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `hook_spans` | 180-198 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `runs_beside` | 201-223 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `live_harness_sessions` | 226-238 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `bridged_session` | 241-323 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `joined_sessions` | 326-340 | nothing | built (unit 1) |
| `event_joined` | 343-355 | nothing | built in `recall_settle` (re-exported) |

The whole module is pure functions over the events, so it is one unit
(399 lines of Rust source, comments included).

What unit 1 reproduces. An event is a `PyValue` dict as the log reads it;
`event.get(k)` reads the last value of a `str` key and a missing field
reads as None. The functions take the events as a slice whatever the
reference's annotation (a list or an iterable). An answer that is a set
is a `BTreeSet<PyStr>`: nothing observes its order. `hook_spans` answers
`HookSpans`, its sessions in first-insertion order as the reference's
dict keeps them, read by `get` and `entries`.

- `x in _OUT_OF_PROCESS_TRIGGERS` (`is_out_of_process`) is `frozenset`
  membership: true only for a `str` equal to one of the four members; a
  hashable value of any other type (None, an int, a bool, a float) is
  absent; a list or a dict (or a tuple holding one) is unhashable and
  raises `TypeError` there, answered as `Err(PyError::TypeError)` by every
  function that reads `triggered_from`, at the event its walk reaches it.
  The reversed walks (`_latest_in_process_session`, `bridged_session`'s
  stamp walk) return before reaching an older unhashable row; the forward
  ones (`harness_joined_sessions`, `hook_spans`) raise on any. An empty
  harness session reads no trigger in `harness_joined_sessions` or
  `hook_spans`; `bridged_session` and `joined_sessions` still fall back to
  `_latest_in_process_session`, which reads it. Neither does
  `_disabled_scopes_from_events` given its anchor.
- `event.get("session") or event.get("session_id")`: every false value
  by Python's `bool` (`events::truthy`: the empty `str`, 0, False, an
  empty list or dict, None) hands over to `session_id`. `_session_of` and
  `_latest_in_process_session` keep the result only when it is a `str`,
  the empty one included where `or` hands it back; `hook_spans` keeps
  only a non-empty `str`; `_disabled_scopes_from_events` compares it
  unfiltered with `!=`, so a non-`str` never equals the anchor.
- `_latest_in_process_session`: the newest event no hook wrote with a
  `str` session, the newest whose `worktree_root` equals the given one
  first, else the newest of any worktree.
- `_disabled_scopes_from_events`: the anchor is `server_session` when
  given, else `_latest_in_process_session`; the anchor's `scope_disable`
  rows add and `scope_enable` rows remove a `str` scope in log order. A
  `kind` or `scope` that is not a `str` is skipped (the tuple test on
  `kind` compares with `==` and hashes nothing).
- `harness_joined_sessions`: the `_session_of` of every event no hook
  wrote whose `harness_session` is the given (non-empty) one. No worktree
  filter: the harness join names a server wherever it runs.
- `hook_spans`: per non-empty `str` session of the hook rows whose `ts`
  parses (`datetime::parse_event_ts`, always aware: naive is UTC, an
  offset is kept, not converted), the least and the greatest stamp as
  instants. `min` and `max` keep their first argument on a tie, so of two
  stamps equal as instants in different offsets the earlier row's
  spelling stays at both ends.
- `runs_beside`: `other` has a span, and `conversation` has none, or
  `other`'s last stamp is at or after `conversation`'s first (`>=` as
  instants).
- `live_harness_sessions`: the sessions of `hook_spans` other than the
  given one that run beside it; empty for an empty harness session.
- `bridged_session`: the events walked newest first, skipping hook rows
  and rows whose `harness_session` is not a non-empty `str` or whose
  `_session_of` is None. The first row stamped with this conversation
  answers its session at once (no worktree filter). Otherwise each
  session keeps the first stamp the reversed walk meets (`setdefault`:
  its newest). With none stamped, `_latest_in_process_session` answers.
  Else the sessions stamped with a conversation that runs beside this one
  are set aside; and when this conversation has a hook row, the stamps of
  the sessions not set aside that wrote at or after its first hook row
  (in the given worktree only, when one is given) are counted, and two or
  more set aside every stamped session. `_latest_in_process_session`
  then answers over the events whose `_session_of` is not set aside (an
  event without one is kept).
- `joined_sessions`: `harness_joined_sessions` when it names any, else
  the one `bridged_session` names, else none.

No pattern of `re` is involved. No reference finding.

Fixtures: `tests/contract/gen_sessions.py` writes `sessions.jsonl` (not
gated: every id, stamp and worktree is ASCII, every stamp carries an
offset or reads as UTC; 61 KB). The header holds the triggers and the
count; 56 rows are hand-built logs (each trigger, an absent, None, int,
bool, float and other `str` trigger, list, dict and empty-list triggers at
the newest and the oldest row, the session and session_id fallbacks with
each false value, a truthy non-`str` session, the worktree match and its
fallback, scope toggle sequences with non-`str` scopes and kinds, harness
stamps that are not a non-empty `str`, the scenarios of
`bridged_session`'s docstring: a server stamped before a /clear, a /clear
beside another window's turn in the same worktree and in another, the
foreign join, a live other window, a /resume's first and second call, a
restamped session, equal instants in other offsets, a span one
microsecond short), each with every function's answer for every harness
session, worktree and anchor the log names plus null, empty and absent
ones. The last row is a sweep of 5,000 logs drawn by a 64-bit LCG from
pools of kinds, triggers (an unhashable one among them), sessions,
session ids, harness stamps, worktrees, scopes and timestamps the row
holds, each
through `bridged_session` and `joined_sessions` (five harness sessions by
three worktrees), `live_harness_sessions` and
`_disabled_scopes_from_events`: 115,000 answer lines pinned by count and
SHA-256. `golden_sessions` checks every row and regenerates the sweep;
`sessions_kills` holds the cases a plausible wrong port fails (the
bridge's walk read forwards, a session's oldest stamp kept, `runs_beside`
with `>`, the worktree filter in the harness join, the stamps check
skipped, `min` keeping the later of equal instants, `or` read as
is-None, an unhashable trigger answered as absent); `sessions_robustness`
runs 100,000 events over 10,000 sessions through every function against
10,000 over 1,000 (`timing::TENFOLD`), unhashable, deeply nested (100,000
levels), huge and non-`str` values at every field the functions read,
and stamps at the ends of the calendar.

Left for later units: wiring these functions in place of the traits and
closures that stand for them today (`hook_stop_side`'s `StopSide`
methods `bridged_session`, `joined_sessions`, `harness_joined_sessions`
and `_disabled_scopes_from_events`, `recall_settle::Sessions`, and the
`latest_session` closure of `hook::emit_hook_attributions`);
`recall_counters` reads `hook_spans` and `runs_beside`.

## The prompt recall's steps (`recall_prompt.py`)

`recall_prompt` reproduces `src/bettermemory/recall_prompt.py` (280 lines
at origin/v9) whole, in one unit (recall_prompt-1). The map by function:

| Function | Lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_PromptTurn` | 74-95 | nothing | built (`PromptTurn`, read through `PromptTurnView`) |
| `_prompt_window` | 98-121 | the store's event reads, `sessions.bridged_session` and `_disabled_scopes_from_events`, the clock (an argument) | built |
| `_settle_before_probe` | 124-157 | `recall_settle.settle_interrupted` (a closure), `previous_audit_at`, `Admission.on` (a closure) | built |
| `_prompt_probe` | 160-186 | `recall_settle._probe_message` (a closure), `Admission.on` | built |
| `_record_hold` | 189-221 | the recorder (a factory closure), `audit.recall_held_fields`, `recall_admission._delivery_membership` | built |
| `_record_delivery` | 224-280 | the same, `audit.prompt_recall_fields`, `recall_admission._rc3_admitted`, `RecallState.forget` | built |

What it reproduces.

- `prompt_window`: the dedup cut (`now - REAUDIT_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECONDS`)
  first, then the own cut: the segment's start when `view.segment > 0`,
  else `now - STATE_IDLE_SECONDS`. The comparison is Python's: an int, a
  bool or a float compares, anything else (None, a string, a list) raises
  `TypeError` before the log is read; a clock less than an hour (or, for
  a first segment, a day) after year 1 raises `OverflowError`. Then the
  log since the dedup cut, the bridged session over it (the harness
  session and the caller's worktree) and the scopes switched off.
- `settle_before_probe`: the admission on POOL_PREFILTER, then the
  previous audit's stamp, then `settle_interrupted` with the reference's
  keyword arguments (`triggered_from` "prompt_hook", no excluded prompt).
  The stamp is read inside the reference's `try`, so its `OverflowError`
  is swallowed like the settlement's own failures and the settlement is
  not called. The warning the reference logs (`interrupted turns not
  settled at the prompt: <class>: <str(exc)>`) is the return value.
- `prompt_probe`: the probe over the owner's words, under the admission
  on POOL_PREFILTER when the surface is PROMPT_RECALL and under the turn's
  own admission otherwise, never floored.
- `record_hold`: the recorder is built first, whatever follows; the row
  is built only when the recorder records `recall_held` (not inside
  `events.suppressed`, and with telemetry on, since it is a measurement
  row), so a refused cause raises `ValueError` only then. The row is
  `recall_held_fields` (probe mode the search mode, or "hybrid" when it
  is empty or None; `RULE`; the segment, prompt id, transcript and
  harness), then `admission` set to the surface and the membership keys
  merged as `dict.update` does: a key already there keeps its place.
- `record_delivery`: `prompt_recall_fields` with the mode as the
  delivered reason and the block's length in code points; `event_id`
  overwritten in place, `admission`, the membership keys, then
  `rc3_admitted`: the gate's ids in order, duplicates kept, less the
  chosen pointers that were not shown. A row the recorder fails to write
  forgets the session's held state (`SettleState::forget`) and raises;
  `record_hold` forgets nothing.

Decisions. The configuration is read through its two switches
(`telemetry`, `search_mode`); the closures that need the rest of it hold
it themselves. The resolution, admission and caller are type parameters
the closures and `DeliveryGate` read; `caller.worktree_root` is a field
of its own. `Admission.on` is a closure, `settle_interrupted` and
`_probe_message` are closures over the store and an argument struct, so
this unit does not wait for settleint. The recorder factory takes
`recall_settle::RecorderSpec` with an empty `triggered_from`, the
`Recorder` dataclass's default. `recall_settle::Recorder` gains two
methods with default bodies, `suppressed` (false) and `try_record` (a
write that cannot fail), and `SettleState` gains `forget` (a no-op by
default), so existing implementations need no change. A chosen hit is
`Chosen<M, T>` (the hit, the record, its trust row, its in-force entry);
only the hit's id is read. POOL_PREFILTER and PROMPT_RECALL are local
constants, pinned by the golden header. No regular expression is used.

Fixtures: `gen_recall_prompt.py` writes `recall_prompt.jsonl` (not
gated, 24 KB): each step over a real `_PromptTurn` and scripted fakes,
with every call the fakes saw in order (the store's reads and their
bounds, the joins, `Admission.on`, the settlement's and the probe's
arguments, the warning, the recorder built and the rows it wrote, the
membership and rc3 calls, `forget`) and the answer or the error raised.
`golden_recall_prompt` checks every row; `recall_prompt_kills` holds the
cases a plausible wrong port fails (the segment comparison, the order of
the cuts, the swallowed stamp failure, the admission per surface, the
recorder asked before the row is built, the probe mode default, the event
id kept in place, code point lengths, the drop, the forget on a failed
delivery only); `recall_prompt_robustness` holds a 100,000-event window,
clocks at both ends of the calendar, segment numbers past machine
integers, a megabyte block and the drop's growth (20,000 pointers against
2,000).

Nothing is left for a later unit. `settle_interrupted` and
`_probe_message` arrive with settleint and are handed in by the caller
(`recall.prompt_recall`, not built).

| function | reference lines | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_CONTROL_TOKENS`, `_CONTROL_TOKEN_KIND`, `_TURN_MARKER_KIND` | 116-179 | nothing | built (`CONTROL_TOKENS`) |
| `_CONTROL_TOKEN_RE` | 203-210 | Unicode data (`\s`) | built (hand-written matcher) |
| `ControlTokenHit`, `to_dict` | 213-223 | nothing | built (`Hit`) |
| `_matches` | 226-243 | nothing | built |
| `find_control_tokens` | 246-257 | nothing | built |
| `control_token_offsets` | 260-275 | nothing | built |
| `_touches` | 283-291 | Unicode data (`isspace`, `isalnum`) | built |
| `_named` | 301-323 | nothing | built |
| `defang_control_tokens` | 326-353 | nothing | built |
| `folded_quote` | 356-365 | Unicode data (`str.split`) | built |
| `_children`, `_Visit`, `_rebuilt`, `named_tokens` | 369-444 | nothing | built over `PyValue` |
| `_FIELD_WHY`, `BARE_NAME_REMEDY`, `ControlTokenError`, `refuse_control_tokens` | 463-516 | nothing | built |

### The pattern, matched by hand

No regex crate is used. `_CONTROL_TOKEN_RE` is six alternatives, and
each delimited one is a fixed opener, an optional `/`, a run of a class
bounded `{1,32}` and a closer the class excludes. A greedy bounded run
that backtracks gives back only class members, none of which is the
closer, so the alternative matches exactly when the whole run (not capped
at 32) is 1 to 32 long and the closer follows; the matcher reads at most
33 class members. The alternatives start on distinct second characters
(`|`, `｜`, `<`, a lowercase letter or `_`), so trying them in the
pattern's order is one decision. The turn alternative is `\A\s*` only
at index 0 (finditer and sub from 0) and `\n[ \t\r]*\n` at a newline,
each followed by `Human:` or `Assistant:`; their runs give back only
whitespace, which neither name starts with, so only the full run can
match. `\s` is `str.isspace` (`unicode::is_space`), as `re` reads it on
a `str` pattern. Matches are scanned as `finditer` and `sub` scan: from
the end of the last match, an unlisted shape (`<b>`, `<|foo|>`) consumed
like a listed one.

### Decisions

- `named_tokens` walks `PyValue` with its own stack and clones each
  unchanged subtree once, where its parent is rebuilt. A rebuilt dict
  merges keys as `dict(zip(...))` does: the first key kept, the last
  value. Key equality is Python's across `bool`, `int` and `float`, and
  element by element in tuples; a NaN key equals nothing, since two keys
  here are never one object. A path and a datetime pass through, as the
  reference passes a `Path`; the reference's identity results (`is`) are
  equal values here.
- `refuse_control_tokens` returns `ControlTokenError` with the message;
  `remedy` and `why` are arguments, `BARE_NAME_REMEDY` and `FIELD_WHY`
  the defaults the caller passes.

### Tests

`control_tokens.jsonl` (not gated) pins the table, the two texts, every
listed token alone and in contexts, each shape at and past its bound,
nested and adjacent tokens, the turn markers in every whitespace context,
350 texts drawn from fixed fragments by a seeded generator, refusals with
other fields, remedies and whys, and `named_tokens` over nested values
with merging keys. Its texts hold only ASCII, surrogates, U+FF5C and
U+2581. `control_tokens_unicode.jsonl` (Unicode-gated) holds texts with
other code points and a sweep of every code point beside a token, inside
a DeepSeek delimiter and before `Human:`, hashed per block of 0x1000.
`control_tokens_kills.rs` holds cases a wrong reading fails (the bound,
consumption of unlisted shapes, `\A` at index 0 only, `\s` past ASCII,
a vertical tab in a blank line, code point offsets, the second defang
pass, a speaker set apart, a single fold, key merging).
`control_tokens_robustness.rs` reads a megabyte of each opener within
three times the reference's measured time in release, checks linear
growth, every code point, names past the bound and a value nested
100,000 deep.

Nothing is left for a later unit. No reference defect was found: 300,000
random texts gave no defanged text and no folded quote that still carries
a listed token.

No pattern of `re` is used by the built functions.

### Decisions

- `WordsSeen` keeps its `OrderedDict` as a vector in recency order under
  a `std::sync::Mutex` (a poisoned lock is taken as it stands): at most
  500 keys, so a linear search costs less than hashing two texts. The
  store path is the text `str(store_path)` gives; the caller passes it.
  `held` lists a key's prompts for tests; the reference has no such
  method.
- `_bounded` walks every occurrence, overlapping ones included, from one
  Knuth-Morris-Pratt pass: the same indexes `str.find(wanted, start + 1)`
  visits, in linear time. An empty quote, which the reference never
  passes, answers `None` where the reference raises `IndexError` (the
  text's first character alphanumeric) and true otherwise.
- `summarize` takes its limit as `i64`; a limit below one cuts to the
  ellipsis alone, as `text[:0] + "…"` does.
- `disputed_marks` returns the dict's items in its order (first naming
  of each member), with a hash index where the reference's `not in` scans
  the member's list; the answers are the same.
- `render_recall_block` returns an empty text and no ids when nothing
  fits, as `("", [])`.

### Tests

`recall_render.jsonl` (not gated) pins the constants, `_fold` and
`_bounded` over ASCII, U+00A0, U+3000, U+00DF, U+00E9 and surrogates (the
empty-quote raise included), `summarize` at and around each bound,
`disputed_marks` grids (duplicates, self pairs, the cut at 15 and the cap
at +99), `_core`, the line and excerpt rules over every annotation, and
`render_recall_block` over pointer sets that cross the cap at each length
step (summary and snippet lengths in runs), and `WordsSeen` sequences:
the twenty-prompt bound, the 500-key eviction and its refresh on use,
control tokens quoted by name, word boundaries. `recall_render_unicode.jsonl`
(Unicode-gated) holds `_fold` and `_bounded` past the stable code points
and a digest of every code point through `_fold` and `_bounded` on each
side. `recall_render_kills.rs` holds the cases a wrong reading fails
(overlapping occurrences, the quote's own edges, full case folding, the
recency refresh, the name of a token, code point lengths, the mark's cut
and cap, the ellipsis character alone, the order of the cap's cuts).
`recall_render_robustness.rs` holds `_bounded` to linear growth on near
misses and on a match at every index, megabyte prompts of surrogates,
`summarize` at the integer bounds, 2,000 pointers, and `disputed_marks`
to linear growth.

What is left: the brief (`_select_brief`, `session_brief` and its
helpers), `clean_prompt` with `owner_prompt`, and the prompt recall's
entry (`prompt_recall`, `_caller_resolution`, `_prompt_turn`), each over

### Unit recall-choose, as built (`recall::choose`)

Reference lines at origin/v9: `_seen_in_log` 1375-1448,
`_seen_in_segment` 1714-1732, `_choose_hits` 1735-1831,
`_deliver_recall` 1834-1902, with `recall_admission._unless_standing`
(162-172) and `_contradiction_open` (174-188). `recall_result.HookResult`
is not otherwise in the crate, so `choose::HookResult` is a plain struct
naming `recall_result.py`; its constructor is `__post_init__` (the text's
control tokens named by `defang_control_tokens`, `chars` following when
it was the text's length).

- `seen_in_log` is `_seen_in_log` over events as `PyValue` dicts. A
  `kind`, or a session tested against the sessions set, that Python
  cannot hash raises TypeError (`ChooseError::TypeError`): `kind` is
  tested against a frozenset, so a list kind raises before the stamp is
  read. A harness stamp that names `harness_session` never tests the
  session (`or` short-circuits), so an unhashable session there answers.
  `event.get("status", "committed")` keeps a present `None`, so a write
  with a null status is not committed and one with no status is. The id
  lists are `returned or memory_ids or hit_ids` with Python truthiness
  through `events::str_ids`.
- `seen_in_segment` joins `{key[1]} | joined_sessions(...)` (the
  `recall_settle::Sessions` trait) and reads the log from
  `min(own_since, started_at)`, the first on a tie, as `min` keeps it.
  The kinds passed are `SEEN_KINDS`; the reference passes a frozenset,
  whose order no caller may read.
- `choose_hits` takes the turn as the trait `PromptTurnView` (its store,
  its admission, surface, key, clock, worktree root and remint), the
  segment's `shown` and `started_at` with the own cut and the recent
  events (`Window`), and `model.admit_recall(resolution, hits,
  admission=)` as a closure answering `(delivered, suppressed)`. The
  store's reads are the trait `ChooseStore`, over `in_force`'s
  `LinkReader`; `standing.standing_ids` is a store method taking the
  admission. `in_force` is the crate's; ids cross into it as Rust
  strings, so an admitted hit id holding a lone surrogate cannot reach it
  unchanged, and `choose_hits` declines (`ChooseError::NotUnicode`)
  where the reference reads that id's in-force entry (store ids are
  ASCII). `dict(admitted.suppressed)` keeps the last relation of an id.
  The hashability test of a `kind` or a session walks a tuple without
  recursion.
- `deliver_recall` takes the recall state as `ClaimState`,
  `generate_ulid` as `mint`, `_record_delivery` as `record` (answering
  `str(fields["event_id"])`) and the hold as a closure. Until
  `recall_prompt` is ported its `_PromptTurn` implements nothing here;
  that unit implements `PromptTurnView`.

Regular expressions: none.

Findings about the reference (reproduced, pinned): a hit the probe ranks
twice is chosen twice and rendered as two pointers with one id, since the
already-chosen test runs only on a head that took a history hit's slot
(`gen_recall_choose.py`'s case with hits `a, a, b`;
`recall_choose_kills::a_hit_ranked_twice_is_chosen_twice`). A hit whose
record does not load is dropped before the admission is consulted, so it
leaves no held entry even when the admission withheld it.

through `_deliver_recall` (admission, provenance, contradiction and its

and their own gates, held records, an extender, disputed marks, a control
