Reference findings (reproduced, pinned or recorded):

- `has` and `has_many` can disagree on a case-insensitive file system.
  `has(x)` checks the loose path with `isfile`, which on macOS's default
  APFS or on NTFS finds a file stored as `AB/CDEF...`; `has_many([x, y])`
  with `y` in the same fanout lists the folder and compares exact bytes,
  so it leaves `x` out. Reproduction: on macOS, a loose blob stored at
  `objects/ce/0136...` renamed to `objects/CE/0136...` in uppercase:
  `has(name)` is True and `has_many([name, other])` with `other` starting
  `ce` is empty. The port asks the same questions of its `Fs`, so `StdFs`
  answers as the host's file system does; no golden row holds it, since
  the answer follows the volume.
- A damaged zlib check is seen by `header` of a loose object only where
  the 32 bytes asked for reach the stream's end: a 13-byte loose blob
  with a wrong Adler-32 has no header (None), while `has` is True. The
  golden case "loose a wrong check" (`gitobjects_reader_zlib.jsonl`).

Fixtures and tests:

- `gitobjects_reader.jsonl` (class i, 35 cases, 60 KB),
  `gitobjects_reader_zlib.jsonl` (class ii, zlib, 6 cases) and
  `gitobjects_reader_posix.jsonl` (POSIX only, 5 cases), written by
  `tests/contract/gen_gitobjects_reader.py`. Every store is laid out by
  hand: zlib streams of stored blocks (no compressor's bytes), packs with
  whole, OFS and REF entries, version 2 indexes with a 64-bit table,
  names that are the content's SHA-1 or SHA-256. The cases: loose
  objects of every type and each question; malformed loose headers; a
  blob of 100,000 bytes in two blocks at and one past its cap; loose
  files cut at six lengths; a folder at a loose path; eviction of a loose
  file and of a pack; a pack of a blob, an OFS delta, a REF delta on it, a
  tree and a commit; a chain of 20 deltas under caps past the size and
  the work factor; damaged pack entries (type 5, a lost base, a distance
  past the start, a wrong source size, a cut header); an offset at 2**63;
  prefixes shared by two loose names, two packs, a pack and a loose file,
  and one object in two packs and loose; fanout names not hex or of
  another width; a fanout that is a file; packs written between
  questions; sha256; an unknown format; no objects folder. The zlib file
  holds damaged loose streams and deltas of 20 and 21 bytes with a wrong
  check; the POSIX file a FIFO at a loose path, unreadable files, an
  unlistable fanout and objects in an alternate.
- `golden_gitobjects_reader` (2 tests) and
  `golden_gitobjects_reader_posix` ask each case in memory (`MemFs`)
  and, on unix, on disk (`StdFs`), under unit 3's `Claims`;
  `gitobjects_reader_not_posix` records the gap off unix;
  `gitobjects_reader_kills` (9 tests); `gitobjects_reader_robustness`
  (4 tests: 20,000 names against 2,000 and a fanout of 20,000 names
  against 2,000 for linear growth, names of a MiB, outside ASCII and
  empty, caps at 0 and `u64::MAX`, a 4 MiB object and a chain of 5,000
  deltas).

Left for later: `location_git`'s `RepositoryHistory` takes this reader
through a trait (lane lochist); the impl is a follow-up.

## A location capture's vocabulary

Read at ececad8c. The pure part is about 1,150 lines of reference logic,
so it was split; parts (a) and (b) below are built (`src/capture/`),
part (c) is not.

- `location_git.FileSeen` (1188-1198) and `Capture` (1201-1385): the
  capture's fields with their defaults. `to_token` (1268-1322) writes
  `v` (`_location_probe.TOKEN_VERSION`, 1) then 28 keys in a fixed order;
  keys become `[device, inode, birth]` or null, tuples become lists,
  `manifest` `{"name", "entries"}`. `kept_apart`, `tree_recorded`,
  `config_files` and `config_sources` are not in the token. Pure.
- `from_token` (1324-1385) with helpers `_text` to `_manifest_from`
  (1388-1451): refuses (None) anything not a mapping or whose `v` is not
  the version; a missing `cwd` or `state` is a refusal, every other key
  defaults. Counts are bounded (`ref_tips` 64, `remotes`/`aliases` 256,
  `stamps` 8, `files` 64, `file_errors` 64, manifest entries 4,096).
  Python's rules leak in and must be ported as such: `shallow`,
  `evicted`, `boundary`, `file_tracked` take any value's truth; stamp
  numbers go through `int()` (`True`, `1.9`, `"7"` are accepted);
  `_key` takes `str()` of any value, so `[[[]], 1, 1]` is the key
  `("[[]]", "1", "1")`; hashes are lowercased before matching. Pure,
  and the same under Python 3.11 to 3.14 except how deep `str()` may
  nest (below).
- `location.remote_key` (378-405) with `_SCHEME_URL`/`_SCP_URL`/`_DRIVE`
  (366-370): the hosted branch (`host/rest`, lowercased, `/` stripped,
  one `.git` dropped) is pure. The local branch is not: `_local`
  (408-411) calls `os.path.realpath`, which reads the file system, and
  `_file_url_path` (422-459) reads `os.path.sep` and Python's
  `url2pathname`, which changed in 3.14. No `insteadOf` is applied here
  (aliases arrive already keyed in the capture). Proposed: port the
  hosted branch and the classification (hosted or local, and the
  pre-realpath path for a local one); leave realpath to a reading unit.
- `membership_records.ObjectKey` (288-332): three text fields, `compare`
  and `on_any_device`; it has no text form or parse of its own (the
  token's three-item list is its only spelling). Pure.
- `location.to_location` (1355-1411): field-by-field copy into
  `membership_records.Location` (447-539) with `frozenset`s for remote
  and alias keys; `history` is an opaque reader, left out. Pure.
- `_paths.norm`, `inside`, `basename` (22-58): separators read off the
  spelling, never the host. Pure, no flavour needed.
- `membership_lines` (660 lines) and `_printable.printable`/`quoted`
  (19-130): every `line_*` is a function of its arguments. Pure, and on
  its own near the guide.

Proposed split: (a) capture types, token both ways, `ObjectKey`,
`to_location`, `_paths` (about 420 lines); (b) `remote_key`'s pure part
(about 50 lines, many fixture cases), may ride with (a); (c)
`_printable` and `membership_lines` (about 780 lines).

Findings (reproduced at 3.13.13): `Capture.from_token` raises
`OverflowError` for a stamp number that is a non-finite float (JSON
`Infinity` as `json.loads` reads by default), and `RecursionError` for a
key item nested about 100,000 deep (`str()` in `_key`, location_git.py
1430); neither is in its `except` (1384), so a hostile token raises
where a refusal is documented.

### Built: parts (a) and (b)

`capture` (`src/capture/mod.rs`): `Capture`, `FileSeen`, `Stamp`,
`Manifest`, `State`, `Kind`, `Key`; `Capture::to_token(&self) -> PyValue`
(the dict, keys in `TOKEN_KEYS` order) and `Capture::from_token(&PyValue)
-> Result<Option<Capture>, PyError>`: `Ok(None)` where the reference
returns None, `Err(OverflowError | RecursionError)` where it raises (the
findings above, pinned in the fixture, not smoothed over). Strings are
code points (`PyStr`, a lone surrogate kept), ints canonical decimal text.
Python's rules are ported where they show: `bool()` of any value for the
flags, `int()` (`pyvalue::py_int`, with its 4,300-digit limit) for stamp
and manifest numbers, indexing a str or a dict where a list was meant,
`1`, `True` and `1.0` all being the version, and `str()` of any key item
(`capture::str_of`). `str_of` raises ValueError (a refusal) for an int
past 4,300 digits, as `str()` does; `pyvalue::py_str` and `repr` apply
no such limit, and a general fix there would touch every caller that
spells a `PyValue::Int` (the JSON writer, `repr`, the log payload), so it
is left to its own change. It raises RecursionError past the port's own
depth limit, 9,999 levels at a top-level key and 9,997 inside ``files``
(`STR_DEPTH_TOP`, `STR_DEPTH_FILES`): what CPython 3.13 does on Linux and
macOS on a fresh thread, not a parity claim, since its C limit is 3,000
on Windows, less on ARM64 and debug builds, and a caller deeper in C has
less. The reference's RecursionError here is a property of the
interpreter build and its stack, not of the reference: it differs
between Python 3.13 and 3.14, and under 3.14 between Linux (where CI saw
`from_token` return None for a key item 100,000 deep) and macOS (where
it raises). It is pinned only in the gated file. Native answers
RecursionError at its own fixed depth on every platform; the boundary is
a native test. `config_files` (stamped files) is the file-reading unit's and is
not carried; `kept_apart`, `tree_recorded` and `config_sources` are
fields but not token keys, as in the reference.

`capture::remote::remote_key(Option<&[u32]>) -> Option<RemoteKey>`: the
hosted branch exactly (`_SCHEME_URL` and `_SCP_URL` as `re` matches them,
`[a-z]` under IGNORECASE taking U+0130, U+0131, U+017F and U+212A, `\d`
any Unicode digit, `str.strip`, `str.lower`), and the decision that a URL
is local: `RemoteKey::Local { text, file_url }` carries the stripped URL
unchanged, which the golden test compares with what the reference hands
`_local` and whether it called `_file_url_path`. The local key itself is the file-reading unit's: `_local`
joins with the host's `os.path` and calls `realpath`, and
`_file_url_path` reads the host's separator and
`urllib.request.url2pathname`, which changed in Python 3.14.

`capture::paths::{norm, inside, basename}`: `_paths`, separators read off
the spelling, so no flavour. `capture::location`: `ObjectKey` with
`compare` (`Sameness`) and `on_any_device`, `ProjectFileRef`,
`Location` (its `frozenset`s as `BTreeSet`s, `born`) and `to_location`;
the `history` reader and `Location`'s properties that read `_same_path`
are the resolving unit's.

Fixtures (`tests/contract/gen_capture_vocabulary.py`):
`capture_vocabulary.jsonl` (198,300 bytes, not gated; checked identical
under 3.11 and 3.13) holds 72 captures built through `Capture` and
read back, 749 hostile tokens (among them every refused field paired
with every field that raises OverflowError, which pins the order
`from_token` reads in, `int()` and `str()` of floats, texts and ints at
the digit limit, and nesting 50 to 400 deep), 8 `to_location` cases,
1,303 URLs, 25 paths (each against all 25 for `inside`) and 56 key
pairs. `capture_vocabulary_python.jsonl` (23,984 bytes, gated on the
Python release) holds the 173 tokens with a key item nested 100,000
deep: the 119 whose answer is RecursionError and the 54 where another
field is read first. A case goes there by its input, not its answer, so
the split is the same under every interpreter (sorting by answer moved
the cases back into the ungated file under Python 3.14 on Linux, which
does not raise).
Tests: `golden_capture_vocabulary` (class i and ii) and
`capture_vocabulary_robustness`
(5: every key with every wrong type, 100,000-deep nesting on a 512 KiB
thread, 10 MB texts and URLs, the native depth and digit limits at their
boundaries).

Left for later: part (c) is built in "Text made safe to show" below,
with `line_restated`; the local
branch of `remote_key`, `_file_url_path`, the capture's discovery, its
cache and `checkout_token`, which read files.

## A caller's resolution (location.py 1420-1997)

Read at e2837eff. The part of `location.py` that resolves a caller
(lines 1420-1997) is cut into units, leaves first; unit locstate is
built (`src/location_caller.rs`).

| Function | Lines | Needs from the machine | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_MACHINE_LOCK`, `_MACHINE`, `_RECORDED`, `_clear_machine` | 1439-1448 | nothing | built (locstate) |
| `process_machine` | 1451-1460 | `machine.open_machine` (a closure) | built (locstate) |
| `_recorded` | 1463-1478 | `Membership.record_machine` (a closure) | built (locstate) |
| `_Held`, `_LOCKS_GUARD`, `_LOCKS`, `_location_lock` | 1481-1519 | threads | built (locstate) |
| `_cwd_of` | 1522-1528 | `os.getcwd` (a closure) | built (locstate) |
| `_Stand`, `_STANDS`, `STANDS_CAP`, `_clear_stands`, `_keep_stand`, `_stand_of`, `forget_session` | 1598-1654 | nothing | built (locstate) |
| `_with_file_errors` | 1803-1815 | nothing (`printable`) | built (locstate) |
| `_same_namespace` | 1879-1890 | `object_key` and `_hostname` (closures) | built (locstate) |
| `capture_location`, `_model`, `Caller` (`home`, `add_head_witness`), `resolve_caller`, `_caller`, `_resolved`, `resolve_here`, `_hooked` | 1420-1431, 1531-1595, 1657-1767, 1818-1828, 1862-1876, 1982-1997 | the model, the capture cache, `checkout_token.remint` (all arguments) | built (loccaller) |
| `resolve_hook` | 1893-1979 | the store, the client's answers, the kept exchanges, a clock and sixteen random bytes (all arguments) | built (lochook) |
| `_earlier_tree`, `_machineless` | 1770-1800, 1831-1859 | the store, the file system | unit locearly |

What locstate reproduces:

- Each module global and its `threading.Lock` is a value the caller
  owns behind a `Mutex`: `ProcessMachine` (`_MACHINE`, `_RECORDED`),
  `Locks` (`_LOCKS`) and `Stands` (`_STANDS`). A table is a `Vec` in
  insertion order, as a `dict` keeps it: a key dropped and kept again
  goes to the end. A poisoned mutex is read through, as a Python lock
  has no poisoning.
- `process_machine` opens once; an `open` that fails keeps nothing, so
  the next call opens again. `_recorded` checks and keeps the (store
  path, machine id) pair in two holds of the lock with the record
  between them, as the reference does: two threads may both record,
  and a record that raises is asked again next time.
- `_location_lock`: `lock_name` is `machine:device:inode` where the
  location has an object key (the birth is not in it), else `machine:`
  and `loc.root or loc.cwd` (an empty root names the cwd). `Locks::take`
  is the part under the guard: where the name is new and the table holds
  `CACHE_CAP * 4` (1,024) or more, every lock whose users are zero is
  dropped, in insertion order, then the new one is kept; a lock taken
  but not yet acquired has users and stays (ENG-160). Where every lock
  is in use the table grows past the cap, as the reference's does.
  `give_back` is the `finally`; `with_location_lock` runs a closure
  holding the lock and gives it back however the closure ends.
- `_keep_stand` drops the session's stand in the store and keeps the new
  one at the end only where the resolution has a checkout (an empty
  checkout is one); the oldest stand goes first at `STANDS_CAP`.
  `forget_session` drops the session in every store.
- `_with_file_errors` writes each error through `printable` and keeps it
  unless the resolution's own lines hold it: errors are not compared with
  each other, so an error given twice is shown twice, and the
  resolution's lines are not written through `printable`.
- `_same_namespace` asks `object_key(cap_cwd)` only where the client gave
  a key and `_hostname()` only where it named a host. A host name is
  bytes, as `location_probe` spells one; a client that names the empty
  host never matches, since `_hostname` answers None for an empty name.

`CACHE_CAP` is a private constant here (256, `location_git.py` 148); the
fold of the lane that builds `location_cache` replaces it with
`location_cache::CACHE_CAP`. `NO_CWD` (186) and `NO_MACHINE` (192) belong
to `_machineless` and are left for unit locearly. No pattern of `re` is
read here.

The fixtures (`gen_location_caller_state.py`, `location_caller_state.jsonl`,
ungated) drive the reference's functions directly: `open_machine`,
`record_machine`, `os.getcwd`, `object_key` and `_hostname` are the
case's, and each `_Held`'s lock is one that never blocks, so one thread
can take a location twice as two threads would. A table near its cap is
pinned as its length, first and last three entries and the SHA-256 of
its entries in order.

`Stands` holds a hash map from (store path, session) to a sequence
number and stand, beside the keys by sequence number, so `_stand_of` and
`_keep_stand` take constant time near the cap as the reference's dict
does. A stands row keeps one session's stand in two stores, and an errs_cp
row holds lone surrogates as code points, which `printable` writes as
`\ud800`.

What loccaller reproduces (`src/location_resolve.rs`, read at the
lines in the table above, which match `location.py` as it is now):

- `_caller` keeps the reference's order of effects: the machine (the
  given identity, else `process_machine`, whose failure goes to
  `_machineless` before any capture), the capture (cached), the model
  made and its machine recorded once per store, `_earlier_tree`, and
  where it answers True `forget` and a second capture that skips the
  cache; then the ladder (`_resolved`) under the location's lock, and
  `forget` once more where the token writer was called with a git
  directory, whatever the re-mint answered (a token of None still
  counts, as `wrote` is a non-empty list). The token writer sees the
  git directory and bareness of the capture resolved: after a second
  capture it re-mints the new git directory, as the reference's
  closure reads its rebound locals. An empty git directory writes
  nothing. The file errors' lines are the capture resolved's.
- A caller with no cwd is the indeterminate location at `NO_CWD` with
  the detail "the caller has no working directory" and every other
  field its default; it is never captured, and a hook of such a caller
  with a session and a checkout keeps a stand at `NO_CWD`.
- `Caller.home` asks the model's `unresolved_home` where the outcome is
  indeterminate or deferred, even with a project, or where the
  resolution names no project; else it is the resolution's project,
  checkout and rule. `add_head_witness` adds nothing without a project,
  in `global` or without a head (an empty head is none), and names the
  source `source@checkout` only where the checkout is not empty.
- `resolve_caller` reads the session's stand in the store; `_hooked`
  passes none, the process's machine and `FETCH_BUDGET`, and keeps its
  resolution as the session's stand. `resolve_here` asks `getcwd` only
  where the cwd is None, and a cwd that cannot be read is a caller with
  no cwd.

Decisions. The model is a `CallerModel` made by a closure, `_model`'s
`Membership(...)` (the liveness argument is the model's own); its
errors are the trait's `Error` and propagate as the reference's
exceptions do. The token writer takes the lineage (`k.lineage`) of the
checkout the model re-mints, not the checkout, and answers the token
and status. `checkout_token.remint` is a closure of (git directory,
policy, bare, lineage). The location carries no history reader here
(`capture::location::Location`), so `Caller.history` holds the common
directory `_history_of` answers, which `add_witness` receives.
`_earlier_tree` and `_machineless` (unit locearly) are closures;
`_machineless` answers the whole `Caller`, as the reference's does, and
is given a `Machineless`: the cwd `_caller` was given (under
`resolve_here`, the `getcwd` answer where its caller gave None), the
session, the error and the stand, as the reference's
`_machineless(store, config, cwd, session, exc, stand)` is. The model's
constructor and `_earlier_tree` answer a `Result` with the model's
`Error`, as `Membership(...)`, `model.checkouts()` and `gitdir_pin.put`
may raise; such an error leaves `_caller` before the lock is taken.
`config.membership` is the two values `Policy` holds. `FETCH_BUDGET`
(0.3) and `NO_CWD` are constants here until the lanes that build
`location_git`'s constants fold. No pattern of `re` is read.

The fixtures (`gen_location_resolve.py`, `location_resolve.jsonl`,
ungated, 21 KB) drive the reference's `_caller`, `_hooked`,
`resolve_caller`, `resolve_here`, `capture_location` and `Caller` with
recording doubles for `Membership`, `capture`, `forget`, `remint`,
`_earlier_tree`, `_machineless`, `open_machine` and `os.getcwd`, and
pin the calls in order with the location and resolution. Left for unit
lochook: `resolve_hook`.

Hostile input, timed once against the reference on the robustness
tests' inputs with the generator's doubles (release build, macOS
arm64): 5,000 file errors 1.6 ms against 3.9 ms, 5,000 re-mints 3.9 ms
against 3.7 ms, a 100,000-code-point cwd 0.7 ms against 0.1 ms (the
port's share is turning the JSON into code points). No ratio reaches
10; the tests themselves check only that the port grows linearly.

What lochook reproduces (`src/location_hook.rs`, `resolve_hook`, read
at 1893-1979 as `location.py` is now):

- No location mapping in what was posted (an rc3 client, or a
  `location` that is no dict) is `_hooked` at the cwd, the process's
  cwd (`_cwd_of`) where none was given.
- An indeterminate probe (`state` exactly `indeterminate`, `probe` true
  by Python's truth: the string `"0"` is true, `0` and `[]` are not) is
  the unreadable location resolved by `_model` of the process's machine.
  An `OSError` from `open_machine`, from the model's constructor or from
  `record_machine` makes the model at `NO_MACHINE` instead, with no
  record; any other error leaves. The location's cwd is `str()` of the
  posted cwd where it is true, else the cwd given, else empty, written
  after the model is made, so an int past `str()`'s 4,300 digits raises
  ValueError after the record. A detail that is no `str` is
  `cwd unreadable`. The resolution is kept as the session's stand.
- Else `_key(cwd_object)` is read; a ValueError (a wrong shape, or an int
  past the digit limit) is no key, and RecursionError from `str()` of a
  deeply nested item leaves. Where the posted cwd is a non-empty `str`
  and `_same_namespace` holds, it is `_hooked` at the posted cwd. A
  `hostname` that is no `str` is no host; host names are compared code
  point by code point.
- Else `Capture.from_token` (skipped for a probe) and `_identity_from`
  of `machine` are read, in that order, each raise leaving; where either
  is None the exchange asks `location`, `machine` and `write_token`. With
  both, the answers (a dict, else `{}` and not posted) give
  `AnsweredToken` and `AnsweredLiveness`, `_model` is made with them,
  `ExchangeReads` is built, the location is `AnsweredToken.located`
  (the model's `checkouts` asked only past its early returns), and the
  model resolves it under the location's lock with the reads declared.
  `NeedWitnesses` is the exchange `{**question, **carried,
  "write_token": policy}`: a key already in the question keeps its
  place and takes the new value. A resolution takes the token's file
  errors (`_with_file_errors`) and is kept as the session's stand.

Decisions. `_hooked` is a closure the caller fills with
`location_resolve::hooked` and its hands, so this unit's fixtures pin
`resolve_hook`'s own choices, and loccaller's fixtures pin `_hooked`.
The model is a `HookModel`: loccaller's `CallerModel` with `machine`,
`checkouts_of`, `resolve_declared` (`resolve(loc, strict=...,
declared=reads)`, its inner `Err` the `NeedWitnesses` it raises) and
`is_os_error`, which stands for the reference's `except OSError`. The
model's constructor is given the `Answered` readers (liveness and token
writer) on the token path and none on the probe path; `Membership(store,
NO_MACHINE, session=...)` is a second closure. `ExchangeReads` and
`carried` read the monotonic clock and `secrets.token_hex(16)` in the
reference; here the kept exchanges, `now` and the sixteen bytes are
arguments, and `INDEPENDENT_MAX` is the history bound. A raise is
`HookError::Model` (the model's or a closure's) or `HookError::Raised`
(Python's own: `str()`, `int()`, a question that is no dict).
`location_git._key` is `capture::object_key_of`, the token reader's own
`key` with a refusal read as ValueError. `NO_MACHINE` is a constant here
until the lane that builds `location_git`'s constants folds. No pattern
of `re` is read.

The fixtures (`gen_location_hook.py`, `location_hook.jsonl`, ungated,
71 KB) post mappings to the reference's `resolve_hook` with recording
doubles for `_hooked`, `os.getcwd`, `object_key`, `_hostname`,
`open_machine` and `Membership`, the nonce fixed and the kept exchanges
cleared per case: no location, every branch of the probe, the namespace
test by key, birth and host, the token asked for, the token resolved
with file errors, a re-mint located, `NeedWitnesses` with and without
reads, and two rounds where the second takes up the first's reads (or,
in another session, does not). A posted value is written in `neutral`
form, so the code points of a host name with a lone surrogate are read
whole. Inputs whose `neutral` form `str()` cannot write (an int past
4,300 digits) and nesting 12,000 deep are in the kills tests, each
answer read from the reference by hand and checked once against it.

## The checkout token (`checkout_token.py`)

Read at 465bc600. The module is 1,015 lines; its write protocol stands on
the file system, so it is cut into units, leaves first.

### Map, by function

| function | reference lines | needs from the machine | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `random_crockford`, `mint` | 234-243 | randomness (`secrets.randbits`) | built: the bytes are an argument |
| `valid`, `Lineage`, `Lineage.read`, `lineage` | 246-284 | nothing | built |
| `successor`, `succeeds`, `_link` | 287-325 | randomness (`successor`) | built |
| `token_path`, `render`, `parse` | 328-350 | nothing (the path flavour is data) | built |
| `_cut_short`, `_malformed_detail` | 851-871 | nothing | built |
| `read`, `_read_at`, `_read_text`, `_open_plain`, `_read_all`, `_clear_nonblock` | 353-363, 753-848 | open, stat, fstat, read, close, fcntl and a pause | built (unit 2) |
| `write`, `_guard`, `_existing`, `_info_dir`, `_create`, `_write_temp`, `_fs_now`, `_sweep`, `_place`, `_after_race`, `_failed`, `_unlink_quietly` | 366-398, 466-484, 690-701, 874-1015 | mkdir, exclusive create, fsync, hard link, unlink, owner, the file system's clock, a monotonic clock and a pause | built (unit 3) |
| `remint`, `_replace_named`, `_claim`, `_wait_for`, `_take`, `_blocked`, `_holder`, `_claim_read`, `_break`, `_break_marks`, `_release`, `_remove_holding` | 401-465, 487-750 | rename, exclusive create, unlink, a clock and a pause | built (unit 4) |

### Unit 1, built (`checkout_token`)

- `random_crockford(length, urandom)`: `secrets.randbits(5 * length)`
  reads `(5 * length + 7) // 8` bytes from `os.urandom` and drops the low
  surplus bits; the port takes those bytes and writes the top
  `5 * length` bits, five at a time, most significant first. A negative
  length is ValueError (`Raised::NegativeBits`); a byte count other than
  the one asked for is the caller's error (`Raised::RandomBytes`).
  `random_bytes_needed` gives the count. `mint` is 26 characters from 17
  bytes.
- `valid`: a `str` of exactly 26 Crockford characters.
  `_TOKEN_RE.fullmatch` is written by hand: an exact count of members of
  an ASCII set, which `re` reads the same way for every input (no flag,
  no anchor, no class shorthand).
- `lineage`, `Lineage::read`: a valid token and a list or tuple whose
  first two items are `str` matching `-?[0-9]+` under `fullmatch`,
  written by hand: an optional minus then one or more ASCII digits (an
  explicit range, so `re` reads no Unicode digit). `Lineage::read` takes a
  list or tuple of exactly three.
- `link` (`_link`): BLAKE2b with a 16-byte digest and the personalization
  `bm-token-remint` over the four fields, each its UTF-8 length, `:`, its
  bytes and `,`; the digest's low 65 bits as 13 characters. BLAKE2b is
  written out (`checkout_token::blake2b`, RFC 7693, unkeyed, with a digest
  length and a personalization): no crate for it is in the local cache.
  A field with a lone surrogate raises UnicodeEncodeError
  (`Raised::Encode`), as `str.encode` does.
- `successor(replaced, urandom)`: 13 characters from nine bytes, then the
  link. `succeeds`: false for no lineage, a value that is not a valid
  token, or the token replaced; else whether the last 13 characters are
  the link of the first 13. The link is computed only past those checks,
  so a surrogate in the lineage raises only there, as in the reference.
- `token_path(git_dir, flavour)`: the text of
  `Path(git_dir) / "info" / "bettermemory"`, as `os.path.join` of the
  three (`gitfile_rule::hostpath::join`) spelled by `config::pure_path`.
  The flavour is an argument, so a POSIX world reads the same on every
  runner.
- `render`: the two lines, ASCII encoded; a character past ASCII raises
  UnicodeEncodeError. `parse`: split at `\n`, one empty last piece
  dropped, exactly two pieces, one trailing `\r` removed from each, the
  header and a valid token. `cut_short` and `malformed_detail` as the
  reference writes them.

Decisions. `Lineage` holds three texts: the reference's `NamedTuple`
takes any object, and a field that is not a `str` would raise
AttributeError in `_link`; the port admits text only, since every caller
builds one through `lineage` or `Lineage.read`. `token_path` takes Rust
text: a path with a lone surrogate is not expressible there.

Findings about the reference (reproduced, pinned):

- `parse` accepts a token line ending in `\r` with no line end after it
  (`"<header>\n<token>\r"`), where its documentation says a CR is accepted
  before each line end. Repro: `parse(TOKEN_HEADER + "\n" + "0"*26 + "\r")`
  is the token.
- `_cut_short` reads only `\n` line ends, so a writer's partial file
  written with CRLF (`"<header>\r\n"`) is "not a ... file", not "cut
  short", although `parse` accepts the CRLF form when whole. Repro:
  `_malformed_detail(TOKEN_HEADER + "\r\n")`.
- `lineage` accepts a device or inode that is not canonical decimal
  (`"-0"`, `"007"`), so two spellings of one key name two lineages with
  different links. Repro: `lineage("0"*26, ("007", "1"))` is not None.
- `random_crockford` costs time quadratic in its length (a shift of a
  big integer per character): 0.02 s for 20,000 characters, 0.36 s for
  40,000. Every caller asks for 13 or 26. The port is linear.

Fixtures (`tests/contract/gen_checkout_token.py`): `checkout_token.jsonl`
(909 rows, not gated) pins every function above over random bytes from a
seeded generator, values of every type, keys at every bound, lineages
with long and non-ASCII fields (BLAKE2b over more than one block),
successors and near misses, file texts around each branch of `parse` and
`_cut_short`, tokens of code points whose low byte is a Crockford
character, and POSIX and Windows paths. The Windows paths are drives,
roots and relative forms, which come out the same under CPython 3.9, 3.13
and 3.15, so the file is not gated. UNC shares and device paths are left
out, since the golden guard
(`gen_store_files.host_fact`) reads a doubled backslash as a host path;
`hostpath::join` and `pure_path` are pinned over them by their own
fixtures.

Tests: `golden_checkout_token` (`checkout_token.jsonl`, every row);
`checkout_token_kills` (mutants: bits read least significant first or
from the low end, no length prefixes, no personalization, the digest's
high bits, case-folded or loose token checks, a trimmed integer parse,
CR handling of `parse`, the final empty line kept, `<= 26` in
`_cut_short`, naive path concatenation, UTF-8 for ASCII, a code point
read by its low byte; each answers differently on some row; and BLAKE2b
with a 16-byte person against two hashlib digests); `checkout_token_robustness` (integer bounds,
byte counts, nesting 100,000 deep, inputs to 1.6 million characters
linear in time, surrogates and code points past Unicode).

Left for later units: `write` (unit 3), `remint` and
the claim (unit 4), each over the `fsdata` file-system trait with the

### Unit 2, built (`checkout_token::read`)

Line ranges confirmed against the source as it is now: `read` 353-363,
`_read_at` 753-763, `_read_text` 766-801, `_open_plain` 804-815,
`_read_all` 818-833, `_clear_nonblock` 836-848, and `_os_text` 1002-1006
(listed with unit 3; the reads word their details with it, so it is
built here).

Every OS call goes through the `fsdata` file-system trait, extended at
its end with methods whose default declines, so existing implementations
need no change: `open_blocking` (the plain open of `_open_plain`),
`fstat_result` and `read_once` (one `os.read`, with the errno),
`close` (which can fail), `nonblock_flag`, `status_flags` and
`set_status_flags` (`fcntl`'s `F_GETFL` and `F_SETFL`, None or declined
where the platform has no `fcntl`), and `strerror`. `StdFs` implements
them: the non-blocking open is the existing `open_result` (`O_RDONLY |
O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC`), the plain open the standard library's read-only
open, `fcntl` and `close` are `bettermemory_sys` calls (the core crate
forbids unsafe), and `strerror` is the C library's text for the errno's
number on POSIX. `MemFs` gives `strerror` for the texts macOS and glibc
share. The pause before the reread is an argument (`pause(0.01)`); a
relative path is joined to the working directory of the `Ctx`.

- `read(ctx, git_dir, pause)`: `_read_at` of `token_path(git_dir)`.
- `read_at`: `_read_text`; a text that is no token and is cut short
  (`_cut_short`) is read once more after the pause; the second read's
  answer stands, whatever it is (absent, unreadable, or another text).
- `read_text`: the non-blocking open. A path the OS says is not there
  (`path_missing`: ENOENT or ENOTDIR) is absent; an errno other than
  EINVAL or EIO is unreadable, `open: <strerror> (<NAME>)`; EINVAL or EIO
  goes to `_open_plain`. Then `os.fstat`: not a regular file is
  malformed; else `_read_all`. An OSError of the fstat or of a read is
  unreadable, worded `read:`. The close runs in `finally`: its failure
  raises out of the read, replacing whatever the body answered
  (`Fault::Raised`). Then more than 4,096 bytes is "larger than a token
  file" (checked before the text), bytes past ASCII "not ASCII text".
- `open_plain`: `os.stat` (links followed); not a regular file is
  malformed; else the blocking open. An error of either is absent or
  unreadable, worded `open:`.
- `read_all`: `os.read` of `4097 - len(data)` until an empty answer or
  more than 4,096 bytes. A read refused with EINVAL or EIO is made once
  more after `_clear_nonblock` succeeds; else, or if that read fails,
  the error is raised to `_read_text`. The clearing is tried at every
  refused read, not once.
- `clear_nonblock`: False where there is no `fcntl` (`sys.platform ==
  "win32"`) or either call fails; else `F_SETFL` with the flags
  `F_GETFL` gave less `O_NONBLOCK`.
- `os_text`: `strerror` and the errno's name in brackets.

Decisions. An error with no errno name, or whose text the file system
does not give, makes the read decline (`Fault::NotPorted`) rather than
guess the reference's `str(exc)` or a C library's wording: Windows'
C runtime texts are not ported, and `MemFs` leaves out the names macOS
and glibc word apart. `bettermemory_sys::errno_name` names, on macOS and
Linux, every errno CPython raises as plain `OSError` that both share
with one name each (EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOMEM, EBUSY, EOVERFLOW, EHOSTDOWN
among them), so descriptor exhaustion and the like read as unreadable,
worded as the reference words them. Still declined: a number two names
share (EAGAIN and EWOULDBLOCK; EDEADLK, and on Linux EOPNOTSUPP and
ENOTSUP), an errno CPython raises as a subclass the port has no class
for (ESRCH, ECHILD, EPIPE, the connection errors), and an empty text.
A NUL in the path is ValueError, which no `except OSError` catches: it
raises (`Fault::Raised`), as in the reference. A relative path under
the Windows flavour declines, as `Ctx::at` does.
`StdFs::read_once` allocates at most 1 MiB per call whatever the count.
No regular expression is involved.

Findings about the reference (reproduced, pinned):

- `read` says nothing in it raises for an OS error, but a failing
  `os.close` in `_read_text`'s `finally` raises out of it (OSError,
  InterruptedError for EINTR), replacing even a token already read.
  Repro: rows `close fails`, `close interrupted` and `close fails on the
  reread` of `checkout_token_read.jsonl` (`os.close` raising EIO).
- A git directory holding a NUL makes `read` raise ValueError, against
  the same sentence. Repro: `checkout_token.read("/r/\0")`.
- `_open_plain` stats and then opens: a regular file replaced by a FIFO
  between the two makes the blocking open wait for a writer. Not pinned
  (a race); the port makes the same two calls in the same order.

Fixtures (`tests/contract/gen_checkout_token_read.py`):
`checkout_token_read.jsonl` (77 rows, POSIX only) runs the reference over
a scripted OS (`os.open`, `os.stat`, `os.fstat`, `os.read`, `os.close`,
`fcntl.fcntl`, `sys.platform`, `time.sleep` replaced), errors raised as
`OSError(errno.<NAME>, "text of <NAME>")`, and pins each answer with
every call made, in order: each open, stat, fstat, read and close
error, both retry errnos, the plain open's every branch, the read
retry's `fcntl` failures and the `win32` platform, sizes 4,095 to
5,000, chunked and byte-at-a-time reads, the reread's every outcome,
close failures, NULs and a relative path. Its bytes follow the OS family:
on Windows the logged open spells the path as `WindowsPath` does
(`open \r\.git\info\bettermemory`) and a detail names the errno as
that host's `errno.errorcode` does (`WSAELOOP` for ELOOP), so Windows
makes no such file and runs no test that reads it, in the parity job's
step 1 either. The scripted reads, the `win32` rows among them, are
compared on macOS and Linux only. `checkout_token_read_posix.jsonl`
(17 rows, POSIX only) reads a real scratch tree: a token, an empty
file, files of 5,000 and 4,096 bytes, a file holding the single byte
0xFF and one holding 0x80, a FIFO, a folder, a link to the token, a
dangling link, a loop, a link to the FIFO, a missing name, a path
through a file, a name of 300 bytes, `/dev/null`, and `read` of a git
directory; its texts (ELOOP, ENAMETOOLONG) are those macOS and glibc
share.

Tests: `golden_checkout_token_read` (unix; every row, with the call log,
over the scripted file system in `tests/ct_read_script`; recorded as
having no case on Windows by `checkout_token_read_not_posix`),
`golden_checkout_token_read_posix` (every row through `StdFs`; recorded
as having no case on Windows by `checkout_token_read_not_posix`),
`checkout_token_read_kills` (unix, as it reads the same file: a single read, no `fcntl` retry, a close
that never fails, no stat before the plain open, every errno retried,
no plain open, `>=` for the size bound, text judged before size), and
`checkout_token_read_robustness` (a 64 MiB chunk, a byte at a time, a
refusal every time, chunk sizes at the bound, paths of a million bytes
linear in time, NULs, a FIFO with no writer that never waits, an empty
error text, `MemFs`'s texts against the C library's, one `read_once`
answering its whole count up to the 1 MiB cap, and an open with every
descriptor taken, read in a child capped at 64).

### Unit 3, built (`checkout_token::write`)

Line ranges confirmed against the source as it is now: the constants
76-159 (`_RACE_READ_SECONDS` 111, `_RACE_PAUSE_MAX_SECONDS` 112,
`_TEMP_SUFFIX_LENGTH` 117, `_TEMP_PREFIX` 119, `_STALE_TEMP_SECONDS` 148,
`_FILE_MODE` 149, `_READONLY_ERRNOS` 150, `_OPEN_CREATE` 159),
`WriteStatus` 161-171, `TokenWrite` 200-231, `write` 366-398, `_guard`
466-484, `_fs_now` 690-701 (mapped under unit 4; built here, unit 4
reuses it), `_existing` 874-886, `_info_dir` 889-896, `_create` 899-913,
`_write_temp` 916-920, `_sweep` 923-940, `_place` 943-961, `_after_race`
964-992, `_failed` 995-999 and `_unlink_quietly` 1009-1015 (`still`
None; unit 4 passes one).

Effects are arguments. `TokenFs` (in `write.rs`, over `fsdata::Fs`, so
`fsdata.rs` is not touched) carries the write-side calls: `mkdir`,
`create_excl` (the exclusive open, mode 0o644), `write_once`,
`fsync_file`, `close_created`, `link`, `fsync_dir`, `scandir_names`,
`lstat_mtime`, `unlink`, `utime_now`, `stat_mtime` and `owner_uid`;
`StdFs` implements it. `Machine` carries `os.geteuid`, `sys.platform ==
"win32"`, the random bytes (17 for `mint`, then 8 for the 12-character
temporary suffix, in that order), `time.monotonic` and `time.sleep`.
The reads are unit 2's `read_at`, its pause the machine's sleep.

What each function reproduces:

- `_guard`: policy off, then bare, then (off Windows) `os.stat(git_dir)`
  and `os.geteuid()`, in that order; a failing stat is `_failed`.
- `_existing`: absent is None, present is `exists`, malformed keeps its
  detail, unreadable is `failed:io` with `the existing token cannot be
  read: ` and the read's detail.
- `_info_dir`: `<git_dir>/info` spelled as `Path` spells it; only a
  FileExistsError of `os.mkdir` is suppressed.
- `_create`: the exclusive open; then writes until the body is out (a
  count past the rest ends the loop, as slicing a `memoryview` does);
  `fsync_file` swallows its error; the `finally` close, whose error
  replaces the write's. The path is unlinked only after this call's own
  open succeeded and a write or the close failed: an open that fails
  (EEXIST above all, where the path is the token name in the fallback)
  unlinks nothing.
- `_write_temp`, `_fs_now`, `_sweep`: the name is drawn after the
  `mkdir`; the clock is `os.utime` then `os.stat(...).st_mtime` (any
  OSError is None, which sweeps nothing); `st_mtime` is CPython's
  `fill_time` (seconds plus `nsec * 1e-9` in doubles). Only names starting
  `bettermemory.tmp-` whose `lstat` time is strictly below `now - 3600`
  are unlinked, by a plain `os.unlink` (no Windows retry); every error is
  ignored, and an error of the listing's iteration ends it there.
- `_place`: the link; EEXIST reads the winner's token; any other link
  error falls to the exclusive create of the token name, whose EEXIST
  also reads the winner's token and whose other errors are `_failed`;
  `fsync_dir` of `info` (skipped on Windows) only after success.
- `_after_race`: deadline `monotonic() + 1.5`; a found file is
  unfinished when absent, `failed:io`, or malformed with detail exactly
  `empty` or `cut short`; `left <= 0` or a finished file ends the loop;
  the pause is `min(pause, left)` as Python's `min` picks, starting at
  0.01 and doubling to at most 0.2. Absent at the end is `failed:io`
  `the token another writer placed was removed`.
- `_failed`: EACCES, EPERM and EROFS are `failed:readonly`, any other
  errno `failed:io`, the detail `_os_text`; an error whose errno has no
  name or no text is declined (`Fault::NotPorted`), never guessed.
- `write`: the guard, the existing file, the token, the info folder, the
  temporary file, the placing; the `finally` unlinks the temporary path
  alone (through `fsutil::unlink_retrying_by`, retried on Windows),
  whatever `_place` answered, and never the token name.
- A ValueError (a NUL in the git directory) raises out of `write`
  (`Fault::Raised`), as the reference's does: no `except OSError` there
  catches it.

Decisions:

- `StdFs::fsync_dir` has no `O_DIRECTORY` (the crate has no libc and
  forbids `unsafe`): it stats the path and opens and fsyncs it only where
  the stat says a directory, so a FIFO put at `info` is not opened;
  every error is swallowed, as the reference's is. A directory replaced
  between the stat and the open is the race this leaves.
- `StdFs::utime_now` on POSIX is `bettermemory_sys::utime_now`,
  `utimensat(AT_FDCWD, path, NULL, 0)`, the call `os.utime(path)` makes:
  the file system's own clock (the server's on NFS, so every age is read
  in one clock) and no open, so no read access is needed. An explicit
  time from this machine's clock would let a client running ahead of an
  NFS server sweep another writer's young temporary file. On Windows
  `os.utime` reads this machine's clock and calls `SetFileTime` on a
  handle opened with FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, and so does the port
  (`File::set_times`). Links are followed in both.
  `checkout_token_write_robustness` pins a temporary file of mode 0o200.
- `StdFs::link` is `std::fs::hard_link`; the source is always the
  regular temporary file, so whether a link is followed at the source
  does not arise.
- `StdFs::scandir_names` on Windows spells a name as WTF-8: a lone
  surrogate becomes its own three-byte form, as `os.scandir` gives it as a
  `str` holding the surrogate, so `bettermemory.tmp-` followed by one
  still matches the prefix and is swept when stale. `host` turns those
  bytes back into the same UTF-16 (a lib test in `write.rs` pins both).
- `StdFs::owner_uid` declines off POSIX (`None`, then `Fault::NotPorted`);
  the reference asks it only off Windows.
- No regular expression is involved.

Findings about the reference (reproduced):

- `_create`'s loop never ends where `os.write` returns 0 for a non-empty
  buffer (`view = view[0:]`). Not pinned (a loop); the port's loop is the
  same.
- `write` says it never raises for an OS error, but a NUL in the git
  directory raises ValueError (from `os.stat` in `_guard`, or from the
  read on `win32`). Repro: rows `nul in the git dir` and `nul in the git
  dir, win32` of `checkout_token_write.jsonl`.
- A temporary name already taken (EEXIST of the exclusive create in
  `_write_temp`) fails the write as `failed:io` with no second draw.
  Repro: row `temp open exists`.
- Under a clock whose step is below the double's resolution at its
  value (a `monotonic` that a pause of 0.01 does not move), `_after_race`
  reads for ever while nothing is found. A real monotonic clock always
  moves; not pinned.

Fixtures (`tests/contract/gen_checkout_token_write.py`):
`checkout_token_write.jsonl` (72 rows, POSIX only, as the read file is
and for the same reasons: logged paths spelled by the host's `Path`,
errno names the host's) runs `write` over the read file's scripted OS,
extended with the write-side calls, the random bytes, the platform, the
monotonic clock (starting at 100.0, moved only by the pauses) and the
pause, over relative git directories (`r/.git`: no disk is touched, and
the test session's guard on `write` asks for a git directory under its
scratch working directory), and pins each answer with every call made, in order: policy off,
bare, a foreign owner, each stat error, an existing token, malformed,
empty, cut short and unreadable file, each `mkdir` error and EEXIST,
the temporary file's open, short and overlong writes, write, fsync and
close errors and both together, the unlink retried on `win32`, `utime`

`checkout_token_write_posix.jsonl` (8 rows, POSIX only) writes real git

Tests: `golden_checkout_token_write` (unix; every row with the call log,
